Title: Raktātisāra
Sanskrit: रक्तातिसार
INTRO: The patient of Paittika Atisāra (diarrhea) due to the further increase of Pitta if passes blood with faeces and develops the symptoms like fever, burning sensation, thirst, gripping pain and swelling of anus, then this condition is known as Raktātisāra.
TREATMENT: Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Take the equal parts of the leaves of Jambū (jamun), Āmalakī (embelic myrobalan) and Āmra (mango) and express its Svarasa (fresh juice). 28 ml. of the juice is to be taken three times a day after adding to it 14 g. honey and 100 ml. goat’s milk. 2. Rakta Candana (red sandal wood) powder – 2 to 6 g., to be taken with Śarkarā (raw sugar) – 6 g. and honey – 6 g. followed by a draught of Taṇḍulodaka (rice washing) – 100 to 250 ml. It is to be taken two times a day. 3. Mix Nāgakeśara (Indian iron – wood tree stamen) – powder, honey and Śarkarā (raw sugar) in equal parts and add to it 16 parts of butter. Its 15 to 25 g. is to be taken three times a day. 4. Prepare Kuṭaja (kurchi) – bark Siddha Kṣīra. Its 100 ml. is to be taken with honey, two times a day. 5. Take Kṛṣṇa Tila (black sesame seed) – 4 parts and Śarkarā (raw sugar) – 1 part. Its 3 to 6 g. is to be chewed slowly followed by a draught of 100 to 250 ml. of goat’s milk, three times a day. 6. Decoction prepared from equal parts of fruit bark of Dāḍima (pomegranate) and bark of Kuṭaja (kurchi) to be taken in 14 to 28 ml. dose with 6 g. honey, two times a day. 7. Decoction prepared from equal parts of powder of rhizome of Haridrā (turmeric), whole plant of Parpaṭa (five leaved fumitory), wood of Candana (white sandal), Śuṇṭhī (dried ginger), and roots of Balā (country mallow) and Sārivā; to be taken in 14 to 28 ml. dose two times a day. 8. Decoction prepared from equal parts of flowers of Nīlotpala (blue lotus) and Dhātakī (downy grislea), Śuṇṭhī (dried ginger), Mocarasa (silk cotton tree resin), roots of Mañjiṣṭhā (madder) and Mustaka (motha), whole plant of Kirātatikta (chirata), bark of Śāla and Rasāñjana (dry extract of berberis), to be taken in 14 to 28 ml. dose, two times a day. 9. Prepare decoction from the equal parts of Śuṇṭhī (dried ginger) and roots of Mustaka (motha) and Ativiṣā (Indian atees), and take its 14 to 28 ml. three times a day. 10. Make a paste from Candana (white sandal wood) – 2 to 6 g. in sufficient quantity of water, and take it with 4 to 6 g. honey and 5 to 10 g. Śarkarā (raw sugar), two times a day. 11. Take 1 to 3 g. of powder of Trikaṭu with 100 to 250 ml. of Takra (butter milk) or water once a day early in the morning. 12. 1 to 3 g. of powder of Pañca Lavaṇa (5 types of salt), to be taken with 100 to 250 ml. of Takra (butter milk) or water, once a day early in the morning.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: Kuṭajaghana Vaṭī: 1 to 2 Vaṭī to be taken 2 to 3 times a day with water.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Raktātisāra, Beng: Raktītisāra, Dogr: Kunnī Atisāra, Guj: Khūnī Ānva, Hind: Khunī Dasta, Kan: Raktabhedhī, Maly: Raktayuktātisāram, Mra: Raktātisāra, Raktī Ānva, Ori: Raktāṅaga, Panj: Lahu De Dasta, Tam: Rakihā Bedhi, Raktha Kajhichchal, Tel: Netturu Virechanamulu, Eng: (blood) dysentery

Title: Āntra Śothaja Atisāra
Sanskrit: आन्त्र शोथज अतिसार
TREATMENT: Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Take equal parts of powder of Jātiphala (mace nut), fruit of Jīraka (cumin) and fruit pulp of Bilva (bael). Its 3 to 6 g. is to be taken with Cūrṇodaka (limewater) – 14 to 28 ml. twice a day, morning and evening. 2. Prepare decoction from the fruit of Viḍaṅga, roots of Ativiṣā (Indian atees) and Mustaka (motha), wood of Devadāru (deodar), whole plant of Pāṭhā (false pareira) and Indrayava (kurchi seed). Its 14 to 28 ml is to be taken twice a day in the morning and evening. 3. Prepare decoction from equal parts of whole plant of Punarnavā (pigweed), Indrayava (kurchi seed), roots of Pāṭhā (false pareira), Ativiṣā (Indian atees) and Mustaka (motha), rhizome of Vacā (sweet flag) and fruit pulp of Bilva (bael). Its 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken with 1 g. powder of Marica (black pepper) once a day in the morning.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Nāri-Śothaja Atisāra, Beng: Āntra-Śothaja, Dogr: Āntrośotha Se Atisāra, Guj: Kaphaja Maraḍa, Hind: Āṁta Sūjana Janya Dasta, Maly: Kuṭalvīkkam Kondulla, Vayārilakkam, Mra: Āntraśothaja Atisāra, Tam: Kapa Perumkajhichal, Eng: Diarrhea due to colitis

Title: Jvarātisāra
Sanskrit: ज्वरातिसार
INTRO: In Jvarātisāra alongwith the signs and symptoms of Atisāra, fever of varying degree is also accompanied.
TREATMENT: Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Prepare decoction from the equal parts of fruit pulp of Bilva (bael), Śuṇṭhī (dried ginger), fruit of Dhānyaka (coriander), root of Mustaka (motha) and rhizome of Sugandha Bālā (valerian). Its 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken once a day early in the morning. 2. Prepare decoction from the equal parts of whole plants of Pāṭhā (false pareira), Kirātatikta (chirata) and Parpaṭa (five leaved fumitory), root of Mustaka (motha), Śuṇṭhī (dried ginger), Indrayava (kurchi seed) and stem of Guḍūcī. Its 14 to 28 ml., to be taken twice a day in the morning and evening. 3. Prepare decoction from the equal parts of Śuṇṭhī (dried ginger), root of Ativiṣā (Indian atees), stem of Guḍūcī, whole plant of Kirātatikta (chirata), and bark of Kuṭaja (kurchi). Its 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken twice a day. 4. Prepare decoction from the equal parts of roots of Uśīra (khas), Balā (country mallow) and Mustaka (motha), Śuṇṭhī (dried ginger), flower of Dhātakī (downy grislea), stem bark of Lodhra and fruit pulp of Bilva (bael). Its 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken twice in a day.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Caturbhadra Cūrṇa: 1 to 3 g., to be taken with honey twice a day. 2. Daśamūla Kvātha: 14 to 28 ml., to be taken with 1 g. powder of Śuṇṭhī (dried ginger) twice a day. 3. Siddha Prāṇeśvara Rasa: 1 to 2 pills, to be taken with honey – 4 to 6 g. thrice a day. 4. Ānanda Bhairava Rasa: 250 to 500 mg., to be taken with honey – 4 to 6 g. twice a day. 5. Rāmabāṇa Rasa: 250 to 500 mg., to be taken with honey 4 to 6 g. twice a day. 6. Sañjīvani Vaṭī: 1 to 2 Vaṭī, to be taken with Ārdraka Svarasa (ginger juice) – 5 to 10 ml. twice or thrice a day.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Jvarātisāra, Beng: Jvarātisāra, Dogr: Jvarātisāra, Kan: Jvara Bedhī, Maly: Paniyodūkudiya Vayārilkkam, Mra: Jvarātisāra, Ori: Jara-Jhāḍā, Tam: Jura Bedhī, Jura Perumkajichal, Eng: Diarrhea with fever

Title: Guda-Bhraṁśa
Sanskrit: गुदभ्रंश
INTRO: Due to the very frequent motions, a part of the rectum protrudes out of its normal position in weak, lean and thin patient, and this condition is known as Gudabhraṁśa.
TREATMENT: Following preparations are to be applied locally on the anus two times a day. 1. Apply Tila Taila (gingelly oil), give light fomentation, replace the anus with cotton to its normal position and give T bandage. 2. Apply Mūṣaka Taila, foment with cotton, press up prolapse to its position and give T bandage. 3. Apply fresh flesh of a rat and give T bandage.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Śūla Oloya, Beng: Gudabhraṁśa, Dogr: Tūniutharnā, Tuntāri, Guj: Māṇa Nikalvun, Hind: Kāṁca Niṣkāśana, Kan: Gudailitā, Maly: Guḍabhraṁśam, Mra: Guḍabhraṁśa, Ori: Maladvāra Banari Pāḍibā, Panj: Guda Utaranā, Tam: Asanovoy Velipaduthal, Tel: Pegu Jāruṭa, Eng: Prolapsus ani

Title: Pravāhikā
Sanskrit: प्रवाहिका
INTRO: Pravāhikā is a disease in which patient passes small quantity of mucoid or slimy or blood stained stool with considerable strain, gripping pain and burning sensation.
TREATMENT: Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Mocarasa (silk cotton tree resin) – 5 to 15 g., to be taken with 1 g. powder each of bark of Dāḍima (pomegranate) and fruit of Jīraka (cumin), twice or thrice a day before or after meal with water. 2. Fruit pulp of Bilva (bael) – 3 g. and seed of Kṛṣṇa Tila (black sesame) – 2 g., to be ground together with cream or curd and to be taken twice or thrice a day. 3. Take fruit pulp of Bilva (bael), 1 year old Guḍa (jaggery), Tila Taila (gingelly oil), Lodhra and fruit of Marica (black pepper) in equal parts, mix together and take it in the dose of 3 to 6 g. twice a day. 4. Powder of equal parts of Jātiphala (macenut), Lavaṅga (clove), fruit of Jīraka (cumin) and Śuddha Ṭaṅkaṇa (purified borax), to be taken in 1 g. dose with honey or Śarkarā (raw sugar) thrice a ay. 5. Seeds of Īṣadgola (plantago) – 3 to 6 g. is to be taken with half fried Śarkarā (raw sugar) twice in a day. The preparation is specially useful in Raktaja Pravāhikā. 6. Take powder Īṣadgola (plantago), fruit pulp of Bilva (bael), fruit of Miśreyā (fennel) and Śarkarā (raw sugar) in equal parts. Its 3 to 6 g. is to be taken with Takra (butter milk) twice or thrice a day. 7. Kṣīrapāka prepared from 4 g. root of Pippalī (long pepper) or Marica (black pepper), to be taken after adding 2 g. of Śarkarā (raw sugar) and 100 to 250 ml. of goat’s milk.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Bilvādi Cūrṇa: 2 to 6 g., to be taken with Takra (butter milk) – 50 to 100 ml. twice a day. 2. Śatapuṣpādi Cūrṇa: 2 to 6 g., to be taken with Takra (butter milk) twice a day. 3. Catuṣaṣṭiprahārī Pippalī: 120 to 250 mg., to be taken with honey – 4 to 6 g. twice or thrice a day. 4. Kuṭajāvaleha: 12 to 24 g., to be taken twice a day. 5. Kuṭajāriṣṭa: 14 to 28 ml., to be taken with equal quantity of water twice a day after meal. 6. Laghu Gaṅgādhara Cūrṇa: 1 to 3 g., to be taken three times a day with water. 7. Kuṭajaghana Vaṭī: 2 to 4 Vaṭī, to be taken with Takra or water 100 to 250 ml. twice or thrice a day before meal.
PATHYA: Purāṇa Śāli (old rice), Lājamaṇḍa (gruel prepared from pop of paddy), soup prepared from Mudga (phaseolus bean) or Masūra (lentil); milk, butter from goat’s or cow’s milk; Ārdraka (ginger), Śuṇṭhī (dried ginger), leaves of Cāṅgerī (wood sorrel), fruits of Jambū (jamun), Dāḍima (pomegranate) and Bilva (bael), flower and fruit of banana are useful for the patient of Atisāra.
APATHYA: The use of uncherished food (Asātmya Bhojana), spicy and acidic food, intake of incompatible articles of food (Viruddha Āhāra), Uṣṇa and Guru Dravya; products of sugarcane, Godhūma (wheat), Māṣa (black phaseolus bean), Yava (barley), Vāstuka Patra Śāka (leaf of a variety of chenopodium) should be avoided. Excessive water intake and bath, awaking late in the night, irregular hours of sleep may also be avoided.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Peṭkāmoraṇī, Beng: Prabāhikā, Dogr: Maroḍa, Guj: Maroḍa, Hind: Peciśa, Kan: Āmaśaṅke, Maly: Vayarukati, Mra: Āmāṁśa, Ori: Nalasutajnada, Nalaraktajnada, Tam: Śīta Bedhī, Tel: Banka Virechanamulu, Eng: Dysentery

Title: ĀNTARIKA VIDRADHI
Sanskrit: आन्तरिक विद्रधि
INTRO: Abscess of an internal organ is known as Āntarika Vidradhi. It may affect the anal region, urinary bladder, umbilical region, groin, kidney, spleen, liver etc.
SYMPTOMS: Acute pain, swelling, pus discharge through the external openings and dysfunctions of the affected organ are the common signs and symptoms of Āntarika Vidradhi. The specific signs and symptoms caused by the involvement of a particular organ are as follows: 1. Guda Vidradhi: Internal abscess in the anal region causes obstruction to flatus. 2. Basti Vidradhi (Abscess of Urinary Bladder and Prostate): In this condition patient passes less urine with difficulty. 3. Nābhi Vidradhi (Internal Abscess of Umbilical Region: It causes hiccough and bloting (Āṭopa). 4. Kukṣi Vidradhi (Internal Abscess of Flanks): It causes flatulence. 5. Vaṅkṣaṇa Vidradhi (Internal Abscess of Groin): It causes pain and immobilily of back and lumber region. 6. Vṛkka Vidradhi (Perinephric Abscess): It causes rigidity of the sides 7. Plīha Vidradhi (Splenic Abscess): It causes obstruction to breathing. 8. Yakṛt-Vidradhi (Liver Abscess): It causes difficulty in breathing.
TREATMENT: Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Decoction prepared from equal parts of root of Śveta Punarnavā (white pigweed) and bark of Varuṇa, to be taken in 14 to 28 ml. dose with 12 g. honey, twice a day. 2. Decoction of bark of Śigru (horse-radish), to be taken twice a day in 14 to 28 ml. dose after adding to it 0.25 g. Śuddha Hiṅgu (purified asafoetida) and 1 g. Saindhava (rock-salt).
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Jātyādi Ghṛta: 12 to 24 g., to be taken with 50 ml. warm water twice a day. 2. Varuṇādi Ghṛta: 12 to 24 g., to be taken with 50 ml. warm water twice a day. 3. Kāñcanāra Guggulu: 1 to 2 Vaṭī, to be taken with 50 ml. warm water twice a day. 4. Triphalādi Guggulu: 1 to 2 Vaṭī, to be taken with 50 ml. warm water twice a day. 5. Kajjalī: 125 to 250 mg., to be taken twice a day with 7 to 14 ml. Svarasa (fresh juice) of bark of Śigru (horse-radish).
PATHYA: Old Śāli variety of rice, soup of Mudga (phaseolus bean); bulb of Rasona (garlic), ghee, oil; seeds of Śyāmā (a variety of millet) and Kulattha (dolichos bean); fruit and leaf of Śigru (horse radish), fruits of Kāravellaka (bitter gourd) and Paṭola (a variety of small cucumber-snake gourd); and leaf of Punarnavā (pigweed) are useful for the patient of Āntarika Vidaradhi.
APATHYA: Lavaṇa, Kaṭu, Amla-Rasa Dravya, Piṣṭamaya Dravya (superfine powder of cereals and pulses), Navīna Dhānya (freshly harvested cereals), Māṣa (black phaseolus bean), Tila (sesame seed), Guḍa (jaggery) and curd should be avoided.
REGIONAL NAMES: Beng: Āntera Bidradhi, Dogr: Āntḍiya-Kā Phoḍā, Guj: Andarūnī Phoḍā, Hind: Andarūnī/Ābhyantara Phoḍā, Kan: Olaguru, Maly: Ābhyantaragalu, Antaragalu, Mra: Ānthara Vidhradhi, Panj: Andarūnī Phodā, Tam: Utpurakkaṭṭī, Tel: Kaḍupulo Puṇḍu, Eng: Internal abscess

Title: ĀNTRA-VṚDDHI
Sanskrit: आन्त्रवृद्धि
INTRO: The abnormal protrusion of small intestine is called Āntra Vṛddhi. Commonly in case of a male it protrudes through inguinal canal into the scrotum and in case of a female it forms a glandular mass beneath the inguinal ligament. The pecularity of the swelling is this that on applying pressure from below it disappears but reappears after removing the pressure.
TREATMENT: To cure the disease surgical intervention is necessary. In case of strangulated hernia immediate hospitalization is recommended.
PATHYA: Laghu Dravya like old rice of Śāli variety, soup of Mudga (phaseolus bean), bulb of Rasona (garlic), Nimbū Pānaka; fruits of Kāravellaka (bitter gourd) and Paṭola (variety of small cucumber); leaves of Śigru (horse-radish) and Vāstūka (a variety of chenopodium) are useful for this disease.
APATHYA: Dravya having Tikta, Kaṭu and Kaṣāya Rasa and Rūkṣa and Guru properties; Tila (sesame) and Śimbi Dhānya (legumes) are harmful for the patients of Āntra Vṛddhi.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Āntra Bṛddhi, Beng: Antra bṛddhi, Dogr: Anthimegada, Guj: Sarvagranthā, Hind: Ānta Utaranā, Kan: Karalu Beleyuvudu, Maly: Kutalirakkam, Mra: Āntra Vṛddhi, Panj: Dharana-painā, Tam: Iluyuvdu Kudalirakkam, Tel: Pegu Jāruṭa, Eng: Hernia

Title: ĀNTRA-PUCCHA PRADĀHA
Sanskrit: आन्त्रपुच्छ प्रदाह
INTRO: Inflammation of appendix vermiform is known as Āntra-Puccha Pradāha (appendicitis).
SYMPTOMS: Sudden onset of generalized abdominal pain followed by its localization in the right lower quadrant of abdomen, nausea, vomiting, constipation, fever, localized tenderness and rigidity of the right lower quadrant are the general signs and symptoms of Āntra-Puccha Pradāha.
TREATMENT: A case of appendicitis should be hospitalized immediately. For relief of pain, Śūlahāraṇa Yoga – 250 to 500 mg. be given with water two times a day.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Nāri Pucha Śotha, Hind: Āntra Pucha Śotha, Kan: Karulabalā Uriyuta, Maly: Unḍuka Vīkkam, Mra: Āntra Puccha Sūja, Eng: Appendicitis, Tam: Nangujhu Thapitham

Title: APASMĀRA
Sanskrit: अपस्मार
INTRO: Apasmāra is a disease which comes in paroxysms and due to the derangement of Buddhi (intellect) and the mind, the patient loses his memory or consciousness for a brief period.
SYMPTOMS: It comes in paroxysm; patient see imaginary things and falls down; eyes and eye brows become distorted; foaming from the mouth; tremors; hand and feet become convulsed; paroxysm lasts for a brief period and patient regains his consciousness as he is awaking from sleep.
TREATMENT: A. At the time of attack Sprinkle the cold water and remove the patient to an airy place. Any one of the following preparation may also be used locally. 1. 5 to 10 drops of juice of bulb of Palāṇḍu (onion), to be instilled in the nose as Nasya. 2. 5 to 10 drops of juice of root of Nirguṇḍī (five leaved chaste tree), to be instilled in the nose in the form of Nasya. 3. Give a Nasya (snuff) prepared from extra fine powder of seed of Marica (black pepper), Śigru (horse-radish) and Damanaka, twice a day. 4. Give Dhūmra (smoke) or root of Vacā (sweet-flag) and fruit of Marica (balck pepper) to nose. 5. Prepare an Añjana from the equal parts of the powder of roots of Madhuyaṣṭi (glycyrrhiza) and Vacā (sweet flag), rhizome of Tagara (valerian), bark of Śirīṣa (a variety of acacia) and bulb of Rasona (garlic), It may be used as Añjana and Nasya. 6. Boil Sarṣapa Taila (mustard oil) in 4 times goat’s urine and prepare Taila by Taila Pāka method. Whole body of the patient is to be massaged with it. B. Between the attacks The following preparations are useful for preventing the attacks of Apasmāra.
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Take the powder of Hiṅgu (asafoetida), fruit of Amlavetasa, Śuṇṭhī (dried ginger), Souvarcala Lavaṇa (a salt) and seed of Dāḍima (pomegranate) in equal parts. Its 3 to 6 g. is to be taken with 14 to 28 ml. decoction of Yava (barley) twice a day. 2. Prepare a Siddha Ghṛta with Souvarcala Lavaṇa (a salt), fruit rind of Harītakī (chebulic myrobalan) and Trikaṭu. Its 12 to 24 g. is to be taken twice a day.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Sārasvata Cūrṇa:1 to 3 g., to be taken with 50 ml. water twice a day. 2. Daśamūla Kvātha: 14 to 28 ml., to be taken twice a day. 3. Jaṭāmānsyādi Kvātha: 14 to 28 ml., to be taken with 4 to 6 g. honey twice a day. 4. Vacā Brāhmi Yoga: 0-5 to 1 g., to be taken with 4 to 6 g. honey twice a day (with caution). 5. Brāhmī Vaṭī: 1 to 2 Vaṭī, to be taken with 50 ml. water twice a day. 6. Svalpa Pañca Gavya Ghṛta: 3 to 6 g., to be taken twice a day. 7. Brāhmī Ghṛta: 12 to 24 g., to be taken with 50 ml. warm water twice a day. 8. Aśvagandhāriṣṭa: 14 to 28 ml., to be taken with equal quantity of water, twice a day after meal. 9. Daśamūlāriṣṭa: 14 to 28 ml., to taken with equal quantity of water, twice a day after meal. 10. Sārasvatāriṣṭa: 14 to 28 ml., to be taken with equal quantity of water, twice a day after meal.
PATHYA: Godhūma (wheat), Mudga (phaseolus bean), Śāli variety of rice; milk, ghee; Leaves of Brāhmī (Indian pennywort), Paṭola (a small variety of cucumber), Taṇḍulīyaka (a variety of amaranth) and Vāstūka (a variety of chenopodium); Drākṣā (dried grape fruit) are the useful articles of diet for the patient of Apasmāra.
APATHYA: Wine, hot food, incompatible food; suppression of urges like hunger, thirst and sleep and living in insanitary places should be restricted. Patient should be saved from the sources of water like well, pond etc and fire.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Mṛgī, Māripeloya Roga, Beng: Mṛgī Roga, Dogr: Mṛgī, Guj: Phephḍānu Vkoī Ābuna, Hind: Mirgī, Kan: Malaroga, Maly: Apasmāram, Mra: Phemphaḍe, Apasmāra, Ori: Hapara, Panj: Mirgī, Tam: Kākkaivolippu, Tel: Somma, Eng: Epilepsy

Title: AMLAPITTA
Sanskrit: अम्लपित्त
INTRO: It is the disease caused by the excessive formation of acid in the stomach and due to which patient feels burning sensation in the throat and heart area.
SYMPTOMS: Bitter or acidic eructation, burning sensation in throat and heart area, nausea, loss of appetite, indigestion, prostration and heaviness in the body are the main signs and symptoms of Amlapitta.
TREATMENT: Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Mix Lājāsaktu, Śarkarā (raw sugar) and honey in equal quantity. Its 100 to 200 g. is to be taken twice a day. 3. Take powdered fruit rind of Harītakī (chebulic myrobalan) and whole plant of Bhṛṅgarāja in equal quantity. Its 3 to 6 g. is to be taken 12 g. of Guḍa (jaggery) and warm water twice a day. 4. Take dried rhizome of Haridrā (turmeric), leaf of Paṭola and fruit rind of Āmalakī (embelie myrobalan) in equal parts and make the powder. Its 3 to 6 g. is to be taken with the fresh juice of Ārdraka (ginger) and 30 drops of papaya latex twice a day. 5. Prepare decoction from the equal parts of stem of Guḍūcī, fruit of Nimba, leaf of Paṭola (a variety of small cucumber) and Triphalā. Its 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken twice a day. 6. Prepare decoction of equal parts of Śuṇṭhī (dried ginger), fruit of Dhānyaka (coriander) and leaf of Paṭola (a variety of small cucumber). Its 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken twice a day. 7. Prepare decoction of equal parts of leaves of Paṭola (a variety of small cucumber) and Vāsā (vasaka), Śuṇṭhī (dried ginger), stem of Guḍūcī and rhizome of Kaṭukī. Its 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken with 4 to 6 g. honey twice a day.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Avipattikara Cūrṇa: 3 to 6 g. is to be taken with 50 ml. warm water twice a day. 2. Daśāṅga Kvātha: 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken with 4 to 6 g. honey twice a day. 3. Dhātri Loha: 500 mg. to 1 g. is to be taken with sufficient ghee to make a paste, twice a day. 4. Kāmadudhā Rasa: 250 to 500 mg. is to be taken with sufficient honey to make a paste twice a day. 5. Līlāvilāsa Rasa: 60 to 250 mg. is to be taken with sufficient honey to make a paste twice a day. 6. Sūtaśekhara Rasa: 250 to 500 mg. is to be taken with sufficient honey to make a paste twice a day. 7. Śaṅkha Bhasma: 250 to 500 mg. is to be taken with sufficient honey to make a paste twice a day. 8. Kṣāra-Rāja: 1 to 2 g. is to be taken with 5 to 10 ml. fresh juice of Nimbū (lemon) and 6 g. Śarkarā (raw sugar) twice a day. 9. Nārikelā Khaṇḍa: 6 to 12 g. is to be taken with 100 to 250 ml. milk twice a day.
PATHYA: It is better to keep the patient on milk diet for sometime. Other beneficial articles for the patients of Amlapitta are old rice of Śāli variety, Godhūma (wheat), Yava (barley), Mudga (pahseolus bean), Saktu, Śarkarā (raw sugar); honey, milk, cold water; fruits of Kāravellaka (bitter gourd), Kadalī (banana), Kapittha (wood apple), Dāḍima (pomegranate) and Āmalakī (embelic myrobalan); fruit and leaf of Paṭola (a variety of small cucumber), leaf of Vāstuka (a variety of chenopodium), and Vetasa Śuga (roots of cane).
APATHYA: Guru and amla Dravya, Navīna Anna (newly harvested cereals), incompatible items of food; seeds of Tila (seasame), Māṣa (black phaseolus bean) and Kulattha (a kind of pulse); items prepared in oil; curd, goat’s milk, and Madya (wine) are harmful for the patient of Amlapitta.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Amlapitta, Teṅgā-kāmī, Beng: Amlapitta, Dogr: Amlapitta, Kalājatu Khoḍe, Guj: Amlapitta, Hind: Khaṭṭī Ḍakāra, Kan: Hulithegukaṭṭameoṭe, Maly: Pulichu Theṭṭal, Mra: Amlapitta, Āmbaṭa Ḍhekard-Yaṇe, Panj: Peṭa Jalana, Tam: Puliyeppam, Tel: Pulitrenupulu, Eng: Hyperacidity

Title: AROCAKA
Sanskrit: अरोचक
INTRO: Arocaka is a condition in which the patient does not have desire to eat.
SYMPTOMS: In addition to loss of appetite the patient may have sensitiveness of teeth and Kaṣāya taste in the mouth due to Vāta; sour or acidic (Amla) taste and foul smelling in the mouth due to Pitta; and salty or sweet taste and feeling of sliminess, heaviness and stiffness in the mouth due to Kapha.
TREATMENT: Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Prepare decoction from the seed of Yava (barley). Its 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken with 1 g. powdered fruit of Pippalī (long pepper) and 4 to 6 g. honey twice a day. 2. Mix fresh juice obtained from the seed of Dāḍima (pomegranate) 14 ml. with 1 g. Kṛṣṇa Lavaṇa and 14 g. honey. It is to be retained in the mouth as Kavala (mouth wash) for 2 minutes. 3. Fresh juice obtained from the seed of Dāḍima (pomegranate) – 14 ml., fried seed of Jīraka (cumin) – 1 g. and Śarkarā (raw sugar) – 12 g. are to be mixed together and to be retained in the mouth as Kavala (mouth wash) for 2 minutes. 4. Macerate 26 g. of old fruit of Ciñcā (tamarind) in 100 ml. of water, strain, and add 25 g. of Guḍa (jaggery) and small quantity of powdered Tvak-Dālacīnī (cinnamon) and fruits of Elā (small cardamom) and Marica (black pepper). Take its Kavala (mouth wash) which is to be retained in the mouth for two minutes. 5. Mix Drākṣā (raisin or grape fruit), fruit rind of Harītakī (chebulic myrobalan) and Śarkarā (raw sugar) in equal parts and make the powder. Its 3 to 6 g. is to be taken with 50 ml. warm water twice a day.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Dāḍimādi Cūrṇa: 1 to 3 g., to be taken with 50 ml. water thrice a day. 2. Yavānī Sāḍava Cūrṇa: 3 to 6 g., to be taken with 50 ml. warm water twice a day. 3. Dāḍimāṣṭaka Cūrṇa: 2 to 6 g., to be taken with 50 ml. water thrice a day. 4. Lavaṇa Bhāskara Cūrṇa: 2 to 6 g., to be taken with 50 ml. warm water thrice a day. 5. Ārdraka Khanḍāvaleha: 2 to 6 g., to be taken half an hour before meal with 50 ml. water. 6. Pippalyādi Rasāyana: 3 to 6 g., to be taken thrice a day before meal with 50 ml. warm water. 7. Nārikelā Pāka: 1 to 3 g., to be taken with 100 to 250 ml. milk twice a day.
PATHYA: Godhūma (wheat), Mudga (phascoius bean), Rakta Śāli (red variety of rice); Takra (butter milk), curd, milk and ghee; leaf of Śigru (horse-radish), fruit of Paṭola (a variety of small cucumber), bulb of Rasona (garlic), Sūrana Mūla, fruit of Badara (jujube), Vetasa Śuga (cane shoot), Drākṣā (raisin or grape fruit), fruit rind of Harītakī (chebulic myrobalan) and Āmalakī (embelic myrobalan), Ārdraka (ginger), Marica (black pepper), seeds of Yavānī (ptycotis) and Dāḍima (pomegranate), fruit of Āmra (mango) are useful for the patient of Arocaka.
APATHYA: Suppression of hunger, eructation and tears; anger, fright, shock, over indulgence in food, intake of uncherished food and living in insanitary condition should be avoided.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Aruci, Beng: Aruci, Dogr: Arocaka-Dokhi, Guj: Aruci, Hind: Aruci, Kan: Aruci, Hasivunāsa, Maly: Ruciyillayma, Mra: Annadveṣa, Ori: Aruci, Panj: Bhukha Nāsa, Tam: Ruciyiṇmai, Aruci, Tel: Aruci, Eng: Anorexia

Title: ARBUDA
Sanskrit: अर्बुद
SYMPTOMS: Arbuda is a disease in which elevated, round, deep, rooted, large and immovable mass develops in any part of the body. In the early stage it is less painful, grows slowly and generally does not suppurate. It may be classified into Vātika, Paittika, Kaphaja, Raktaja, Māṁsaja and Medoja according to Doṣa and tissue of the body involved. Further the tumours are classified into two groups viz. benign and malignant. Benign tumours are less harmful while malignant tumours require immediate treatment, otherwise may lead to death of the patient.
TREATMENT: Treatment
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Mahāmañjiṣṭhādi Kvātha: 14 to 28 ml., to be taken twice a day. 2. Pañcatikta Ghṛta Guggulu: 2 to 4 pills, to be taken with 50 ml. warm water twice a day. 3. Kaiśora Guggulu: 2 to 4 pills, to be taken with 50 ml. warm water twice a day. 4. Kāñcanāra Guggulu: 2 to 4 pills, to be taken with 50 ml. warm water twice a day. 5. Sārivādyāsava: 14 to 28 ml., to be taken twice a day with equal quantity of water after meal.
PATHYA: Old Śāli variety of rice; seeds of Yava (barley), Kodrava and Mudga (phaseolus bean) and leaves of Paṭola (a variety of small cucumber and Śigru (horse-radish) are useful for the patient of Arbuda.
APATHYA: Guru and Amla Dravya; Māṣa (black phaseolus), Māṁsa (meat), fruit of Paṭola (a variety of small cucumber), cream, curd, casein and cane sugar products, and sweet dishes are harmful for the patient of Arbuda.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Nerua, Temuna, Beng: Arbuda, Āba, Dogr: Viyāda, Rasolī, Guj: Granṭhā, Gāntha, Hind: Rasaulī, Kan: Arbuda, Maly: Arbudam, Mra: Ganṭha, Ori: Ābu, Tam: Arbudakkaṭṭi, Kajhalai, Tel: Puṭṭakurupu, Eng: Tumour

Title: ARŚA
Sanskrit: अर्श
INTRO: Arśa (piles) is a condition in which a fleshy swelling of variable size, shape and colour appears (due to varicosity of veins) in the anus. From the treatment point of view Arśa may be divided into two groups viz. Śuṣkārśa and Srāvī Arśa.
SYMPTOMS: Appearance of fleshy swelling (Māṁśāṅkura) in the anus, obstruction to the passage of gases, pain particularly on defecation, diminished appetite and constipation are the general signs and symptoms of Arśa. In addition to these, following are the specific symptoms of Śuṣkarśa and Srāvī Arśa. a. Śuṣkarśa: The piles which generally do not bleed are known as Śuṣkārśa. This type of piles occur due to the dominance of Vāyu and Kapha. b. Srāvī Arśa (Raktārśa): Srāvī Arśa are the piles which occur due to the dominance of Pitta and Rakta. In this condition patient passes suddenly streaks of bright red blood with the stool. Sometimes it may bleed profusely leading to the complications like anaemia.
TREATMENT: Treatment Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. 16 g. powder of wood of Rakta Candana (red sandal) is to be kept in 400 ml. of water to make Siddha Jala. It is to be taken twice a day. 2. Powder of equal part of fruit pulp of Bilva (bael), Śuṇṭhī (dried ginger), fruit of Yavānī (ptycotis) and root of Citraka (leadwort), to be taken in 3 g. dose with Takra (butter milk) twice a day. 3. Prepare Sūraṇa Kanda (amorophallus-elephant’s foot) by Puṭapāka method and its 12 to 25 g. is to be taken after mixing with 6 to 12 ml. of Sarṣapa Taila (mustard oil) and 1 g. of Lavaṇa (common salt), twice a day. 1. Powder of Nāgakeśara (flower stamen of iron wood tree) – 6 g., butter – 25 g. and Śarkarā (raw sugar) – 10 g., to be taken once in the morning. 2. Grind the root of Apāmārga (prickly chaff) – 25 g. in Taṇḍulodaka (rice washing) and strain. Add to it 250 ml. of goat’s milk and 1 g. powdered root of Śatāvarī (wild asparagus). It is to be taken twice a day.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Vijayā Cūrṇa: 3 to 6 g., to be taken with 50 ml. warm water twice a day. 2. Pathyādi Kvātha: 14 to 28 ml., to be taken twice a day. 1. Samaśarkarā Cūrṇa: 5 to 12 g., to be taken with 50 ml. water twice a day. 2. Vijayā Cūrṇa: 3 to 6 g., to be taken with 50 ml. water twice a day. 3. Arśakuṭhāra Rasa: 1 to 2 pills, to be taken with 50 ml. water twice a day. 4. Nityodita Rasa: 250 mg., to be taken with 5 to 10 g. ghee twice a day. 5. Candraprabhā Vaṭī (Arśadhikāra): 1 to 2 pills, to be taken with 50 ml. water twice a day. 6. Take fruit of small variety of Harītakī (chebulic myrobalan), whole plant of Dūrvā (doob grass), root of Pippalī (long pepper) and Nāgakeśara (stamen of Indian iron wood tree) in equal parts and make pills of 8 g. by adding Svarasa (fresh juice) or decoction prepared from fruit rind of Āmalakī (embelic myrobalan). Such 1 to 2 pills is to be taken with Takra (butter milk) twice a day.
PATHYA: Godhūma (wheat), Śāli variety of rice, seeds of Yava (barley) and Kulattha (dolichos bean); goat’s milk, butter; fruit of Kapittha (wood apple), leaf and fruit of Paṭola (a variety of small cucumber), root of Punarnavā pigweed), Sūraṇa Kanda (tuber of amorophallus-elephant’s foot), leaf of Vāstūka (a variety of chenopodium), fruit rind of Āmalakī (embelic myrobalan) are the useful articles of diet for the patient of Arśa (piles).
APATHYA: Māṣa (balck phaseolus bean), seed of Tila (sesame), Piṇyāka (oil cake), Piṣṭamaya Dravya (dishes prepared from Piṣṭi); fried, constipative and difficult to digest articles of food are harmful for the patient of Arśa (piles). Excessive use of water, sun bath, heat and riding; and suppression of natural urges of urination and defecation should be avoided.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Kechumuri, Arśa, Beng: Arśa, Dogr: Babāśira, Mesiyama, Guj: Harasa, Masa, Hind: Bavāśira, Kan: Mūlavyādhi, Maly: Mūlakkuru, Mra: Mūlavyādha, Tam: Mūlanoy, Mūlam, Tel: Mūla Vyādhi, Ariśamolalu, Eng: Haemorrhoid, piles

Title: AŚMARI (MŪTRAŚMARI)
Sanskrit: अश्मरी (मूत्राश्मरी)
INTRO: Aśmarī is a disease caused by the formation or lodging of a stone in the urinary passage. It is also called Mūtraśmarī.
SYMPTOMS: Severe Abdominal pain in the umbilical or urinary bladder region referred to perineal raphe or penis, obstruction to urinary flow due to to which patient passes urine drop by drop with difficulty, effort to urinate causes intense pain, the pain is aggravated by running, jumping, riding and walking long distance, and blood in the urine are the main signs and symptoms of Mūtrāśmarī.
TREATMENT: Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Decoction prepared from the fruit rind of Āmalakī (embelic myrobalan) – 14 to 28 ml., to be taken with 25 g. Guḍa (jaggery) twice a day. 2. Decoction prepared from the seed of Kulattha (dolichos bean) – 14 to 28 ml., to be taken thrice a day. 3. Prepare decoction from 12 g. bark of Varuṇa, 2 g. Śuṇṭhī (dried ginger) and 6 g. fruit of Gokṣura (small caltrops). Its 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken with 0.5 g. yavakṣāra and 25 g. Guḍa (jaggery) twice a day. 4. Prepare decoction from equal part of bark of Varuṇa, rhizome of Pāṣāṇa Bheda (saxifraga), Śuṇṭhī (dried ginger) and fruit of Gokṣura (small caltrops). Its 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken with 0.5 g. Yavakṣāra twice a day. 5. Prepare decoction from the equal part of Elā (cardamom), roots of Pippalī (long pepper) and Madhuyaṣṭi (glycyrrhiza), bark of Śigru (horse-radish), leaf of Vāsā (vasaka), rhizome of Pāṣāṇabheda (saxifrage), seed of Reṇuka, fruit of Gokṣura (small caltrops) and root bark of Eraṇḍa (caster). Its 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken with 5 g. Śuddha Śilājatu, 25 g. Śarkarā (raw sugar) and 14 g. honey twice a day. 6. Prepare decoction from the equal part of roots of Kuśa (sacred grass), Ikṣu (sugarcana), Kāṣa, Sara and Darbha, seed of Kulattha (dolichos bean), bark of Varuṇa and fruit of Gokṣura (small caltrops). Its 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken with 25 g. Śarkarā (raw sugar) and 0.5 g. Yavakṣāra twice a day. 7. Decoction prepared from the equal part of fruit of Gokṣura (small caltrops), Śuṇṭhī (dried ginger), leaf of Eraṇḍa (castor), bark of Varuṇa is to be taken in 14 to 28 ml. dose twice a day.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Bṛhat Varuṇādi Kvātha: 14 to 28 ml., to be taken with 0.5 g. of Yavakṣāra twice a day. 2. Candraprabhā Vaṭī: 1 to 2 pills, to be taken with water twice a day. 3. Gokṣurādi Guggulu: 1 to 2 pills, to be taken with water twice a day.
PATHYA: Old Śāli variety of rice, seed of Kulattha (dolichos bean), Ārdraka (ginger), fruit of Kūṣmāṇḍa and leaves of Śālaparṇi and Varuṇa are the useful articles of diet for the patient suffering from the urinary stone (Mūtrāśmarī).
APATHYA: Incompatible, acidic, constipative and Guru items of food and drink should be eliminated from the diet. Avoid suppression of natural calls like urination.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Patharī Roga, Beng: Mūtrāśmari, Dogr: Patharī Roga, Guj: Patharī, Hind: Patharī, Kan: Mūtrada Kallu, Maly: Kallaḍappu, Mra: Mūtrabheda, Mūtaknaḍā, Ori: Patnuri, Panj: Patharī, Tam: Kalladaippunoy, Achmari, Tel: Mūtramulo Rāyi, Eng: Stone in bladder

Title: AṢṬHĪLĀ
Sanskrit: अष्ठीला
INTRO: A round stone like gland situated at the neck of urinary bladder known as prostate when enlarges and causes obstruction to the external passage of urine then it is known as Aṣṭhīla. It generally occurs in the old age.
TREATMENT: Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Śilājatu – 1 g., to be taken with 250 ml. milk twice a day. 2. Decoction of fruit of Gokṣura (small caltrops) – 14 to 28 ml., to be taken with 14 g. honey and 25 g. Śarkarā (raw sugar), twice a day. 3. Fresh juice obtained from the fruit pulp of Kūṣmāṇḍa (a kind of pumpkin gourd) is to be taken in 56 ml. dose with 0.5 g. Yavakṣāra and 25 g. Śarkarā (raw sugar) twice a day. 4. Kalka (paste) prepared from 2 g. wood of Śveta Candana (white sandal) in 2 ml. water is to be taken with 56 ml. Taṇḍulodaka (rice washing) and 25 g. Śarkarā (raw sugar), twice a day. 5. Seed of Karkaṭī (cucumber) – 25 g. bruised in 25 ml. Kāñji with 4 g. Saindhava (rock-salt) is to be divided in two doses. One dose is to be taken in the morning and one in the evening. 6. Powder of equal part of seed of Karkaṭī (cucumber), Saindhava (rock-salt) and Triphalā (fruit rind of three myrobalans) – 3 to 6 g., to be taken with 50-100 ml. warm water twice a day.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Mala Mūtra Ruhaka Granthi, Beng: Aṣṭhīla, Dogr: Mūtra Grandhi, Dakhontara, Maly: Kujhavi, Mra: Aṣṭhīlā, Panj: Purakha Granthi Vādha, Tam: Purastha Kūla Thapithan, Eng: Enlarged prostate

Title: ASTHI BHAṄGA
Sanskrit: अस्थि भङ्ग
INTRO: Due to trauma if dislocation of the joint or fracture occurs then this condition is known as Bhagna (Asthi Bhaṅga). In Short it is of two types viz. Sandhi Bhagna (dislocation) and Kāṇḍa-Bhagna (fracture).
SYMPTOMS: Sandhi-Bhagna (Dislocation): Due to trauma if the only displacement of the joint occurs then this condition is known as Sandhi-Bhagna. Loss of movements like contraction, expansion etc. at the affected joint and severe pain on the slightest touch are the main symptoms of Sandhi-Bhagna (dislocation). Kāṇḍa-Bhagna (Fracture): Breaking of the bone is known as Kāṇḍa-Bhagna. Looseness, swelling, intense pain and tenderness in the affected part, and no relief of pain in any posture are the main symptoms of Kāṇḍa-Bhagna.
TREATMENT: Support the fractured part with splint after bringing the bones to normal position as far as possible, pack with cotton, apply bandage and give rest and support. For setting of bone consult a bone expert. Following treatment is useful for the early healing of the settled bone.
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Take equal part of stem of Asthisanhāraka, purified Lākṣā (lac), Godhūma (wheat) and bark of Arjuna, and make the power. Its 3 to 6 g. is to be taken with 50 ml. water twice a day.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Powdered and purified (Śuddha) Lākṣā (lac) – 1 to 3 g. is to be taken with sufficient honey to make a paste, twice a day. 2. Lākṣādi Guggulu: 2 to 4 pills, to be taken with 50 ml. warm water twice a day.
PATHYA: Red Śāli variety of rice, Godhūma (wheat), soup of Satīna (Pea); milk, ghee, oil, meat soup and honey; bulb of Rasona (garlic), leaf of Paṭola (a variety of small cucumber), fruit of Śigru (horse-radish), Drākṣā (raisin or grape fruit); fruit rind of Āmalakī (embelic myrobalan) are the useful articles of diet for the patient of Asthi-Bhaṅga.
APATHYA: Amla, Lavaṇa, Kaṭu, Kṣāra and Rūkṣa Dravya are harmful for the patients of fracture and dislocation. Open sun, physical exercise and sexual intercourse should be avoided.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Hāḍa Bhaṅga, Beng: Asthibhaṅga, Dogr: Haḍḍī Ṭuṭanā, Maḍḍī Ṭuṭanā, Guj: Hāḍa Kā Bha gauṅa, Hind: Haḍḍī Ṭuṭanā, Kan: Mule Murita, Maly: Ellodivu, Mra: Hāḍa Moḍne, Bhega, Ori: Hāḍabhaṅgijiba, Panj: Haḍḍī Ṭuṭṇā, Tam: Elumbu Murivu, Tel: Emuka Viruguṭa, Eng: Fracture of bone

Title: ASTHI-KṢAYA
Sanskrit: अस्थि क्षय
INTRO: Abscess of the bone leading to suppuration may be called as Asthi-Kṣaya.
SYMPTOMS: In the initial stage the resultant pus may not get an outlet and the patient feels intense heat like that his affected part is burning in the fire, and it may take prolonged course giving considerable distress. However, if the pus gets an outlet due to the decay of the tissues or through surgical intervention, then a slimy, fatty, white, purulent and cold discharge oozes out of the affected part.
TREATMENT: In case of abscess finding an outlet, the disease should be treated like Vidradhi. In case of prolonged course of the disease a specialist should be consulted.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Hāḍakṣaya, Beng: Asthikhaya, Dogr: Astiksaya, Haḍḍī Paṭṭalipona, Guj: Hāda Kā Nāśa, Hind: Asthi Suṣiratā, Kan: Asthikṣaya, Maly: Asthikṣayam, Mra: Hādanci Jhuja, Hāḍancha Kṣaya, Panj: Haḍḍī Dā Tapadika, Haḍḍi Dā Nasūra, Tam: Elippu Noy, Elumburukkinoy, Eng: Tuberculosis of bone/osteomyelitis

Title: ĀDHMĀNA
Sanskrit: आध्मान
INTRO: Distension of abdomen due to the accumulation of gases accompanied by colicy pain is known as Ādhmāna.
TREATMENT: Apply for fomentation and turpentine stoop on the abdomen.
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Decoction of equal part of Triphalā and Trikaṭu – 14 to 28 ml., to be taken twice a day. 2. Take seed of Ajājī (nigella) – 4 parts Śuṇṭhī (dried ginger) – 2 parts, Kṛṣṇa Lavaṇa (a salt) – 1 part and Śaṅkha Bhasma – 1part, and make the powder. Its 3 to 6 g. is to be taken with 50 ml. warm water twice a day.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Pācana Cūrṇa: 2 to 6 g. is to be taken with 50 ml. warm water twice a day. 2. Samudrādi Cūrṇa: 1 g. is to be take with 50 ml. warm water twice a day. 3. Narsārādi Cūrṇa: 3 to 6 g. is to be taken with 50 ml. warm water twice a day. 4. Hiṅgvāṣṭaka Cūrṇa: 3 to 6 g. is to be taken with 50 ml. warm water twice a day. 5. Nimbū Pānaka: 6 to 12 ml. is to be taken twice a day. 6. Nimbū Drava: 6 to 12 ml. is to be taken with 6 to 12 ml. warm water twice a day.
PATHYA: Laghu Anna like Mudga (phaseolus bean), old Śāli variety of rice; bulb of Rasona (garlic); fruits of Kāravellaka (bitter gourd) and Śigru (horse radish), leaf and fruit of Paṭola (a variety of small cucumber); and leaf of Vāstūka (a variety of chenopodium – white goosefoot) are the useful articles of diet for the patient of Ādhmāna.
APATHYA: Kaṭu, Tikta, Kaṣāya, Rūkṣa and Guru Anna; seed of Tila (seasame), Śimbi Dhānya (legumes) are harmful for the patient of Ādhmāna. Incompatible items of food in diet, unnatural postures, sexual intercourse, sitting up at nights, exercise, suppression of urges, anger and grief should be avoided.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Peṭa Phūla, Beng: Ādhmāna, Peṭaphanapa, Dogr: Aphārā, Guj: Aphāro, Hind: Peṭaphūlanā, Aphārā, Kan: Hotte Ubbarā, Maly: Vayaraṭacu Vīrpu, Mra: Poṭa Phūgi, Ori: Peṭa Phampā, Panj: Aphārā, Tam: Vayattru Porumal, Tel: Kaḍupubbaramu, Eng: Tympanites

Title: ĀNĀHA (BADDHAKOṢṬHA)
Sanskrit: आनाह (बद्धकोष्ठ)
INTRO: Ānāha is a disease characterised by the slow accumulation of Āma or Purīṣa (faecal matter) in the intestines due to vitiation of Vāta. It is of two types according to the involvement of Āma or Purīṣa.
SYMPTOMS: 1. Āmaja Ānāha: if the disease is due to the accumulation of Āma, then the patient may have the symptoms like thirst, burning sensation in the head, pain in abdomen, suppression of eructation and coryza. 2. Purīṣaja Ānāha: In this condition retention of faeces and urine, acute pain, fainting, vomiting of faecal matter and oedema are found.
TREATMENT: Patient of Purīṣaja Ānāha should be hospitalized. Following treatment may be tried for a benign case.
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Take purified and fried Hiṅgu (asafoetida), Amlavetasa, fruit of Yavānī (ptychotis), Saindhava (rock-salt) and seed of Miśreyā (fennel) in equal parts, and make the powder. Its 2 to 6 g. is to be taken with 5 ml. fresh juice of Nimbū (lemon) twice a day.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Triphalā Cūrṇa: 2 to 6., to be taken with 50 ml. warm water twice a day. 2. Rasonādi Vaṭī: 1 to 2 pills, to be taken with 50 ml. warm water twice a day. 3. Harītakī Khaṇḍa: 3 to 6 g., to be taken with 50 ml. warm water twice a day. 4. Sukumāra Kumāra Ghṛta: 6 to 12 g., to be taken with 250 ml. milk twice a day.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Vāhya Savakasa, Beng: Koṣṭhabaddhā, Dogr: Kabis, Gandhiati, Guj: Kabjīyata, Hind: Kabjī, Kabja, Kan: Malabhaḍhathe, Maly: Vedanayodukūdiya, Vayaruvirpu, Mra: Poṭa Phūgī, Malāvarodha, Ori: Koṣṭhabaddha, Panj: Kabaja, Tam: Malachchikkal, Malakaṭṭu, Malbantham, Tel: Kaḍupubbaramu, Eng: Constipation

Title: ĀMAVĀTA
Sanskrit: आमवात
INTRO: Vitiated Āma and Vāyu by involving Koṣṭha, Trika and Sandhi (joints) cause pain in the joints, loss of appetite, indigestion, stiffness of the body, weakness and heaviness in the heart area and this condition is known as Āmavāta.
SYMPTOMS: Pain and inflammation of one or more joints particularly of hand, foot, tarsals, knee, thigh and sacrum; scorpion bite like pain in the affected joints, loss of appetite, indigestion; fever, vague pain in different parts of the body, feeling of heaviness in the body, lack of initiative, disturbance in sleep habit, stiffness in heart area, constipation are the signs and symptoms of Āmavāta. The disease ultimately leads to the disability.
TREATMENT: Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Decoction of equal part of Śuṇṭhī (dried ginger) and stem of Guḍūcī – 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken with 6 g. powder of fruit rind of Harītakī (chebulic myrobalan) twice a day.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Ajmodādi Cūrṇa: 1 to 3 g., to be taken with 50 ml. warm water twice a day. 2. Vaiśvanāra Cūrṇa: 3 to 6 g. is to be taken with 50 ml. warm water twice a day. 3. Guḍūcyādi Kvātha: 14 to 28 ml., to be taken twice a day. 4. Mahā-Rasnādi Kvātha: 28 to 56 ml., to be taken before meal twice a day. 5. Rāsnā-Daśamūla Kvātha: 14 to 28 ml., to be taken with Eraṇḍa Taila (castor oil) – 7 to 14 ml. once a day early in the morning. 6. Rāsnādi Kvātha: 14 to 28 ml., to be taken twice a day. 7. Hiṅgulesvara Rasa: 1 to 2 pills, to be taken with 50 ml. warm water twice a day. 8. Mahā Yogarāja Guggulu: 1 to 2 pills, to be taken with 50 ml. warm water thrice a day. 9. Yogarāja Guggulu: 1 to 2 pills, to be taken with 50 ml. warm water thrice a day. 10. Siṁhanāda Guggulu: 1 to 2 pills, to be taken with 50 ml. warm water thrice a day. 11. Viṣatinduka Vaṭī: 1 to 2 pills, to be taken with 50 ml. warm water twice a day. 12. Eraṇḍa Pāka: 12 to 24 g., to be taken with 50 ml. warm water once a day.
PATHYA: Rakta Śāli (a red variety of rice), seeds of Kodrava (a type of cereal), Śyāmāka (a type of cereal), Yava (barley) and Kulattha (dolichos bean); warm water; Ārdraka (ginger), bulb of Rasona (garlic), leaf and fruit of Paṭola (a variety of small cucumber), root of Punarnavā (pigweed), leaves of Śigru (horse-radish) and Vāstūka (a variety of chenopodium, white goose-foot) and fruit of Kāravellaka (bitter gourd) are the useful articles of diet for the patient of Āmavāta.
APATHYA: Guru, Abhiṣyandi Anna; seed of Māṣa (black phaseolus bean); milk, curd, Guḍa (jaggery); incompatible and unrelished foods, fish, excessive eating, nonpotable water; sitting up at night; suppression of calls of nature and exposure to eastern winds are harmful for the patient of Āmavāta.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Jaḍabāta, Beng: Āmabāta, Dogr: Āmavāta, Gaṭhiyā, Guj: Sāndhanovā, Hind: Gaṭhiyā, Kan: Vāyu Novu, Maly: Āmavātham, Mra: Āmavāta, Ori: Anthuganthivāta, Panj: Gaṭhiā, Tam: Kīlavāyu, Tel: Vāta Kīllanoppulu, Eng: Rheumatism

Title: ĀMĀŚAYA VRAṆA (ANNA-DRAVA ŚŪLA EVAṀ PARIṆĀMA ŚŪLA)
Sanskrit: आमाशय व्रण (अन्नद्रव शूल एवं परिणाम शूल)
INTRO: Abdominal pain having definite relation with meal is due to Āmāśaya Vraṇa (peptic ulcer). Depending upon the site of ulcer, it is of two types viz. Annadrava Śūla (gastric ulcer) and Pariṇāma Śūla (duodenal ulcer)
SYMPTOMS: 1. Annadrava Śūla (Gastric ulcer): This type of abdominal pain occurs due to the ulcer in the stomach. In this disease patient may have pain immediately after taking the meal or during the digestion and the pain is not relieved after taking Pathya, Apathya or meal but the pain may be relieved by vomiting. 2. Pariṇāma Śūla (Duodenal Ulcer): This type of pain is caused by the ulcer in the duodenum. In this disease the pain occurs after digestion of food i.e. 3 to 4 hours of taking the meal. Its other symptoms are burning sensation, nausea and vomiting.
TREATMENT: In this disease patient may vomit blood and in that case patient should be hospitalized immediately.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Śūlavajraṇi Vaṭī: 1 to 2 pills, to be taken 10 g. honey or 50 ml. warm water to relieve the pain when it is intolerable. 2. Kāmadudhā Rasa: 250 mg. is to be taken with sufficient honey to make a paste twice a day. 3. Sūtaśekhara Rasa: 120 mg. is to be taken with honey three times a day. 4. Kapardikā Bhasma: 250 mg. is to be taken with 100 to 250 ml. milk twice a day. 5. Nārikela Lavaṇa Kṣāra: 1 g. is to be taken with water two times a day. 6. Dhātrī Lauha: 1 to 2 pills, to be taken with 4 to 6 g. honey or 100 to 250 ml. milk, twice a day. 7. Triphalā Lauha: 1 to 2 pills, to be taken with 4 to 6 g. honey or 100 to 250 ml. milk, twice a day. 8. The treatment described for Amlapitta may also be given.
PATHYA: It is better to keep the patient on milk diet. Unfried preparations of Godhūma (wheat), milk and casein products, banana, small and repeated liquid meals are the useful articles of diet for the patients of Āmāśaya Vraṇa.
APATHYA: Dravya having Amla, Kaṭu and Lavaṇa Rasa, fried and spicy food, spirituous liquor, rice and Śuṇṭhī (dried ginger) are harmful for the patients of Āmāśaya Vraṇa. Sitting up at night, exposure to sun, excessive intercourse, suppression of natural urges, grief and anger should be avoided.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Pakasthali Ghā, Beng: Āmāśaya Vraṇa, Dogr: Kāleja Derda, Hind: Udaravraṇa, Kan: Hotte Hunnu, Maly: Kuṭāl Punnu, Mra: Āmāśayatila Vraṇe, Tam: Vali Gunmam, Tel: Kaḍupulo Puṇḍu, Eng: Peptic ulcer (gastric ulcer and duodenal ulcer)

Title: UDARA-ROGA
Sanskrit: उदररोग
INTRO: Long standing Mandāgni (diminished digestive power) and Ajīrṇa (indigestion) cause generalized enlargement of the abdomen and this condition is known as Udara Roga. Out of the eight types of udara Roga four are Doṣaja viz. Vātodara, Pittodara, Kaphodara and Sannipātodar, fifth is due to the enlargement of spleen or liver i.e. Plīhodara and Yakṛddālyudara, sixth is due to the intestinal obstruction i.e. Baddha – Gudodara, seventh is due to the injury of the abdomen i.e. Parisrāvyudara and the last is due to the accumulation of fluid i.e. Jalodara.
SYMPTOMS: Distension of abdomen, loss of appetite, indigestion, retention of flatus and faeces, weakness, fatigue, difficulty in walking, oedema, burning sensation and torpor are the general signs and symptoms of Udara Roga. In addition to these, followings are the specific signs and symptoms of Doṣaja Udara Roga. 1. Vātodara: Dry cough, constipation, oedema over hands and feet, sounds in the intestine and resonant sound on percussion are the signs and symptoms of Vātodara. 2. Pittodara: Fever, burning sensation, giddiness, fainting, diarrhea, thirst, soft abdomen on palpation and tendency to suppurate are the signs and symptoms of Pittodara. 3. Kaphodara: Oedema, heaviness in the body, excessive sleep, loss of appetite, nausea, cough, dyspnoea and firm and cold abdomen on palpation are the signs and symptoms of Kaphodara. 4. Saanipātodara: It occurs due to slow poisoning. Emaciation, anaemia, frequent fainting, dryness in the mouth are the main signs and symptoms of Sannipātodara.
TREATMENT: The patients suffering from Pittodara and Sannipātodara should be treated in the hospital. The treatment of Vātodara and Kaphodara is as follows. Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Decoction of Triphalā – 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken with 7 to 14 ml. Eraṇḍa Taila (castor oil) twice a day. 2. Gomūtra Siddha Daśamūla Kvātha – 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken twice a day. 1. Take fruits of Yavānī (ptychotis), Śveta Jīraka (cumin) and Marica (black pepper), Śuṇṭhī (dried ginger), root of Pippalī (long pepper) and Saindhava (rock salt) in equal parts and make the powder. Its 3 to 6 g. is to be taken with 5 g. honey and 100 ml. Takra (butter milk) twice a day. 2. Decoction prepared from the bark of Śigru (horse-radish) – 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken after adding 1 to 3 g. powder of equal parts of root of Pippalī (long pepper), Marica (black pepper) and fruit of Amlavetasa twice a day. 3. Decoction prepared from Śuṇṭhī (dried ginger) – 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken by adding 2 g. powdered fruit rind of Harītakī (chebulic myrobalan) and 7 to 14 ml. Gomūtra (cow’s urine) twice a day.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Hiṅgvāṣṭaka Cūrṇa: 3 to 6 g., to be taken with 50 ml. warm water twice a day. 2. Rasonādi Vaṭī: 2 to 4 pills are to be taken with 50 ml. warm water twice a day. 3. Śaṅkha Bhasma: 250 to 750 mg. is to be taken with 50 ml. warm water twice a day. 4. Kalyāṇa Kṣāram: 5 to 10 g. is to be taken with 5 to 10 g. ghee, quarter hour before meal or one hour after meal twice a day. 5. Arka Lavaṇa: 1 g. is to be taken with 50 ml. warm water twice a day. 6. Vāsā Kaṇṭakārī Lehyam: 3 to 6 g. is to be taken one hour before or after meal twice a day. 7. Pippalī Ghṛta: 12 to 24 g. is to be taken with 100 ml. warm water or milk twice a day. 1. Hiṅgvāṣṭaka Cūrṇa: 3 to 6 g. is to be taken with 50 ml. warm water twice a day. 2. Daśamūla Kvātha: 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken with 7 to 14 ml. Eraṇḍa Taila (castor oil) twice a day. 3. Śaṅkha Vaṭī: 2 to 4 pills are to be taken with 50 ml. warm water twice a day. 4. Rasonādi Vaṭī: 2 to 4 pills, to be taken with 50 ml. warm water twice a day. 5. Śambūka Bhasma: 250 to 500 mg. is to be taken with 50 ml. warm water twice a day.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Udara Roga, Beng: Udara Roga, Dogr: Udura Roga, Ḍhida Roga, Hind: Peṭa Kā Roga, Kan: Hoṭṭe Ubbara, Maly: Udararogam, Mra: Udara Roga, Poṭāche Vikāra, Panj: Peṭa De Roga, Tam: Vayiru Noygal, Eng: Diseases of the abdomen

Title: Yakṛddālyudara Evaṁ Plīhodara
Sanskrit: यकृद्दाल्युदर एवं प्लीहोदर
INTRO: Enlargement of liver (Yakṛt) – an important organ of the body situated in the right upper portion of the abdomen, is called Yakṛddālyudara. Spleen (Plīha) is situated in the left upper portion of the abdomen and its enlargement is called Plīhodara.
SYMPTOMS: In addition to the enlargement of liver or spleen, low grade fever, thirst, loss of appetite, indigestion, weakness, constipation, emaciation, pallor are the general signs and symptoms of Yakṛddālyudara and Plīhodara.
TREATMENT: Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Decoction prepared from the root of Pippalī (long pepper) – 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken twice a day. 2. Powder of root of Pippalī (long pepper) – 1 g. and Yavakṣāra – 1 g. is to be taken with 7 to 14 ml. Gomūtra (cow’s urine) twice a day. 3. Decoction prepared from equal part of bark of Rohītaka and fruit rind of Harītakī (chebulic myrobalan) – 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken twice a day. 4. Trikaṭu Siddha milk – 250 ml. is to be taken repeatedly as required. 5. Bhasma prepared from fruit shred of Tāla (palmyra toddy) – 1 g. is to be taken with 5 g. Guḍa (jaggery) twice a day.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Punarnavāṣṭaka Kvātha: 14 to 28 ml., to be taken twice a day. 2. Lokanātha Rasa: 120 to 250 mg. is to be taken with sufficient honey to make a paste twice a day. 3. Arka Lavaṇa: 500 mg. to 1 g. is to be taken with 50 ml. warm water twice a day. 4. Yakṛdāri Lauha: 250 to 500 mg. is to be taken with honey sufficient to make a paste three times a day. 5. Yakṛtaplihāri Lauha: 250 to 500 mg., to be taken with honey sufficient to make a paste after meal twice a day. 6. Nāgara Ghṛta: 12 to 24 g. is to be taken with 100 ml. warm water twice a day. 7. Kumāryāsava: 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken with equal quantity of water twice a day after meal. 8. Rohītakāriṣṭa: 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken with equal quantity of water twice a day after meal. 9. Ārogyavardhianī Vaṭī: 500 mg., to be taken with honey two times a day.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Agamamgaha Briddhi Janita Udara Roga, Beng: Jakṛtodara, Dogr: Yakṛt Ke Bedna, Kan: Hoṭṭe Ubbara, Maly: Yakṛta-udaram, Mra: Yakṛt Udara, Panj: Jigara Vādha, Tillī, Tam: Manīralnoy, Kalliralnoy, Kalliral Thabitham, Manīral Thabitham, Tel: Kārjamu Peddadaguṭa, Eng: Enlargement of liver, enlargement of spleen

Title: Jalodara
Sanskrit: जलोदर
INTRO: Accumulation of fluid in the (peritoneum of) abdomen is called Jalodara.
SYMPTOMS: Enlargement in the size of abdomen, eversion of umbilicus, fullness of the flanks, presence of fluid thrill, shifting dullness on percussion, loss of appetite, weakness, thirst, pain in abdomen are the main signs and symptoms of Jalodara.
TREATMENT: Salt restricted diet should be given till the disappearance of fluid from the abdomen.
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Decoction prepared from the root of Punarnavā (pigweed) – 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken with 2 g. powdered root of Punarnavā (pigweed) and 3 g. powder of Triphalā, twice a day. 2. Śilājatu – 1 g. is to be taken with 3 g. powder of Triphalā twice a day. 3. Powdered root of Pippalī (long pepper) – 1 to 3 g. is to be taken with Punarnavāṣṭaka Kvātha – 14 to 28 ml. twice a day. 4. Triphalā and Trikaṭu Siddha Kṣīra – 100 ml. is to be taken twice a day. 5. Take root bark of Trivṛta (Indian turpeth) – 2 parts, fruit of Pippalī (long pepper) – 2 parts and fruit rind of Harītakī (chebulic myrobalan) – 5 parts, and make the powder. Its 6 to 12 g. is to be taken with 12 g. Guḍa (jaggery) and 100 ml. warm water or milk twice a day.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Śaṭsakāra Cūrṇa: 3 to 6 g., to be taken with 100 ml. warm water twice a day. 2. Pippalī-Vardhamāna Yoga: to be taken as directed by the physician. 3. Ārogya-Vardhinī Vaṭī: 1 g., to be taken with warm water once at bet time.
PATHYA: Patient of Udara Roga may be kept on restricted diet for few days. Milk diet gives very encouraging results. Śāli variety of rice, Mudga (phaseolus bean), Kulattha (dolichos bean), Yava (barley); goat’s milk, Uṣṭra Dugdha (she camel’s milk), cow’s milk, Takra (butter milk); Ārdraka (ginger), bulb of Rasona (garlic), fruit of Devadālī, leaf and fruit of Paṭola (a variety of small cucumber), leaf of Śigru (horse-radish) root of Punarnavā (pigweed), Tāmbūla (betel leaf) and fruit of Kadalī (banana) are the useful articles of diet for the patients of Udara Roga.
APATHYA: Guru and Abhiṣyandi articles of diet are harmful for the patients of Udara Roga. Sleeping in the day, exercise, walking and excessive intake of water should be avoided. Salt should not be given to the patient suffering from Jalodara.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Jalodara, Udari, Beng: Jalodara, Dogr: Jalodarī, Jalodara, Guj: Jalodara, Hind: Jalodara, Kan: Jalodara, Oudu, Sobāta, Maly: Mahodaram, Mra: Jalodara, Ori: Jalodudrī, Panj: Jalodara, Tam: Peruvayiru, Mahodharam, Tel: Jalodaramu, Eng: Ascites

Title: UDĀVARTA
Sanskrit: उदावर्त
INTRO: Frequent voluntary suppression of the natural urges like defecation, urination, yawning, sneezing, eructation, hunger, thirst, respiration, sleep etc. leads to a condition known as Udāvarta. In this disease symptoms like distension of abdomen, lassitude, pain, constipation, difficulty in micturation, coryza, headache etc. are found.
TREATMENT: Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Powder of root of Punarnavā (pigweed) – 1 to 3 g., fruit of Gokṣura (small caltrops) – 1 to 3 g. and Yavakṣāra – 0.5 to 1 g. is to be taken with 14 to 28 ml. Gomūtra (cow’s urine), twice a day. 2. Powder of Triphalā (fruit rind of three myrobalans)- 1 to 3 g. and Śilājatu 1 g., to be taken with Punarnavāṣṭaka Kvātha – 14 to 28 ml. twice a day. 3. Prepare decoction from the equal part of whole plant of Yavāsā (camel’s thorns) and bark of Arjuna. Its 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken with 1 g, powdered Saindhava (rock salt) and 2 g. powdered fruit pulp of Karkaṭī (cucumber), twice a day.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Kāṅkāyana Vaṭī: 1 to 2 Vaṭī, to be taken with 50 ml. warm water twice a day.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Begadharāṇa Janita Udara Bikṛti, Beng: Udābarta, Dogr: Udāvartta, Hind: Peṭa Phūlanā, Kan: Malvayu, Maly: Malabandham, Mra: Udāvarta, Ori: Urdhvavāyu, Panj: Aphārā, Tam: Malam Mūtram Vāyu Iratrinthadai

Title: UNMĀDA
Sanskrit: उन्माद
INTRO: Unmāda is a disease characterized by the unsteady state of mind (Mana), intellect (Buddhi), orientation (Sañjñā Jñāna), memory (Smṛti), insight (Bhaktī), character (Śīla), behaviour (Ceśṭā) and conduct (Ācāra).
SYMPTOMS: Confusion of intellect, fickleness of mind; loss of memory, power of understanding and wits; no feeling of pleasure or grief, abnormal behaviour towards the society and duties; irregular and incoherent talk, restlessness, unsteadiness, agitation of the eyes and mental vacuity are the general signs and symptoms of Unmāda.
TREATMENT: Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Purāṇa Ghṛta (1 year old ghee of cow) – 3 g., Vibhītaka Majjā (decorticated seed of beleric myrobalan) – 1.5 g., honey-3 g. and Śarkarā (raw sugar) – 5 to 10 g., to be taken with Dhāroṣṇa Godugdha (freshly milched cow’s milk)-100 to 250 ml. twice a day.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Sārasvata Cūrṇa: 0.5 to 2 g., to be taken with 100 to 250 ml. cow’s milk twice a day. 2. Sarpagandhā Vaṭī: 1 to 2 Vaṭī, to be taken with 100 to 250 ml. cow’s milk twice a day. 3. Drākṣāsava: 14 to 28 ml., to be taken with equal quantity of water twice a day after meal. 4. Kalyāṇaka Ghṛta: 6 to 12 g., to be taken twice a day with cow’s milk. 5. Mahā-Pañca Gavya Ghṛta: 6 to 12 g., to be taken with cow’s milk twice a day.
PATHYA: Śāli variety of rice, Mudga (phaseolus bean), Dhāroṣṇa Godugdha (freshly milched cow’s milk), Leaves of Brāhmī (Indian pennywort), Taṇḍulīya (a variety of amaranth) and Vāstūka (a variety of chenopodium), leaf and fruit of Paṭola (a variety of small cucumber), fruit of Kūṣmāṇḍa (a variety of pumpkin gourd) and Drākṣā (raisin or grape fruit) are the useful articles of diet for the patient of Unmāda.
APATHYA: Incompatible articles of food, hot spicy food and wines are harmful. Suppression of natural urges like sleep, hunger and thirst should be avoided.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Pāgala, Beng: Unmāda, Dogr: Pāgalapana, Hind: Pāgalapana, Pāgala, Maly: Bhranthu, Mra: Unmāda, Vedlagaṇe, Panj: Pāgala, Tam: Veri Noy, Tel: Picci, Eng: Insanity

Title: UPADAṀŚA
Sanskrit: उपदंश
INTRO: Upadaṁśa is a disease transmitted generally by the direct contact with the diseased genital organ of the opposite sex through sexual intercourse. It is characterized by the appearance of swelling (chancre) with or without ulcer on the genital organ (penis or vagina). The colour of the chancre may be black, pale, white or red depending upon the Doṣa involved.
TREATMENT: Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Decoction prepared from equal part of leaf of paṭola (a variety of small cucumber), bark of Nimba (neem), Triphalā and stem of Guḍūcī is to be taken in 14 to 28 ml. dose twice a day. 2. Decoction prepared from the equal part of bark of Khadira (khair tree), wood of Bījaka (Indian kino tree) is to be taken in 14 to 28 ml. dose with 1 g. Śuddha Guggulu and 2 g. powder of Triphalā, twice a day.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Sārivādi Vaṭī: 2 to 4 Vaṭī, to be taken with 50 ml. water twice a day. 2. Copacinyādi Guggulu: 0.5 to 1 g., to be taken with sufficient quantity of honey or ghee to make a paste two or three times a day. 3. Kaiśora Guggulu: 2 to 4 Vaṭī, to be taken with water twice a day. 4. Dvipāntara-Vacā-Mūla Pāka: 12 to 24 g., to be taken with milk twice a day. 5. Khadirāriṣṭa: 14 to 28 ml., to be taken with equal quantity of water twice a day after meal. 6. Mañjiṣṭhādyāriṣṭa: 14 to 28 ml., to be taken with equal quantity of water twice a day after meal.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Garmi Roga, Veśya Samparka Garmi, Beng: Updaṁsa, Dogr: Pahāḍi Roga, Sujāka, Hind: Ātaśaka, Guj: Chandi Paḍvi, Kan: Meha Hunnu, Maly: Parangi Punnu (Uṣṇa Punnu), Mra: Saṅsargana Janya Roga, Guhya Roga, Ori: Garmi, syphilis, Panj: Sujāka, Tam: Kurippum, Parangi Noy, Tel: Koruku Vyādhi, Eng: Hard and soft chancre, syphilis

Title: Phiraṅga
Sanskrit: फिरङ्ग
INTRO: Upadaṁśa (syphilis) not treated properly may become generalized through lymphatics affecting skin, mucosa and nearly all the tissues of the body and this condition is known as Phiraṅga.
TREATMENT: Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Take leaf of Nimba (neem) – 16 parts, fruit rind of Harītakī (chebulic myrobalan) – 2 parts, fruit rind of Āmalakī (embelic myrobalan) – 2 parts and rhizome of Haridrā (turmeric) – 1 part and make the powder. Its 3 g. is to be taken with 50 ml. water twice a day. 2. Take Śuddha Pārada – 12 g. and Gandhaka (sulphur) – 12 g. and make Kajjalī from it. Add it Śāli variety of rice – 12 g. and divide into seven parts. One part is to be smoken once every day for seven days.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: Following preparations should be taken cautiously or under guidance of a physician. 1. Saptaśāli Vaṭī: 1 Vaṭī, to be taken with 50 ml. water once a day for 7 days. 2. Rasakarpūra: 30 to 60 mg. concealed in Drākṣā (raisin) and fruit of Kadalī (banana) is to be taken with 50 ml. water once a day. 3. Malla-Sindūra: 60 to 250 mg. is to be taken with sufficient quantity of ghee to make a paste, twice a day. Treatment given under Upadaṁśa may also be prescribed.
PATHYA: Tikta Dravya Śāli variety of rice, Godhūma (wheat), Purāṇa Yava (old barley), seeds of Āḍhakī (pigion pea), Masūra (lentil) and Mudga (phaseolus bean); Purāṇa Ghṛta (old ghee), Tila Taila (gingelly oil), Hiṅgota Taila, Aguru Taila, Nimba Taila (neem oil); Urine of cow, camel or buffallow; leaf of Nimba (neem), leaf and fruit of Paṭola (a variety of small cucumber), leaf of Punarnavā (pigweed), Vetasa Śuga (cane shoot), Keśara (saffron), Nāgakeśara (Indian iron wood tree stamen) and Kastūrī (musk) are the useful articles of diet for the patients of Upadaṁśa and Phiraṅga. Kākamāci, fruits of Karkaṭī (cucumber) and Kaṭukośātakī (bitter luffa) and seed of Karañja (Indian beech) are also useful, but should not be given while the patient is receiving Pārada (mercury) or its preparations e.g. Kajjalī, Saptasāli Vaṭī, Rasakarpūra etc.
APATHYA: Guru, Navīna Anna (freshly harvested cereals), seed of Māṣa (black phaseolus bean); milk, curd; Guḍa (jaggery) and products of sugarcane are harmful for the patients of Upadaṁśa and Phiraṅga.

Title: URASTOYA
Sanskrit: उरस्तोय
INTRO: Accumulation of fluid into the pleura (a serous membrane investing the lungs) is known as Urastoya.
SYMPTOMS: Difficult and painful breathing, cough with excessive phlegmatic discharge, low grade fever, weakness, pain in the sides, discomfort in lying position and slight relief in sitting are the main signs and symptoms of Urastoya.
TREATMENT: Give boiled water (reduced to one fourth) whenever required.
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Powder of Triphalā (fruit rind of three myrobalans) – 1 g. and Śilājatu – 1 g. to be taken with 7 to 14 ml. of cow’s urine twice a day. 2. Prepare fine powder from the equal part of bark of Arjuna, root of Yaṣṭimadhu (glycyrrhiza) and Kuṣṭha (koot). Its 3 to 6 g. is to be taken with 100 to 200 ml. milk twice a day.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Punarnavāṣṭaka Kvātha: 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken twice a day. 2. Śṛṅga Bhasma: 250 to 500 mg. is to be taken with 4 to 6 g. honey twice a day. The treatment advised for Rājayakṣmā should also be given to the patient of Urastoya. In case of excessive accumulation of fluid, hospitalize the patient for removing the fluid.
PATHYA: Godhūma (wheat), Mudga (phaseolus bean), Śāli variety of rice, goat’s milk, cow’s milk, fruits of Kāravellaka (bitter gourd) and Paṭola (a variety of small cucumber) and leaves of Vāstūka (a variety of chenopodium) and Śigru (horse radish) are the useful articles of diet for the patient of Urastoya.
APATHYA: Guru Dravya, curd, fish, cold drinks and incompatible items of food in diet should be avoided.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Urastoya, Guj: Phephasā Mā Pānī Bharuṅ, Hind: Phephaḍe Meṁ Pān Bharṇā, Kan: Urastoya, Maly: Nenchile Nirkettu, Mra: Urostoya, Ori: Chatire Pānī, Jambika, Eng: Pleurisy

Title: ŪRUSTAMBHA
Sanskrit: ऊरुस्तम्भ
INTRO: The excessive and accumulated Āma along with Kapha, Meda and Vāyu causes rigidity of thighs and this condition is known as Ūrustambha.
SYMPTOMS: Inability to lift legs, coldness and numbness of the thighs, feeling of heaviness in the legs, loss of appetite, fever, vomiting, torpor, feeling of moist wrapping and pain in the body are the signs and symptoms of Ūrustambha.
TREATMENT: Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Take equal part of root of Pippalī (long pepper), Triphalā (frut rind of three myrobalans), Cavya and rhizome of Kaṭukī, and make a fine powder. Its 3 to 6 g. is to be taken with 4 to 6 g. honey twice a day.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Rāsnā-Saptaka Kvātha: 14 to 28 ml. to be taken twice a day. 2. Amṛtādi Guggulu: 1 to 3 g., to be taken with 50 ml. warm water twice a day.
PATHYA: Swimming against the current of water is useful. Kaṭu, Tikta and Kaṣāya Dravya, Śyāmāka, seeds of Kodrava (a variety of grain) and Kulattha (dolichos bean); fruit of Kāravellaka (bitter gourd), leaf and fruit of Paṭola (a variety of small cucumber), bulb of Rasona (garlic) and leaf of Śigru (horse radish) are the useful articles of diet for the patients of Ūrustambha.
APATHYA: Guru and Śīta Dravya, incompatible articles of food, items for which idiosyncrasy is exhibited are harmful for the patients of Ūrustambha. Snehana and Pañca Karma are contraindicated in this disease.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Urustambha, Dogr: Urustambha, Kan: Thode Vāyu, Thode Selethe, Maly: Ūrusthambha, Mra: Mānḍya Stambha Hoṇe, Tam: Thodaiththambitham

Title: KARṆA-ROGA
Sanskrit: कर्ण रोग
INTRO: The signs, symptoms and treatment of the common diseases of the ear (Karṇa Roga) are as follows.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Kānāvi Roga, Beng: Karṇa Roga, Dogr: Karṇa Roga, Hind: Kāna Ke Roga, Kan: Kiviyā Roga, Maly: Chevi Rogam, Mra: Kanace Roga, Panj: Kanna De Roga, Tam: Chevinoy, Kathuvali, Tel: Cevi Rogamulu, Eng: Ear diseases

Title: Bādhirya
Sanskrit: बाधिर्य
INTRO: Vitiated Vāyu by involving the Śabda-Vaha-Srotas, causes deafness or loss of hearing and this condition is known as Bādhirya.
TREATMENT: Treatment
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Kālā, Dhumakālā, Beng: Bādhira, Dogr: Uncā Sunanā, Guj: Berā Pānu, Hind: Baharāpana, Kan: Kivudu, Maly: Poṭṭan, Mra: Bhirepaṇa, Ori: Kālā Roga, Panj: Bolāpana, Tam: Chevidu, Tel: Cevuḍu, Eng: Deafness

Title: Karṇa-Śūla
Sanskrit: कर्णशूल
INTRO: Undue concentration of vitiated Vāyu in the region of the ear causes shooting pain in the ear and this condition is known as Karṇa-Śūla.
TREATMENT: Treatment
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Bilva Tail: instil 2 to 4 drops in the affected ear twice a day. 2. Hiṅgutriguṇa Tail: instil 2 to 4 drops in the ear twice a day. 3. Karṇa Bindu Tail: Instil 2 to 4 drops in the affected ear twice a day.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Kanarā Viṣa, Beng: Karana Śūla, Dogr: Kanna Pīḍa, Guj: Kāna-Dukhāvo, Hind: Kāna Darda, Kan: Kivinovu, Maly: Chevi Vedana, Mra: Karṇa Śūla, Kāna Dhukane, Ori: Kānatanakibā, Panj: Kanna Pīḍa, Tam: Kāduvali, Tel: Cevipoṭu, Eng: Earache

Title: Karṇa-Pāka
Sanskrit: कर्णपाक
SYMPTOMS: Vitiation of Pitta causes abscess in the ear leading to pus formation and this condition is known as Karṇa-Pāka.
TREATMENT: Treatment
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Kānapāka, Beng: Karna Pāka, Dogr: Luta, Karṇapāka, Hind: Kāna Pakanā, Kan: Kivi Hunnu, Maly: Chevi Pajhuppu, Mra: Kānātun Pūyeṇe, Kāna Phūṭaṇe, Ori: Kānāre Puyā, Panj: Kanna-Pāka, Tam: Kathu Vali, Tel: Cevilo Puṇḍu, Eng: Sepsis in the ear

Title: Karṇa-Srāva
Sanskrit: कर्णस्राव
SYMPTOMS: Discharge of pus from the ear with pain is known as Karṇa-Srāva.
TREATMENT: Treatment
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Kāna Bayā, Dogr: Kannstrāva, Kapālānbegnā, Guj: Kānmāthi Payu Madvo, Hind: Kāna Bahāva/Kāna Bahanā, Kan: Kivisoroudu, Maly: Chevi Olippu, Mra: Kānātum Pani Yaṇe, Ori: Kanaru Pānī Bonibā, Panj: Kanna Vagaṇā, Kanna Bahanā, Tam: Kādukkasivu, Tel: Cevilocīmu, Eng: Otorrhoea

Title: Karṇa-Kṣveḍa
Sanskrit: कर्णक्ष्वेड
SYMPTOMS: Hearing of peculiar flute like noises by the patient in his ear is known as Karṇa-Kṣveḍa.
TREATMENT: Sarṣapa Taila (mustard oil)-2 to 4 drops to be instilled while luke warmth in the ear twice a day.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Bilvādi Taila: 2 to 4 drops to be instilled in the ear twice a day. 2. Hiṅgvādi Taila: 2 to 4 drops to be instilled in the ear twice a day. 3. Kṣāra Taila: 2 to 4 drops to be instilled in the ear twice a day.
PATHYA: Godhūma (wheat), Śāli variety of rice, seeds of Mudga (phaseolus bean) and Yava (barley), old ghee; fruit of Paṭola (a variety small cucumber) and Śigru (horse-radish) and leaf of Punarnavā (pig-weed) are the useful articles of diet for the patients suffering from the ear diseases.
APATHYA: Guru and Kapha Vardhaka Dravya are harmful for the patients of ear diseases. Incompatible items of food in diet, suppression of natural urges, excessive talking, brushing of teeth, washing of head, exercise, ice and eastern winds should be avoided. Working of the ear with stick or swab to allay irritation should be avoided.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Karṇa Sveda, Dogr: Sun-Sun Karṇā, Hind: Kāna Meṁ Sīṭī Bajanā, Karṇadhvani, Kan: Kiviyalli Śabda, Maly: Chevi Uttiydappu, Mra: Karṇa Nāda, Ori: Kānā Su Heba, Panj: Kanna Sām Saṁ Karnā, Tam: Kāḍḍu Iraichal, Tel: Dibbaḍi, Eng: Tinnitus

Title: KĀMALĀ
Sanskrit: कामला
INTRO: Kāmalā is a disease characterized by the yellow colouration of the eyes skin, nails, urine etc. It has been classified into two groups viz. Koṣṭhāśrita Kāmalā (medical jaundice) and Śākhāśrita Kāmalā (surgical jaundice).
SYMPTOMS: In addition to the yellow colouration of the eyes, skin, nails, etc., following are the specific signs and symptoms of two types of Kāmalā. Koṣṭhāśrita kāmalā (Medical Jaundice) Loss of appetite, fatigue, weakness, constipation, indigestion, nausea and passing of reddish-yellow (Raktapīta) urine are the specific signs and symptoms of Koṣṭhāśrita Kāmalā. Śākhāśrita Kāmalā (Surgical Jaundice) Pain in abdomen, loss of appetite, weakness, discomfort in right upper abdomen, marked loss of weight, distension of abdomen with rumbling noises in the intestine, yellow coloured urine and whitish stool are the specific signs and symptoms of Śākhāśrita Kāmalā (surgical jaundice).
TREATMENT: Śākhāśrita Kāmalā may require surgical treatment for which a specialist should be consulted. The treatment of Koṣṭhāśrita Kāmalā (medical jaundice) is as follow:
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Decoction prepared from the stem of Guḍūcī – 14 to 28 ml is to be taken twice a day. 2. Decoction prepared from the bark of Dāruharidrā (barberry) – 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken twice a day. 3. Powdered Triphalā 1 to 3 g. is to be taken with equal part of honey, twice a day. 4. Powdered Trikaṭu – 1 to 3 g. is to be taken with honey twice a day. 5. Make powder of purified Narasāra (ammonium chloride) – 180 mg., rhizome of Kaṭukī 120 mg. and fruit rind of Harītakī (chebulic myrobalan) – 3 g. It is to be taken with water twice a day. 6. Make powder of equal part of fruit rind of Harītakī (chebulic myrobalan), rhizome of Haridrā (turmeric) and Lauha Bhasma. Its 1 to 3 g. is to be taken with honey in sufficient quantity to make the paste, twice a day after meal. 7. Prepare decoction from the equal part of Triphalā, stem of Guḍūcī, leaf of Vāsā, rhizome of Kaṭukī, whole plant of Kirātatikta (chirata) and bark of Nimba. Its 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken with 6 to 12 g. honey, twice a day.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Ārogyavardhanī Vaṭī: 1 g. is to be taken with equal part of honey twice a day. 2. Maṇḍūra Bhasma: 1 to 3 g. is to be taken with honey twice a day. 3. Ciñcādi Lehyam: 1 to 3 g. is to be taken half and hour before meal with water, two times a day. 4. Kāmalā-Hara Rasa: 1 g. is to be taken with Takra (butter milk) three times a day.
PATHYA: Śāli variety of rice, Godhūma (wheat), seeds of Yava (barley), Āḍhakī (pigeon pea), Mudga (phaseolus bean) and Masūra (lentil); fruits of Paṭola (a variety of small cucumber) and Kadalī (banana), leaf of Punarnavā (pigweed), Mūlaka (radish) and sugarcane juice are the useful articles of diet for the patient of Kāmalā. In the initial state rest in the bed is advised.
APATHYA: Guru Dravya, ghee, fried and difficult to digest articles of food are harmful for the patient of Kāmalā. Exercise, excessive walking and anger should be avoided.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Kuhuma-Sara, Kāmalā, Beng: Kāmalā, Dogr: Parnca, Varkhana, Guj: Kāmḍo, Hind: Pīliā, Kan: Kāmāle, Arisinamandige, Maly: Manjappittam, Mra: Kāvila, Kāmiṇa, Ori: Haldiā Kāmalā, Panj: Pīliā, Tam: Kanmalai, Hanjalnoy, Tel: Pasirikalu, Kāmerlu, Eng: Jaundice

Title: KĀSA
Sanskrit: कास
INTRO: From the treatment point of view Kāsa (cough) may be divided into two groups viz. Śuṣka Kāsa (dry cough) and Ārdra Kāsa (cough with expectoration) which are being described separately. In the last chronic cough has also been dealt with.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Kāha, Beng: Kāsa, Dogr: Khaṅga, Guj: Udrasa, Khānsi, Hind: Khāṁsī, Kan: Kemmu, Maly: Cuma (Kura), Mra: Khokalā, Ori: Kāsa, Panj: Khaṅga, Tam: Irumal, Tel: Daggu, Eng: Cough

Title: Śuṣka-Kāsa
Sanskrit: शुष्क-कास
INTRO: Cough without expectoration may be called as Śuṣka kāsa.
SYMPTOMS: Dry and frequent cough, pain in the region of heart, temples, head, abdomen and sides, burning sensation or suffocation in the chest, fever, dryness in the mouth, thirst, bitter taste and hoarseness of voice are the main symptoms of Śuṣka Kāsa.
TREATMENT: Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Get Svarasa (juice) of Snuhī (a variety of cactus-milk hedge) by roasting it in the cinder and then squeezing it through a cloth. Its 7 to 14 ml. is to be taken twice a day. 2. 60 mg. powdered fruit of Pippalī (long pepper) and 120 mg. of Saindhava (rock-salt) is to be taken with hot water twice a day. 3. Make powder from the equal part of root of Śaṭī (zedoary), fruits of Karkaṭaśṛṅgī (crab’s claw) and Pippalī (long pepper), roots of Bhāraṅgī and Mustaka (motha), whole plant of Yavāsā (camel’s thorns) and Guḍa (jaggery), Its 1 to 3 g. is to be taken with Tila Taila (gingelly oil) for licking. 4. Powder of equal part of roots of Bhāraṅgī and Śaṭī (zedoary), fruits of Karkaṭaśṛṅgī (crab’s claw) and Pippalī (long pepper), Drākṣā (raisin) and Śuṇṭhī (dry ginger). Its 1 to 3 g. is to be take with Tila Taila (gingelly oil), twice a day. 5. Powder of equal part of fruit and root of Pippalī (long pepper) and Śuṇṭhī (dried ginger) – 3 to 6 g. is to be taken with 4 to 6 g. honey twice a day. 6. Powder of equal part of Śuṇṭhī (dried ginger), fruit of Karkaṭaśṛṅgī (Carb’s claw), Drākṣā (raisin), root of Śaṭī (zedoary), Śarkarā (raw sugar) and whole plant of Yavāsā (camel’s thorns) – 1 to 3 g. is to be taken with Tila Taila (gingelly oil) to make a paste, twice a day. 7. Prepare Ghṛta from the Kalka (paste) of fruit of Pippalī (long pepper) – 1 part, Ghṛta (ghee) – 4 parts, Ajādugdha (goat’s milk) – 16 parts and water 16 parts by Ghṛta Pāka method. It is to be taken in 12 to 24 g. dose twice a day. 8. Prepare Ghṛta from equal part of fruit of Marica (black pepper), Ārdraka (ginger) and Śarkarā (raw sugar) by Ghṛta Pāka method. It is to be taken in 12 to 24 g. dose twice a day.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Sitopalādi Cūrṇa: 1 to 3 g. is to be taken with 4 to 6 g. honey twice a day. 2. Karpūrādi Cūrṇa: 300 mg. to 1 g. is to be taken with equal part of sugarcandy, twice a day. 3. Bṛhat Pañca Mūla Kvātha: 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken with 0.5 g. powdered fruit of Pippalī, twice a day. 4. Candrāmṛta Rasa: 120 to 250 mg. is to be taken with honey sufficient to make a paste, twice a day. 5. Karavīrādi Yoga: 60 to 150 mg. is to be taken with honey sufficient to make a paste, twice a day. 6. Lavaṅgādi Vaṭī: 1 Vaṭī is to be sucked 4 to 6 times a day. 7. Śvāsānanda Guṭikā: 1 Vaṭī of 120 mg. is to be taken with decoction of Jīraka, one hour before meal twice a day. 8. Elādi Vaṭī: 1 Vaṭī is to be sucked 4 to 6 times a day. 9. Godantī Bhasma: 120 to 150 mg. is to be taken with equal part of honey twice a day. 10. Prāvala Bhasma: 60 to 120 mg. is to be taken with milk or 4 to 6 g. honey, twice a day. 11. Pippalyādi Rasāyana: 3 to 6 g. is to be taken before meal with 50 to 100 ml. water, twice a day. 12. Vāsāvaleha: 12 to 24 g. is to be taken twice a day. 13. Vāsā-Kaṇṭakāryāvaleha: 1 to 3 g. is to be taken with 50 ml. water, before or after meal twice a day.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Sukana Kāha, Beng: Śuṣka Kāsī, Dogr: Sukī Khaṅga, Guj: Sūkī Udrasa, Suki Khānsī, Hind: Sūkhī Khāṁsī, Kan: Ona Kemmu, Maly: Varattu Cuma, Mra: Sūkā Khokala, Kordā Khokalā, Ori: Sukhilā Khāsā, Panj: Sukī Khaṅga, Tam: Varatiu Irumal, Tel: Poḍidaggu, Eng: Dry cough

Title: Ārdra-Kāsa
Sanskrit: आर्द्रकास
INTRO: Cough with expectoration may be called as Ārdra kāsa.
SYMPTOMS: Patient of this disease in each paroxysm expectorates thick phlegm in large quantity, his mouth remains almost coated with phlegm and he feels lethargy, headache, loss of appetite and heaviness in the body.
TREATMENT: Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Trikaṭu Cūrṇa – 1 g. is to be taken with equal part of Śarkarā (raw sugar), twice a day. 2. Decoction prepared from the whole plant of Kaṇṭakārī (yellow berried nighshade) – 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken with 1 g. powdered fruit of Pippalī (long pepper), twice a day. 3.
