Decoction prepared from the equal parts of roots of Atibalā (country mallow), Kaṇṭakārī and Bṛhatī (two varieties of yellow berried night shade), leaf of Vāsā and Drākṣā (raisin) – 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken with 5 g. Śarkarā (raw sugar), twice a day. 4. Powder prepared from the equal part of Drākṣā (raisin), root of Madhuyaṣṭi (glycyrrhiza) and fruits of Kharjūra (date) and Marica (black pepper) is to be taken in 1 to 3 g. dose with 4 to 6 g. honey, twice a day.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Sitopalādi Cūrṇa: 1 to 3 g. is to be taken with 4 to 6 g. honey twice a day. 2. Tālīsādi Cūrṇa: 1 to 3 g. is to be taken with 4 to 6 g. honey twice a day. 3. Vyoṣādi vaṭī: 1 Vaṭī is to be sucked 4 to 6 times a day. 4. Khadirādi Vaṭī: 1 Vaṭī is to be sucked 4 to 6 times a day. 5. Elādi Vaṭī: 1 Vaṭī is to be sucked 4 to 6 times a day. 6. Mayūrapuccha Bhasma: 120 to 250 mg. is to be taken with 4 to 6 g. honey twice a day. 7. Amṛtaprāśāvaleha: 12 to 24 g. is to be taken twice a day. 8. Drakṣāriṣṭa: 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken with equal quantity of water after meal two times a day. 9. Cyavanaprāśa: 12 to 24 g. is to be taken twice a day.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Phūṭa, Kāha, Beng: Ārdra Kāsī, Dogr: Kaphvālī Khaṅga, Hind: Gīlī Khāṁsī, Kan: Kaphada Kemmu, Maly: Kapham Thuppunna Cuma, Mra: Kapha Khokalā, Ori: Gnadgnadia Khāsā, Panj: Gilī Khaṅg, Tam: Thondaikkaṭṭu Irumal, Kapa Irumal, Tel: Kaphamu Daggu, Eng: Cough with expectoration

Title: Jīrṇa-Kāsa
Sanskrit: जीर्णकास
INTRO: Śuṣka and Ārdra type of Kāsa (cough) if neglected tend to develop into the chronic stage known as Jīrṇa Kāsa.
TREATMENT: Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Siddha Ghṛta prepared with the decoction or Svarasa (juice) of Drākṣā (raisin or grape fruit) – 12 to 24 g. is to be taken twice a day. 2. Siddha Ghṛta prepared with the decoction of fruit pulp of Āragvadha (cassia) – 12 to 24 g. is to be taken twice a day. 3. Siddha Ghṛta prepared with the decoction of bark of Lodhra – 12 to 24 g. is to be taken twice a day. 4. Take 12 to 24 g. of fresh bark of Badara, make Kalka (paste), and fry in ghee, Add 1 g. of Saindhava (rock-salt) and take twice a day. 5. Boil fruit rind of Āmalakī (embelic myrobalan) – 1 part in milk – 4 parts, and grind, 12 to 24 ml. of the ground drug is to be taken with 12 to 24 g. of ghee twice a day. 6. Prepare Ghṛta by Ghṛta Pāka method by adding double of its weight of fruit juice of Dāḍima (pomegranate), equal parts of powdered Śuṇṭhī (dried ginger), fruit juice of Āmalakī (embelic myrobalan) and powdered Marica (black pepper) and 1/16 part of powdered fruit of Pippalī (long pepper). It is to be taken in 12 to 24 g. dose twice a day. 7. Drākṣādi Cūrṇa: 600 to 850 mg. is to be taken with honey twice a day.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Dhānvantara Guṭikā: 1 g. is to be taken three times a day with warm water. 2. Compound preparations given under Śuṣka-Kāsa and Ārdra Kāsa may also be given in the Jīrṇa Kāsa according to the condition of the patient.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Purāṇa Kapha (Yāhya Kāha), Beng: Jīrṇa Kāso, Dogr: Purānī Khaṅga, Hind: Purānī Khāṁsī, Kan: Hale Kemmu, Maly: Pajhakkam Chenna Cuma, Mra: Junāta Khokalā, Ori: Purāṇa Khāsa, Panj: Purānī Khaṅga, Tam: Nat Paṭṭa Irumal, Eng: Chronic cough

Title: Uraḥ-Kṣata
Sanskrit: उरःक्षत
INTRO: The acts like lifting the heavy load, falling from uneven height, fighting with strong man or animal, excessive indulgence in sex, taking of unnourished diet etc. may cause ulcerative lesion in the chest and this severe condition is known as Uraḥ-Kṣata.
SYMPTOMS: Acute pain in the chest, cough with expectoration having tinge of blood, fever, gradual loss of vitality, strength, complexion, appetite and digestive power, emaciation and loose motions are the main signs and symptoms of Uraḥ-Kṣata. Sometimes the patient may pass large quantity of bright red blood with a bout of cough and in the case a specialist should immediately be consulted.
TREATMENT: Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Flour of Yava (barley) – 100 g. and ghee – 100 g. boiled in 250 ml. milk is to be taken twice a day. 2. Saktu of Yava – 100g., Śarkarā (raw sugar) 50g. and honey- 50 g. is to be taken with 250ml. milk, twice a day. 3. Powders of equal part of roots of Balā (country mallow), Aśvagandhā (winter cherry), Śatāvarī (wild asparagus) and Punarnavā (pigweed) and fruit of Gambhārī – 1 to 3 g. is to be taken with 100 to 250 ml. milk twice a day. 4. Powder of equal part of flower of Madhūka (madhuca), root of Yaṣṭimadhu (glycyrrhiza) and Drākṣā (raisin) mixed with the double quantity of powder of Śuddha Lākṣā (purified lac), fruit of Karkaṭaśṛṅgī (crab’s claw), root of Śatāvarī (wild asparagus), and Vanśalocana (bamboo manna) is to be taken with 3 – 6 g. dose with 4 to 6 g. honey twice a day. 5. Dugdha (milk) Siddha with 12 to 24 g. powder of equal part of Kāśa, Kamala Keśara (lotus stamen) and Rakta Candana (red sandalwood) is to be taken with 4 to 6 gm. honey twice a day. 6. Take powdered root of Punarnavā (pig-weed) – 1 to 3 g. and Taṇḍula 24 g. boil it in the juice of Drākṣā (grapes) and 100 to 200 ml of milk. It is to be taken twice a day.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Sitopalādi cūrṇa: 1 to 3 g. is to be taken with honey twice a day. 2. Elādi Vaṭī: 1 Vaṭī is to be sucked 4 to 6 times a day. 3. Drākṣāsava: 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken twice a day after adding equal quantity of water after meal. 4. Kuṣmāṇḍāvaleha: 12 to 24 g. is to be taken with 100 to 250 ml. milk twice a day. 5. Vāsāvaleha: 12 to 24 g. is to be taken with 100 to 250 ml. milk twice a day. 6. Drākṣāriṣṭa: 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken twice a day with equal quantity of water, after meal. 7. Treatment prescribed for Rājayakṣmā may also be given to the patient of Uraḥ-kṣata.
PATHYA: Godhūma (Wheat), Mudga (phaseoles bean), Śāli variety of rice, Yava (barley seeds), goat’s milk, cow’s milk, ghee; meat soup prepared from the meat of goat or deer; Drākṣā (raisin or grape) and fruit rind of Āmalakī (embelic myrobalen) are the useful articles of diet for the patients of Kāsa and Uraḥ-Kṣata.
APATHYA: Fruits of Bilva (bael), Vārtākī (brinjal), Kāravellaka (bitter gourd), Rājikā (red mustard) food prepared in oil are harmful for the patient of Kāsa and Uraḥ-Kṣata. Sexual intercourse, day sleep and anger should also be avoided.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Haofao Kṣata, Bakṣa Kṣata, Beng: Urakṣata, Bakṣa Kṣata, Dogr: Kālnāḍi, Guj: Chatino Dukhāvo, Hind: Chātī Me Ghāva, Maly: Svāsakoṣa Chathavu, Mra: Chātītīla Jakhama, Panj: Lahū Dī Ultī, Tam: Irumi Raktamṭhuputhal, Eng: Bleeding from lungs, haemoptysis

Title: KAṆṬHA EVAṀ GALAROGA
Sanskrit: कण्ठ एवं गलरोग
INTRO: The signs, symptoms and treatment of the common diseases of the throat are being described here separately.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Kaṇṭha, Bemāra, Galāra, Bemāra, Beng: Kaṇṭha Roga, Gala Roga, Dogr: Galeā De Roga, Saṅgapainā, Hind: Gale Ke Roga, Kan: Gantālu Maṭṭu Kuṭṭige Roga, Maly: Thondayilum Kajhuthilumulla Rogam, Mra: Kaṇṭha Roga; Galyāce Roga, Tam: Tondainoy, Tel: Gontu Rogamulu, Eng: Diseases of throat

Title: Svara-Bheda
Sanskrit: स्वरभेद
INTRO: The disease in which the voice become hoarse, is known as Svara-Bheda.
SYMPTOMS: Hoarseness of voice, burning sensation in the throat, less and slow talking are the main symptoms of Svara-Bheda.
TREATMENT: Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Ghana-satva prepared from the root of Yaṣṭimadhu 250 to 500 mg. is to be sucked, thrice a day. 2. The powdered root of Yaṣṭimadhu (giycyrrhiza) – 3 g. boiled in 250 ml. milk is to be taken twice a day. 3. Powder of Marica (black pepper) fried in ghee – 1 to 3 g. is to be taken with 5 to 10 g. Śarkarā (raw sugar), twice a day. 4. Prepare of Kalka (paste) of equal parts of bark of Badara (jujube) and Saindhava (rock salt). Its 3 g. is to be fried in ghee and taken with 4 to 6 g. honey, twice a day. 5. Boil Tanḍula (rice) – 1 part with 1 part of Guḍa (jaggery) in 4 parts of water, when cooked take with ghee – 1 part, twice a day. The quantity of rice may be taken according to the appetite of the patient.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Sitopalādi cūrṇa: 3 to 6 g. is to be taken with 4 to 6 g. honey or 5 to 10 g. ghee twice a day 2. Khadirādi Vaṭī: 1 Vaṭī is to be sucked 4 to 6 times a day.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Maṭa Bhaṅgā, Beng: Svarabhaṅga, Dogr: Gela Baḍhana, Guj: Sadbesijavo, Gadubesijavo, Hind: Galā Baiṭhanā, Kan: Dhvani Bīluvuḍā, Maly: Ochayaṭappu, Mra: Āvāja Phuṭane; Āvāja Basṇe, Ori: Tānti Basijibā, Panj: Galā Baiṭhanā, Tam: Kural Kammal, Tel: Bonguru, Eng: Hoarseness

Title: Gilāyu
Sanskrit: गलायु
INTRO: In the throat there is a small, round, mass of tissue known as tonsil. Its inflammation is known as Galāyu (tonsillitis).
SYMPTOMS: Pain in the throat and difficulty in deglutition are the main symptoms of Galāyu (tonsillitis).
TREATMENT: In case of continued high fever and acute sepsis refer to a specialist. 1. Make a concentrated solution of Yavakṣāra or common salt in warm water and gargle with it many times a day. 2. Make a solution with 600 mg. of Sphaṭika (alum) in 100 ml. warm water and gargle with it many times a day. 3. Hot Lepa (poultice) of horse-chestnut to be applied on the front portion of the neck. Treatment prescribed for Svara-Bheda may also be used beneficially for the patient of Galāyu.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Gilāyu, Dogr: Galeā Phulanā, Guj: Kākara Vaḍhvo, Hind: Galatuṇḍikā Śotha, Kan: Ganṭālu Novu, Maly: Tonḍa Vikam, Tonḍa Mullu, Mra: Galyācā Roga, Panj: Gale Dī Graṇthī Vaḍhanā, Tam: Lasunā Bitham, Annaku Thūrā Vikkam, Tel: Angiṭimullu, Eng: Tonsillitis

Title: Adhijihvikā
Sanskrit: अधिजिह्विका
INTRO: A tense reddish swelling of uvula (Adhijihvā) which is of the shape of tongue tip situated at the root of the tongue is known as Adhijihvikā. If other part of the throat are affected or pus is formed contact a specialist.
TREATMENT: Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Take a Kavala (mouth wash) with the decoction of fruit rind of Harītakī (chebulic myrobalan) – 3 g. Marica (black pepper) – 1 g. and Śuddha Gairika (purified ochre) – 1 g. It is to be retained in the mouth for one minute and to be repeated 3 to 4 times a day.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Kālaka Cūrṇa: 1 to 3 g. is to be taken with 4 to 6 g. honey twice a day.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Gala Śotha, Beng: Ala Jiba, Dogr: Due Jivi, Guj: Modhū Avaūṅ, Hind: Kākalaka Śotha, Kan: Kirunaligeutha, Maly: Lālānali Śopham, Mra: Jibhevara Jībhayaṇe, Paḍajībavaḍhaṇe, Ori: Gnata Ka Baḍhiba, Panj: Kāṁ Vadhaṇā, Tam: Annaku Valarchi, Eng: Uvulitis

Title: Galaugha
Sanskrit: गलौघ
INTRO: Galaugha is a highly inflamed condition of the throat characterized by obstruction to the passage of food and water, high fever and difficulty in breathing. In this condition if the patient exhibits the symptoms of toxemia, refer to the specialist.
TREATMENT: Treatment prescribed for Galāyu and Svara-Bheda may also be given to the patient of Galaugha.
PATHYA: Seeds of Yava (barley), Mudga (phasecolus bean) and Kulattha (dolichos bean); fruits of Kāravellaka (bitter-gourd) and Paṭola (a variety of small cucumber); seed of Methika (fenugreek) and leaf of Tambūla (betel) are the useful articles of diet for the patient suffering from the diseases of the throat.
APATHYA: Rūkṣa, Guru and Amla Dravya; milk, curd and Guḍa (jaggery) are harmful for the patients of throat diseases. Day sleep, tooth brushing and bath should be avoided during the illness.
REGIONAL NAMES: Beng: Galaguha, Hind: Tīvra Galaśotha, Kan: Gantaluri, Mra: Galyācā roga, Ori: Gnantaka Bāḍhibā, Tam: Kandhamalai; Thondai Vīkkam, Eng: Tumour in the throat

Title: KṚMI-ROGA
Sanskrit: कृमि-रोग
INTRO: Kṛmi Roga is a disease caused by the presence of worms (Kṛmi) in the body particularly in the intestines.
SYMPTOMS: Loss of appetite, loose motions, pain in the abdomen, fever, discoloration of the skin or tongue, lassitude and giddiness are the general signs and symptoms of Kṛmi Roga.
TREATMENT: Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Powder of equal part of seed of Viḍaṅga, Saindhava (rock-salt), Yavakṣāra, Raja of fruit of Kampillaka (kamala dust) and fruit rind of Harītakī (chebulic myrobalan) – 1 to 3 g. is to be taken with Takra (butter milk) twice a day. 2. Powder of equal part of seeds of Palāśa (forest flame) and Pārasīka Yavānī (henbane), Indrayava (kurchi seeds), Avalguja (Somarājī), Kṛṣṇa Lavaṇa, Śuddha Gandhaka (sulpher) and fruit rind of Harītakī (chebulic myrobalan) – 3 to 6 g. is to be taken with Cūrṇodaka (lime water) twice a day. 3. Brew leaves of Kharjūra (date) in the decoction of leaves of Kharjūra (date) for over night, strain next morning and take 14 to 28 ml. with 7 to 14 g. honey twice a day. 4. Decoction prepared from rhizome of Kaṭukī – 3 g., bark of Dāḍima (pomegranate) – 6 g. tuber of Vidārī (giant potato) – 6 g. leaf of Apāmārga (prickly chaff) – 6 g. and Tvak – Dālacīnī (cinnamon bark) – 3 g. is to be taken in 14 to 28 ml. dose with 4 to 5 drops of Sarala Niryāsa Taila (turpentine oil) twice a day.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Somarājyādi Cūrṇa: 3 to 6 g. is to be taken with 50 ml. water twice a day. 2. Viḍaṅgādi Cūrṇa: 1 g. is to be taken with honey in sufficient quantity to make a paste twice a day. 3. Kṛmimudgara Rasa: 1 to 2 Vaṭī is to be taken with 50 ml. water twice a day. 4. Kṛmi-Kuṭhāra Rasa: 1 to 2 pills is to be taken with 50 ml. water twice a day. 5. Viḍaṅgāāriṣṭa: 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken with equal quantity of water after meal.
PATHYA: Tikta Dravya, Śāli variety of rice; Uṣṭradugdha (camel’s milk), Gomūtra (cow’s urine); Hiṅgu (asafoetida); fruit of Kāravellaka (bitter gourd), leaves of Śigru (horse radish) and Vāstūka (a variety of chenopodium), fruit of Yavānī (ptychotis), seed of Sarṣapa (mustard) and fruits of Kadalī (banana) and Tāla (Palmyra) are the useful articles of diet for the patient of Kṛmi-Roga.
APATHYA: Madhura Rasa Pradhāna and Piṣṭamaya Dravya, Māṣa (black phaseolus bean), incompatible items of food, curd and milk are harmful for the patient of Kṛmi-Roga. Day sleep and excessive food should be avoided.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Kṛmi, Beng: Kṛmi, Dogr: Krani, Kiḍā, Guj: Kiramīya Jivara, Hind: Peṭa Ke Kīḍe, Kan: Hulu, Krimi, Maly: Kṛmi, Mra: Janta, Ori: Kurumi, Panj: Peṭa De Kīde, Tam: Kiruni, Kudār Kirumigala, Tel: Vemiḍikalu, Eng: Worm infestation

Title: KUṢṬHA
Sanskrit: कुष्ठ
INTRO: Kuṣṭha (leprosy) is a chronic infectious disease which produces various granulomatous lesions in the skin, the mucous membrane, and the peripheral nervous system.
SYMPTOMS: Excessive smoothness or roughness and discoouration of skin, excessive or absence of sweat, pain like needling, burning sensation, itching, numbness, patches with loss of sensation, increase in the size of wound inspite of treatment, fatigue and exhaustion are the prodromal symptoms of Kuṣṭha.
TREATMENT: Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Decoction of bark of Khadira (khair) is to be taken in 14 to 28 ml. dose twice a day. 2. Use of Khadira (khair) for preparing food, drinks, and water for bath. 3. Pañca-Nimba-Tvak Cūrṇa – 1 to 3 g. is to be taken with water twice a day. 4. Gomūtra Siddha fruit rind of Harītakī (chebulic myrobalan) – 3 to 6 g. Is to be taken twice a day. 5. Khadira Sāra (catechu) – 1 to 3 g. is to be taken with the Svarasa (juice) of fresh leaf of Nimba – 14 to 28 ml. twice a day. 6. Khadira Sār (catechu) – 1 g. and powdered Seed of Bākucī - 1 g. is to be taken with Svarasa (juice) of fresh leaf of Nimba- 14 to 28 ml., twice a day.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Triphalā Cūrṇa: 3 to 6 g. is to be taken with juice of fresh leaf of Nimba – 14 to 28 ml. twice a day. 2. Laghu Mañjiṣṭhādi Kvātha: 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken with the powdered root-bark of Trivṛt (Indian turpeth)- 1 g., twice a day. 3. Bṛhad Mañjiṣṭhādi Kvātha: 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken twice a day. 4. Rasa Māṇikya: 30 to 120 mg., is to be taken with 1 g. powdered seed of Bākucī, thrice a day (with caution). 5. Ārogyavardhanī vaṭī: 1 g. is to be taken with 50 ml. warm water twice a day. 6. Pañcatikta Ghṛta: 14 to 28 g. is to be taken twice a day. 7. Pañcatikta Ghṛta Guggulu: 14 to 28 g. is to be taken twice a day. 8. Khadirāriṣṭha: 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken with equal quantity of water twice a day after meal.
PATHYA: Tikta Dravya, Purāṇa Yava (old oat), Godhūma (wheat). Śāli ( a variety of rice), seeds of Mudga (phaseolus bean), Āḍhakī (pegion pea) and Masūra (Lentil); old ghee, Sarṣapa Taila (Mustered oil), Tila Taila (gingelly oil), Nimba Taila (neem oil), Hingota Taila, Aguru Taila; urine of cow, camel, ass and buffalow; Mṛgamada (Kastūri, musk); fruits of Karkaṭa (cucumber), Trapuśa (a variety of cucumber) and Paṭola (fruit of a variety of small cucumber- snake gourd); Vetas Śuga (cane shoot), fruit and leaf of Kākamācī, leaf of Karañja (indian bīc); bulb of Rasona (garlic); Nāgakeśara, Keśara (saffron), and fruit of Tāla (palmyra) are the useful articles of diet for the patient of Kuṣṭha.
APATHYA: Amla and Guru Dravya; Navīna Anna (freshly harvested grains); Māṣa (black phaseolus bean); Mūlaka (radish); Taila (oil), milk, curd; products of sugarcane, Guḍa (jaggery); incompatible items of food, Madya (wine) are harmful for the patient of Kuṣṭha. Salt restricted diet should be given to the patient. Movement in sun, irregular food habits, suppression of call of nature, day sleep, sexual intercourse should be avoided. Svedana is contraindicated for the patient of Kuṣṭha.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Kuṣṭha Roga, Beng: Kuṣṭha, Dogr: Koḍa, Guj: Galita Koṭha, Ragata Pitta, Hind: Koḍha, Kan: Kuṣṭha, Maly: Kuṣṭham, Mra: Cāmaḍīcā Roga, Mahā Roga, Ori: Baḍaroga, Panj: Koḍha, Tam: Perunoy, Tojhunoy, Tel: Kuṣṭham, Eng: Leprosy

Title: GALAGAṆḌA, GAṆḌAMĀLĀ EVAṀ APACĪ
Sanskrit: गलगण्ड, गण्डमाला एवं अपची
INTRO: Appearance of a big or small, defined, glandular swelling which hangs like scrotum in the neck due to enlargement of thyroid gland is known as Galagaṇḍa. This painless swelling increases very slowly and does not suppurate.
TREATMENT: Treatment
PATHYA: Seeds of Yava (oat) and Mudga (phaseolus bean), leaf of Paṭola (a variety of small cucumber), Kaṭu and Rūkṣa Dravya are the useful articles of diet for the patient of Galagaṇḍa, Patient should be put on sea salt.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Galagaṇḍa, Beng: Galagaṇḍa, Dogr: Gilhara Dirāna, Hind: Gheṅgā, Kan: Galaganda, Mra: Galayācā Ṭhikānī, Panj: Galagaṇḍa, Tam: Kaṇḍa Malai, Eng: Goitre

Title: Gaṇḍamālā Evaṁ Apacī
Sanskrit: गण्डमाला एवं अपची
INTRO: Gaṇḍamālā is a disease in which numerous glands of the size of jujube (Karkandhu) appear in axilla, back sides of neck and groin, which suppurate slowly. The chronic stage of this disease is termed as Apacī in which pus discharge occurs from the glands.
TREATMENT: Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Dissolve Bhasma of whole plant of Jalakumbhī in 7 times of its weight of Gomūtra and filter 21 times. Its 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken thrice a day.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Madhusnuhī Rasāyana: 1 to 3 g., to be taken with water one hour before meal. 2. Kāñcanāra Guggulu: 2 to 4 Vaṭī, to be taken with warm water thrice a day.
PATHYA: Seed of Kodrava (a type of cereal), old Śāli variety of rice, seeds of Yava (oat) and Mudga (phaseolus bean); fruit of Paṭola (a variety of small cucumber), leaf and fruit of Śigru (horse-radish) and fruit of Kāravellaka (bitter gourd) are the useful articles of diet for the patients of Gaṇḍamālā and Apacī.
APATHYA: Guru, Madhura and Amla Dravya, Māṣa (black phaseolus bean), sugarcane and milk products, potato, meat of amphibious animals are harmful for the patients of Gaṇḍamālā and Apacī.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Gaṇḍamālā, Śrābi Gaṇḍamālā, Beng: Gaṇḍamālā, Apacī, Guj: Kaṇṭhamālā, Hind: Kaṇṭhamālā, Kan: Gaṇḍamālā, Maly: Kaṇṭhamālā, Mra: Sūja Gaṇḍamālā, Panj: Kaṇṭhamālā, Eng: Scrofula, Chronic lymphadenitis

Title: GULMA
Sanskrit: गुल्म
INTRO: Gulma is a condition in which a round, motile or non-motile swelling like a gland appears in the abdomen and it changes its size from time to time.
SYMPTOMS: Loss of appetite, difficulty in passing stool, urine and flatus, rumbling noise in the intestine, distension of abdomen and excessive eructations are the general signs and symptoms of Gulma.
TREATMENT: Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Bṛhat Pañcamūla Kvātha: 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken thrice a day. 2. Mix powder of Śuṇṭhī (dried ginger) – 2 g., decorticated Kṛṣṇa Tila (black seasame) – 8 g. and Guḍa (jaggery) – 4 g. with 250 ml. warm milk. It is to be taken twice a day. 3. Take equal part of juices of Bījapūra (lemon) and fruit of Dāḍima (pomegranate) – 14 to 28 ml. and add to it 1 g. each of Saindhava (rock salt), Kṛṣṇa Lavaṇa and Ghṛta Bhṛṣṭa Hiṅgu. It is to be taken twice a day. 4. Mix the powder of Yavānī – 1 to 3 g. and Viḍa Lavaṇa – 1 to 2 g. in 250 ml. of Takra (butter milk). It is to be taken two times a day.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Vijayā Cūrṇa: 1 to 3 g. is to be taken with 50 ml. warm water thrice a day. 2. Drākṣā Ghṛta: 6 to 12 g. is to be taken with 50 ml. warm water twice a day. 3. Yavakṣāra: 1 to 2 g. is to be taken as such or with 14 to 28 ml. Eraṇḍa Taila (castor Oil) or 14 to 28 ml. Tila Taila (sesame oil) thrice a day. 4. Kāṅkāyana Vaṭī: 2 to 4 Vaṭī, to be taken with 50 to 100 ml. warm water thrice a day. 5. Rasonādi Vaṭī: 2 to 4 Vaṭī, to be taken with 50 ml. warm water thrice a day. 6. Sukumāra Ghṛta: 12 to 48 g. is to be taken one hour before food or at bed time once a day. 7. Kṣīra-Śaṭpala Ghṛta: 12 to 24 g. is to be taken with 50 ml. warm water thrice a day. 8. Indukānta Ghṛta: 12 to 24 g. is to be taken with 50 ml. warm water and 300 to 600 mg. Yavakṣāra, thrice a day.
PATHYA: Śāli (red variety of rice), Kulattha (dolichos bean); milk of cow and goat; leaf of Vāstūka (a variety of chenopodium-white goosefoot), Drākṣā (raisin or grape fruit), fruit rind of Āmalakī, fruit of Kharjūra (date) and Parūṣaka (Asiatic grewia), bulb of Rasona (garlic) are the useful articles of diet for the patient of Gulma.
APATHYA: Madhura Rasa Dravya, Māṣa (black phaseolus bean), Śāka (vegetables), potato, Śuṣka Māṁsa (dried meat), Matsya (fish) are harmful for the patient of Gulma.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Gulma, Temuna, Beng: Gulma, Dogr: Balgolā, Golā, Guj: Gorothaban, Goo, Hind: Vāyugolā, Kan: Hoṭṭegadde, Maly: Gunmam, Mra: Golā, Ori: Peṭārugotā Uthibā, Panj: Vā-Golā, Tam: Gunmak Katti, Eng: Localised abdominal tumour or swelling

Title: GRAHAṆĪ-ROGA
Sanskrit: ग्रहणी-रोग
INTRO: Grahaṇī is a disease in which patient is unable to digest his food properly and passes it out frequently through motions in the undigested or digested form with foul smell. The consistency of the stool changes frequently i.e. sometimes it is loose and some time it is formed.
SYMPTOMS: In this condition, the patient passes sometimes loose and sometimes formed motions. Other symptoms are flatulence, loss of weight and energy, indigestion, depression, chaffing of skin, dryness of throat and mouth, thirst, ringing in the ear, and aversion to sexual intercourse.
TREATMENT: Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Powder of equal part of rhizome of Kaṭukī, Śuṇṭhī (dried ginger), Rasāñjana, flower of Dhātakī, Indrayava (kurchi seed), root of Mustaka (motha), bark of Kuṭaja (kurchi), rhizome of Haridrā (turmeric) and root of Ativiṣā (Indian atees) – 1 to 3 g. is to be taken with Takra (butter milk) thrice a day. 2. Powder of equal part of Hiṅgu (asafoetida), root of Ativiṣā (Indian atees), rhizome of Vacā (sweet flag). Sauvarcala Lavaṇa, fruit rind of Harītakī (chebulic myrobalan) – 1 to 3 g. is to be taken with warm water or 50 ml. Takra (butter milk) thrice a day. 3. Make powder of Marica (black pepper) – 1 part, Śuṇṭhī (dried ginger) – 2 parts, bark of Kuṭaja (kurchi) – 4 parts and take it in 1 to 3 g. dose with equal part of Guḍa (jaggery) and 50 to 100 ml. Takra (butter milk) thrice a day. 4. Make powder from one part each of Śuṇṭhī (dried ginger), seeds of Dhānyaka (coriander) and Methika (fenugreek), Bhṛṣṭa epicarp of Dādima (pomegranate), Saṅkha Bhasma, Kṛṣṇa Lavaṇa and fruits of Miśreyā (fennel), half part of Śuddha Hiṅgu (asafoetida) and 2 parts of leaves of Bhaṅga (Indian hemp). Its 1 to 3 g. is to be taken with 50 to 100 ml. Takra (butter milk) twice a day. 5. Powder of equal part of Indrayava (kurchi seed), root of Ativiṣā (Indian atees), Śuddha Hiṅgu (asafoetida), Sauvarcala Lavaṇa, fruit rind of Harītakī (chebulic myrobalan) is to be taken in 1 to 3 g. dose with warm water thrice a day. 6. Pañcakola Siddha Jala – 50 to 100 ml. is to b taken thrice a day. 7. Decoction of equal part of Śuṇṭhī (dried ginger), root of Mustaka (motha) and Ativiṣā (Indian atees) – 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken thrice a day. 8. Decoction of equal part of Śuṇṭhī (dried ginger), roots of Mustaka (motha) and Ativiṣā (Indian atees) and stem of Guḍūcī 0 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken thrice a day. 9. Yavāgu (gruel) prepared from rice along with juice of leaf of Cāṅgerī (wood sorrel) 7 to 14 ml. is to be taken thrice a day.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Bṛhat Gaṅgādhara Cūrṇa: 1 to 3 g. is to be taken with warm water thrice a day. 2. Dāḍimāṣṭaka Cūrṇa: 1 to 3 g. is to be taken with water thrice a day. 3. Hiṅgvāṣṭaka Cūrṇa: 1 to 3 g. is to be taken with 50 to 100 ml. Takra (butter milk) thrice a day). 4. Jātiphalādi Cūrṇa: 1 to 3 g. is to be taken with water thrice a day. 5. Kapithāṣṭaka Cūrṇa: 600 mg. to 1.25 g. is to be taken with 50 to 100 ml. Takra (butter milk) thrice a day. 6. Lavaṇa Bhāskara Cūrṇa: 1 to 3 g. is to be taken with 50 to 100 ml. Takra (butter milk) twice a day. 7. Nṛpati-Ballabha Rasa: 1 to 2 Vaṭī, to be taken with 50 to 100 ml. Takra (butter milk), thrice a day. 8. Piyūṣavallī Rasa: 1 to 2 Vaṭī, to be taken with water or 50 to 100 ml. Takra (butter milk) thrice a day. 9. Mahā-Gandhaka Yoga: 360 to 750 mg. is to be taken with honey sufficient to make a paste thrice a day. 10. Kāmesvara Modaka: 6 to 13 g. is to be taken with 100 to 120 ml. milk thrice a day. 11. Bilvādi Lehyama: 3 to 6 g. to be taken half an hour before meal with 3 to 6 g. butter thrice a day. 12. Pañcāmṛta Parpaṭī: 120 to 360 mg. is to be taken with sufficient honey to make a paste thrice a day. 13. Rasa-Parpaṭī: 120 to 360 mg. is to be taken with sufficient honey to make a paste thrice a day. 14. Svarṇa Parpaṭī: 60 to 360 mg. is to be taken with sufficient honey to make a paste thrice a day. Note: Parpaṭī Kalpa may only be taken under the guidance of a specialist.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Grahaṇī, Beng: Grahaṇī, Dogr: Saṅgraṇī, Guj: Saṅgraṇī, Hind: Apāvaśōṣaṇa, Kan: Grahaṇī, Maly: Grahaṇī, Mra: Grahaṇī, Ori: Laī Jhāḍā, Panj: Saṅgarahaṇī, Tam: Kirani, Eng: Sprue, malabsorption syndrome

Title: Parvatīya Atisāra
Sanskrit: पर्वतीय अतिसार
INTRO: Visitors to hill stations suffer from a malady where in symptoms of Grahaṇī or Atisāra are exhibited.
TREATMENT: Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Śuddha Gairika (ochre) – 250 to 500 mg. to be taken with sufficient honey to make a paste thrice a day. 2. Cut Nimbū (lemon) into two halves, sprinkle Bhṛṣṭa (fried) fruit powder of Jīraka (cumin) and common salt – 1 g. Its juice to be sucked after warming the Nimbū (lemon). The use of boiled water and Takra (butter milk) in diet are useful. If symptoms persist medicines indicated for Grahaṇī or Atisāra may be taken according to the condition of the patient.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Pānātīya Atisāra, Beng: Parvatīya Atisāra, Hind: Parvatīya Atisāra, Mra: Parvatīya Atisāra, Tam: Maladi Bedhi, Eng: Hill diarrhea

Title: Āntra-Kṣaya
Sanskrit: आन्त्रक्षय
INTRO: Āntra-Kṣaya is a disease in which patient passes extremely mucoid stools of liquid consistency with pain and sounds, particularly in the day time.
SYMPTOMS: This disease comes in attacks at the interval of a month, fortnight or ten days during which patient passes loose motions. In between the attack patient suffers from constipation. The symptoms are generally relieved in the night. Its other symptoms are rumbling sound in the intestine, lassitude, asthenia, indigestion and pain in lumber region. This disease is difficult to cure and requires the treatment for longer duration.
TREATMENT: Treatment
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Prāvala-Pañcāmṛta: 120 to 250 mg. is to be taken with sufficient honey to make a paste thrice a day. 2. Svarṇa-Parpaṭī: 60 to 120 mg. is to be taken with sufficient honey to make a paste thrice a day. The medicines prescribed under Grahāṇī and Rāja-Yakṣmā are also useful for the patient of Āntrakṣaya.
PATHYA: Boiled water should only be taken for the drinking purposes. Purāṇa Śāli (old red rice), Vilepi (gruel) prepared from Mudga (phaseolus bean) and rice, soup of Masūra (lentil); cow’s milk, Takra (butter milk), curd and butter; flower and fruit of Kadalī (plantain), fruit rind of Harītakī (chebulic myrobalan), Jambīra (lemon), fruits of Kapittha (wood apple), Bilva (bael) and Dādima (pomegranate), stem of Kamala (lotus) are the useful articles of diet for the patients of Grahaṇī, Parvatīya Atisāra and Āntra-kṣaya.
APATHYA: Guru and Snighdha Āhāra and chillies are harmful for the patient of Grahāṇī. Excessive intake of water, bath and exercise should be avoided.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Nāri Kṣaya, Beng: Āntrakṣaya, Dogr: Āntīya Granthika, Hind: Ānta Kā Tapedika, Maly: Kuṭalu Kṣyayam, Mra: Āntra Kṣaya, Antadyātīl Kṣaya, Panj: Peṭa Dā Tapadika, Tam: Kadar Vyurukkinoy, Eng: Intestinal tuberculosis

Title: CARMA-ROGA
Sanskrit: चर्मरोग
INTRO: The signs, symptoms and treatment of the common skin diseases (Carma-Roga) are as follows.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Chālāra Bemāra, Beng: Carmaroga, Dogr: Camae Ke Roga, Guj: Camā Nā Roga, Hind: Carmaroga, Kan: Carmaroga, Maly: Tvak Rogam, Mra: Carmaroga, Kātadice Roga, Panj: Camaī De Roga, Tam: Carumanoy, Tel: Carmarogamulu, Eng: Diseases of the skin

Title: Pāmā Evaṁ Kacchū
Sanskrit: पामा एवं कच्छू
SYMPTOMS: Pāmā is a disease characterized by appearance of numerous pimples with discharge, itching and burning sensation particularly between fingers, on the ulnar border of the hand, thighs, buttocks etc. If there is severe burning sensation in the vesicles, particularly of hands and buttocks then this condition is known as Kacchū.
TREATMENT: Treatment
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Mahā Mañjiṣṭhādi Kvātha: 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken three times a day. 2. Gandhaka Rasāyana: 120 to 250 mg. is to be taken with 4 to 6 g. honey or Ghṛta (ghee) three times a day.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Khahu, Samariya, Beng: Pāmā Chulkana, Dogr: Kanda, Kuraka, Guj: Khasa, Hind: Khāja, Khujalī, Kan: Kajjī, Maly: Cori, Mra: Kharūja, Ori: Kachu, Panj: Khuraka, Tam: Sori, Sirangu, Tel: Gajji, Durada, Eng: Scabies

Title: Vicarcikā
Sanskrit: विचर्चिका
SYMPTOMS: Appearance of dark or dark brown coloured vesicles on the skin in the group form with itching and excessive discharge is known as Vicarcikā.
TREATMENT: Treatment
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Becu, Beng: Birarcikā, Dogr: Viyānā Paanā, Guj: Kharajauṅ, Hind: Khujalī, Kan: Isubu, Maly: Vātapunnu, Mra: Bicarcikā, Ori: Bineī, Tam: Themal, Tel: Gajji, Eng: Dry and weeping eczema

Title: Arūṁṣikā
Sanskrit: अरूंषिका
INTRO: Weeping or greasy scabs having multiple channels develop in the scalp due to the infestation of lice, vitiation of Rakta etc. and this condition is known as Arūṁṣikā.
TREATMENT: Treatment
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Yāhyāvaraṇa, Beng: Arūṁṣikā, Dogr: Sāru, Guj: Phodhakonikalnūṅ, Hind: Phunsī, Kan: Talle Hunnu, Talle Kove, Maly: Vātapunnu, Mra: Arūṁṣikā, Khāvade, Ori: Badagna, Panj: Śira De Phode, Tam: Padar Thamari, Eng: Furunculosis

Title: Yuvāna-Piḍakā
Sanskrit: युवानपिडका
SYMPTOMS: Appearance of nodules looking like the thorns of Śālmalī (red silk cotton tree) on the face of young people is known as Yuvānapidakā.
TREATMENT: Treatment
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Salamana, Beng: Bāhijā Phorā, Dogr: Muhāsika, Guj: Khīla, Hind: Muhāsā, Kan: Modave, Maly: Mukhakkuru, Mra: Tāruṇyapītikā, Murum, Ori: Vayas Vraṇa, Panj: Kila, Tam: Mugapparu, Tel: Moṭimalu, Eng: Acne

Title: Dadru
Sanskrit: दद्रु
SYMPTOMS: Appearance of copper coloured, elevated pimples in a circular or ring form on the skin with itching is known as Dadru.
TREATMENT: Treatment
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Khāra, Beng: Dadru, Dāda, Dogr: Dādri, Guj: Dādra, Dāda, Hind: Dāda, Kan: Tadu, Daddu, Maly: Vattattatippu, Mra: Nāyaṭā, Gaj karṇa, Ori: Tadu, Panj: Dāda, Tam: Padai, Ecchil Thajanbhn, Eng: Ringworm

Title: Pādadārī
Sanskrit: पाददारी
SYMPTOMS: Due to excessive walking or dryness caused by Vāyu, the painful fissures appear in the sides of the sole and base of the toes and this condition is known as Pādadārī.
TREATMENT: Treatment
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Bhārīphāṭa, Beng: Pādadārī, Dogr: Peḍḍhā, Guj: Pāgphaṭvā, Hind: Khāmara, Bivāī, Maly: Kalvetichuka, Mra: Pādadārī, Talpāya Phāṭane, Ori: Godaphātā, Panj: Biyāī, Tam: Pitta Vedappu, Kalvedappu, Tel: Kāllupaguluṭa, Eng: Chaffed soles

Title: Ahipūtanā
Sanskrit: अहिपूतना
SYMPTOMS: Due to uncleanliness itching occurs around the anus of babies which may lead to formation of rashes or weeping pimples with itching and this condition is known as Ahipūtanā.
TREATMENT: Care should be taken to ensure cleaning and change of napkins promptly as and when required.
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Ghṛta Siddha with equal part of seed of Latākarañja (bonduc nut), Triphalā and fruit of Paṭola (a variety of small gourd) – 1 to 3 g. is to be taken three times a day.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Guda Khajuyāti, Beng: Gudakacchū, Dogr: Pūtanā, Hind: Cūnā Laganā, Lālī Padanā, Kan: Guda Drāra, Seleyurualu, Maly: Kuttikalkku Gudathilu (Varunna Vranam), Mra: Gudakacchu, Ori: Jakusi, Tam: Asannavayppadai, Eng: Erythema, napkin rash, sour buttocks

Title: Vṛṣaṇa-Kacchū
Sanskrit: वृषणकच्छू
INTRO: Due to the uncleanliness and wetness of scrotum, itching occurs which may lead to formation of pimples with discharge and this condition is known as Vṛṣaṇa Kacchū.
TREATMENT: Absolute cleanliness of the part is necessary.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Juli Khajūyatī, Beng: Vṛṣaṇa Kachū, Kan: Andaturike, Mra: Vṛsana Kachū, Ori: Ghaumdata, Tam: Virayl Padai, Eng: Eczema of the scrotum

Title: Cippa Evaṁ Kunakha
Sanskrit: चिप्प एवं कुनख
INTRO: 1. Cippa: It is the acute inflammation of the nail bed in which suppuration occurs in the nail bed accompanied by burning sensation and pain. 2. Kunakha: If the inflammation around the nail bed is of mild nature, then it causes fragility of the nail and this condition is known as Kunakha.
TREATMENT: Treatment
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Bṛhat Mañjiṣṭhādi Kvātha: 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken three times a day. 2. Khadirāriṣṭa: 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken with equal quantity of water twice a day after meal. 3. Sārivādayāsava: 11 to 28 ml. is to be taken with equal quantity of water twice a day after meal. 4. Ārogyavardhinī Vaṭī: 250 to 500 mg. is to be taken with 4 to 6 g. honey twice a day.
REGIONAL NAMES:

Title: CHARDI
Sanskrit: छर्दि
INTRO: Vomiting may proceed with the symptoms like water-brash, nausea, loss of appetite, salty taste and suppression of eructation. It has been classified according to the cause into 5 groups viz. Vātaja, Pittaja, Kaphaja, Tridoṣaja and Āgantuja.
SYMPTOMS: 1. Vātīka Chardi: In this disease patient vomits out small quantity of Kaṣāya, frothy and thin material with difficulty though the act is urgent. Other accompanied symptoms are headache, pain in the heart and umbilical regions, cough, hoarsness of voice and noisy eructation. 2. Paittika Chardi: In this condition patient vomits out yellowish, greenish or smoke coloured material having bitter taste with burning sensation. Other symptoms include thirst, dryness of mouth, giddiness and fainting. 3. Kaphaja Chardi: In this type of Chardi patient vomits out greasy, thick and whitish coloured material having sweet taste without any difficulty. Other symptoms are water-brash, loss of appetite, torpor, and feeling of sleep and heaviness in the body. 4. Tridoṣaja Chardi: in this condition patient vomits out thick and blue coloured material or saline of acidic taste with blood, Colic pain, loss of appetite, indigestion, burning sensation, thirst, dyspnoea and fainting are the other accompanied symptoms. 5. Āgantuja Chardi: Vomiting caused by the unpleasant site or smell, pregnancy, disturbances of Āma, disagreeable food, idiosyncrasy and worms is known as Āgantuja Chardi.
TREATMENT: Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Powder of equal part of Tvak-Dālacīnī(cinnamon bark) and leaf of Tamāla 1 to 3 g. is to be taken with 4 to 6 g. honey twice a day. 2. Powder of equal part of Trikaṭu, Saindhava (rock-salt), Viḍa (a kind of salt) and Sauvarcala Lavaṇa (a kind of salt) – 500 mg. is to be taken with honey to make a paste three times a day. 3. Take powder of equal part of Yaṣṭimadhu (glycyrrhiza) and Rakta Candana (red sandalwood) – 2 g. and grind in 250 ml. milk. It is to be taken three or four times a day. 4. Powder of wood of Śveta Candana (white sandal) – 3 g., and Juice of fresh fruit of Āmalakī (embelic myrobalan) – 50 ml. is to be taken with 25 g. honey, three times a day. 5. Saktu of Yava (barley) – 10 to 20 g. is to be taken with honey to make a paste once a day. 6. Equal part of Lājā (pop of paddy), honey, Śarkarā (raw sugar) – 100 g. is to be taken with the decoction of Mudga (phaseolus bean) – 14 to 28 ml. three times a day. 7. Burn 100 g. bark of Pīpala and drop it in one liter of water. Liquid thus obtained is to be taken frequently. 8. Decoction prepared from whole plant of Parpaṭa (five leaved fumitory) – 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken three times a day. 9. Ghṛta Siddha with equal part of Śuṇṭhī (dried ginger) and Svarasa (juice) of Seed of Dāḍima (pomegranate) is to be taken in 12 to 24 g. dose with 50 to 100 ml. warm water 2 to 3 times a day. 10. Prepare Pānaka (syrup) of equal part of fruit rind of Āmalakī (embelic myrobalan), Drākṣā (raisin) and Śarkarā (raw sugar) in 50 g. honey and 200 ml. water and filter it through cloth. It is to be taken as frequently as possible.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Mayūra Puccha Bhasma: 250 to 500 mg. is to be taken with 4 to 6 g. honey three times in a day.
PATHYA: Śāli (red variety of rice), seeds of Yava (barley) and Mudga (phaseolus bean); Badara (jujube), Drākṣā (raisin), fruits of Nārikela (coconut), Āmalakī (embelic myrobalan) and Dāḍima (pomegranate); Ārdraka (ginger) and Nimbū (lemon) are useful for the patients of Chardi. In case of Āgantuja Chardi the foods of the liking of the patient may also be given.
APATHYA: Biṁbī (kunduru), Kadalī (banana), root of Yaṣṭimadhu (glycyrrhiza), leaf of Rājikā (black mustard) are harmful for the patient of Chardi. Unrelished food should be avoided.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Vami, Beng: Bami, Dogr: Ulaṭī, Guj: Ulṭī, Hind: Ulṭī, Kai, Kan: Vānti, Maly: Chardi, Mra: Ulṭī, Vānti, Ori: Bāntī, Panj: Ulaṭi, Tam: Vānthi, Tel: Vāntulu, Eng: Vomiting

Title: JVARA
Sanskrit: ज्वर
INTRO: Jvara (fever) is characterized by elevation of body temperature, loss of perspiration, and varying degree of pain in the body. Signs, symptoms and treatment of various types of Jvara and Rāja-Yakṣmā in which fever also occurs are being described separately.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Jvara, Nāriya, Beng: Jvara, Dogr: Buhāra, Guj: Tāvā, Hind: Jara, Bukhāra, Kan: Jvara, Maly: Pani, Mra: Tāpa, Ori: Jara, Panj: Bukhāra, Tāpa, Tam: Jvaram, Tel: Jvaramu, Uṣṇamu, Eng: Fever (pyrexia)

Title: Nava-Jvara
Sanskrit: नवज्वर
INTRO: Generally the fever up to 7 days is considered as Nava-Jvara.
TREATMENT: In the early stage of the fever keeping in view the general health of the patient Laṅghana (fasting) or light diet should be given. The duration of Laṅghana (fasting) should be to such an extent that it may not make the patient weak. For drinking purposes Sadaṅgapānīya should only be given. Godantī Bhasma in 125 to 250 mg. dose taken three times a day with honey reduces the temperature. Other treatment should be given on the basis of Doṣa involved.
REGIONAL NAMES:

Title: Vātika-Jvara
Sanskrit: वातिक-ज्वर
SYMPTOMS: The fever accompanied with rigors and having the period of abatement and exacerbation without coming down to normal is known as Vātika Jvara. Its other symptoms include pain in head, heart region or all over the body, loss of taste, constipation, flatulence, excessive yawning, cessation of sneeze, loss of sleep, dryness of lips and throat, and roughness of skin.
TREATMENT: Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Svarasa (juice) of root of Śatāvarī (asparagus) – 6 ml. and juice of stem of Guḍūcī – 6 ml., to be taken with 6 g. Guḍa (jaggery) three times a day. 2. Decoction of Bṛhat Pañcamūla – 14 to 28 ml., to be taken three times a day. 3. Decoction of equal part of Drākṣā (raisin), fruit of Gambhārī, whole plant of Trāyamāṇā, stem of Guḍūcī, root of Sārivā (sarsaparilla) – 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken with 6 g. Guḍa (jaggery) three times a day. 4. Decoction of equal part of fruit of Pippalī, stem of Guḍūcī, and Śuṇṭhī (dried ginger) – 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken three times a day. 5. Decoction of equal part of stem of Guḍūcī, root of Sārivā (sarsaparilla), Drākṣā (raisin) and fruit of Miśreyā (fennel) – 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken with 6 g. Guḍa (jaggery) three times a day. 6. Decoction of equal part of fruit of Pippalī (long pepper), root of Sārivā (sarsaparilla), Drākṣā (raisin), fruit of Miśreyā (fennel) and seeds of Nirguṇḍī – 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken with 6 g. Guḍa (jaggery) three times a day. 7. Decoction of equal part of fruit of Gokṣura (small caltrops), whole plants of Śālaparṇī (ticktrefoil), Pṛśniparṇī, Kaṇṭakārī and Bṛhatī (yellow berried night shade, the two varities), stem of Guḍūcī; fruit rind of Āmalakī (embelic myrobalan) and fruit of Dhānyaka (coriander) – 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken three times a day. 8. Decoction of equal part of whole plants of Rāsnā (Indian groundsel) and Bandaka, woods of Devadāru (deodar) and Sarala (pine) and Elavāluka (aloes) – 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken three times a day with 5 to 10 g. honey and 5 to 10 g. Śarkarā (raw sugar). 9. Decoction of equal part of root of Mustaka (motha), stem of Guḍūcī whole plants of Kirātatikta, Kaṇṭakārī, Bṛhatī, Trāyamāṇā (Indian gentian), Śālaparṇi (trick trefoil) and Pṛśniparṇī, fruit of Gokṣura (small caltrops) and Śuṇṭhī (dried ginger) – 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken three times a day.
REGIONAL NAMES:

Title: Paittika Jvara
Sanskrit: पैत्तिक ज्वर
SYMPTOMS: High temperature accompanied with diarrhoea, vomiting, bitter taste in the mouth, thirst, boils on lips, nose, mouth and throat, delirium, fainting and unconsciousness are the signs and symptoms of Paittika – Jvara.
TREATMENT: In case of high temperature i.e. above 39°C cold compress with ice bag on head is advisable till the temperature comes down to 38°C.
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Take equal part of whole plant of Parpaṭa, wood of Raktacandana (red sandal), rhizome of Bālaka (valerian) and Śuṇṭhī (dried ginger). It may be taken either in powder form or in decoction form. The dose of powder is 3 to 6 g. and of decoction is 14 to 28 ml. three times a day. 5 to 10 g. Śarkarā (raw sugar) may also be added at the time of taking the drug. 2. Phāṇṭa Prepared from 50 g. fruit Dhānyaka (coriander) in 100 ml. water is to be taken with Śarkarā (raw sugar) once a day in the morning. It is specially useful in Antaradāha of Pittaja Jvara. 3. Decoction prepared from whole plant of Parpaṭa (five leaved fumitory) – 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken with 5 to 10 g. Śarkarā (raw sugar) three times a day. 4. Decoction of equal part of rhizome of Kaṭukī, root of Mustaka (motha) and Indrayava (kurchi seed) – 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken with 5 to 10 g. honey three times a day. 5. Decoction of equal part of whole plant of Parpaṭa (five leaved fumitory), stem of Guḍūcī and fruit rind of Āmalakī (embelic myrobalan) – 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken three times a day. 6. Decoction of equal part of Drākṣā (raisin) and fruit pulp of Āragvadha (cassia) – 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken three times a day. 7. Decoction of equal part of bark of Lodhra, flowers of Nīlakamal (blue lotus) and Kamala, stem of Guḍūcī and root of Sārivā (Indian sarsaparilla) – 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken with 5 to 10 g. Śarkarā (raw sugar) three times a day. 8. Decoction of equal part of leaf of Paṭola (a variety of small gourd-snake gourd) and Indrayava (kurchi seed) – 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken with 5 to 10 g. honey three times a day. 9. Decoction of equal part of whole plants of Yavāsā (camel’s thorns), Parpaṭa (five leaved fumitory) and Kirātatikta (chirata), leaf of Vāsā, flower of Priyaṅgu and rhizome of Kaṭukī-14 to 28 ml. is to be taken with 5 to 10 g. honey or 5 to 10 g. Śarkarā (raw sugar) three times a day.
REGIONAL NAMES:

Title: Kaphaja Jvara
Sanskrit: कफज ज्वर
SYMPTOMS: Low grade fever, aversion to food, sweet taste, lassitude, heaviness, stiffness, feeling of cold and moist wrapping on the body, cough, nausea and excessive sleep are the signs and symptoms of Kaphaja Jvara.
TREATMENT: Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Powder of equal part of bark of Kaṭphala (box myrtle), root of Puṣkara (costus) and fruits of Karkaṭaśṛṅgī (carb’s claw) and Pippalī – 1 to 3 g, is to be taken with 5 to 10 g. honey three times a day. 2. Decoction of seed of Sambhāluka – 14 to 24 ml. is to be taken with powdered Marica (black pepper) – three times a day. 3. Decoction of equal part of Mustaka (motha), Indrayava (kurchi seed), fruit rinds of Harītakī (chebulic myrobalan), Āmalakī (embelic myrobalan) and Vibhītaka (beleric myrobalan) and fruit of Parūṣaka – 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken three times a day. 4. Decoction of equal part of fruit rinds of Āmalakī (embelic myrobalan) and Harītakī (chebulic myrobalan), fruit of Pippalī (long pepper), and root of Citraka (leadwort) – 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken three times a day. 5. Decoction of equal part of śuṇṭhī (dried ginger), Marica (black pepper), fruit of Pippalī (long pepper), Nāgakeśara (Indian ironwood tree stamen), rhizomes of Haridrā (turmeric) and Kaṭukī and Indrayava (kurchi seed) – 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken three times a day. 6. Decoction of leaf of Nirguṇḍī – 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken with 1 g. powdered Marica (black pepper) three times a day. 7. Decoction of equal part of root of Bījapūra (lemon), Śuṇṭhī (dried ginger), whole plant of Brāhmī (Indian pennywort) and root of Pippalī (long pepper) – 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken with 1 g. Yavakṣāra three times a day.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Sitopalādi Cūrṇa: 1 to 3 g. is to be taken with 5 to 10 g. honey three times a day. 2. Guḍūcī Satva: 1 to 2 g. is to be taken with 20 to 100 ml. warm water or 5 to 10 g. honey twice a day. 3. Jayā Vaṭī: 60 to 120 mg. is to be taken with honey three times a day. 4. Hiṅguleśvara Rasa: 1 to 2 Vaṭī, to be taken with 50 to 100 ml. warm water three times a day. 5. Mṛtyuñjaya Rasa: 1 Vaṭī, to be taken with sufficient honey or juice of Ārdraka (ginger) to make a paste three times a day. 6. Godantī Bhasma: 250 to 500 mg. is to be taken with sufficient honey to make a paste three times a day.
REGIONAL NAMES:

Title: Vāta Śleṣmika Jvara
Sanskrit: वातश्लेष्मिक ज्वर
SYMPTOMS: Moderately high fever with pain in joints and headache cold, cough, feeling of heaviness and moist wraping in the body, and excessive sleep are the signs and symptoms of Vāta-Śleṣmika Jvara.
TREATMENT: Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Decoction of fruit of Pippalī (long pepper) – 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken three times a day. 2. Decoction of Daśamūla – 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken with 1 g. powdered fruit of Pippalī (long pepper) three times a day. 3. Decoction of Laghu Pañca mūla – 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken three times a day. 4. Decoction of Pañcakola – 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken three times a day. 5. Decoction of equal part of root of Mustaka (motha), Śuṇṭhī (dried ginger) and whole plant of Kirātatikta (chiratia) – 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken three times a day. 6. Decoction of equal part of bark of Nimba, stem of Guḍūcī, Śuṇṭhī (dried ginger), wood of Devadāru (deodar), rhizome of Kaṭukī and root of Vacā (sweet-flag) – 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken three times a day. 7. Decoction of equal part of whole plant of Kaṇṭakārī, bark of Nimba, stem of Guḍūcī, Śuṇṭhī (dried ginger) and root of Puṣkara (costus) – 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken three times a day. 8. Decoction of equal part of fruit pulp of Āragvadha (cassia), roots of Pippalī and Mustaka (motha), rhizome of Kaṭukī and fruit rind of Harītakī (chebulic myrobalan) – 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken three times a day. 9. Decoction of equal part of root of Mustaka (motha), whole plants of Parpaṭa (five leaved fumitory) and Kaṇṭakārī, Śuṇṭhī (dried ginger), stem of Guḍūcī Fruit and root of Pippalī (long pepper), bulb of Rasona (garlic) and seed of Nirguṇḍī – 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken three times a day. 10. Decoction of equal part of root of Mustaka (motha), whole plants of Durālabhā (camel’s thorns) and Parpaṭa (five leaved fumitory) and Śuṇṭhī (dried ginger) – 14 to 28 ml is to be taken three times a day. 11. Śuddha Narasāra (ammonium chloride) – 250 to 500 mg. is to be taken with honey to make a paste three times a day.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Gojihvādi Kvātha: 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken three times a day. 2. Saubhāgya Vaṭī: 120 to 250 mg. to be taken with sufficient honey to make a paste three times a day. 3. Lakṣmī-Vilāsa Rasa: 60 to 120 mg. is to be taken with sufficient honey make a paste three times a day. 4. Tribhuvana Kīrtī Rasa: 60 to 120 mg. is to be taken with sufficient honey to make paste three times a day. 5. Śṛngārābhra Rasa: 120 to 250 mg. is to be taken with sufficient honey to make a paste three times a day. 6. Śvāsa-kāsa-Cintāmaṇī Rasa: 60 to 250 mg. is to be taken with sufficient honey to make a paste three times a day. 7. Śṛṅga Bhasma: 250 to 500 mg. is to be taken with sufficient honey to make a paste three times a day.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Pānīlaga, Beng: Śleṣma Jvara, Dogr: Kapha Vāye Kā Bhuhāra, Kan: Jvara, Maly: Vātakapha Jvaram, Mra: Vātakaphaja Tāpa, Hiva Tāpa, Panj: Vāta-Kaphaja Tāpa, Tam: Viṣa Juram, Eng: Influenza

Title: Abhinyāsa Jvara
Sanskrit: अभिन्यास ज्वर
SYMPTOMS: Fever, loss of power of the sense organs like hearing, seeing and smelling, loss of appetite, pricking pains; patient lies motionless or splashes head on the pillow or frequently changes his sides; talks less or talks in a voice like dove, are the main signs and symptoms of Abhinyāsa Jvara.
TREATMENT: Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Decoction of equal part of roots of Bījapūra (Lemon), Pāṣāṇabheda (saxifrage), Pāṭhā (false pariera) and Eraṇḍa (castor), bark of Bilva (bael) and whole plant of Kaṇṭakārī – 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken with 1 g. Saindhava (rock-salt) and 7 to 14 ml. Gomūtra (cow’s urine), three times a day. 2. Decoction of equal part of Trikaṭu, root of Mustaka (motha), Triphalā, rhizome of Kaṭukī, leaf of Paṭola (a variety of small cucumber-snake gourd), bark of Nimba, flower of Vāsā, whole plant of Kirātatikta (chirata) and stem of Guḍūcī – 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken three times a day. 3. Decoction of equal part of roots of Trivṛt (turpeth) and Indravāruṇī (colocynth), Triphalā, rhizome of Kaṭukī and fruit pulp of Āragvadha (cassia) – 7 to 14 ml. is to be taken with 1 g. Yavakṣāra once a day. This medicine is to be used with caution on account of its drastic/strong ingredients. 4. Decoction of equal part of root of Mustaka (motha), whole plants of Parpaṭa, Yavāsā (camel’s thorns), and Kirātatikta (chirata), Śuṇṭhī (dried ginger), stem of Guḍūcī, rhizome of Kaṭukī, roots of Yaṣṭimadhu (glycyrrhiza), Balā (country mallow), Pippalī (long pepper) and Trivṛt (turpeth), wood of Devadāru (deodar), Triphalā and Kampillaka Phala Raja (kamala dust) – 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken once a day.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Bṛhat Kastūrī-Bhairava Rasa: 1 to 2 Vaṭī, to be taken with 5 ml. juice of Ārdraka (ginger), three times a day. 2. Bṛhat Vāta-Cintāmaṇi Rasa: 1 to 2 Vaṭī, to be taken with 5 g. honey or 5 ml. juice of leaf of Tambūla (betel), three times a day. 3. Kṛṣṇa-Caturmukha Rasa: 60 to 120 mg. is to be taken with honey to make a paste three times a day. In case of excessive sweating sprinkle fine powder of fried seed of Āḍhakī or Śaṅkha Bhasma. Patient not responding to the treatment should be referred a specialist.
REGIONAL NAMES:

Title: Punarāvartaka-Jvara
Sanskrit: पुनरावर्तक ज्वर
INTRO: Punarāvartaka Jvara is characterized by rapid rise in temperature which remains for 6 or 7 days and then returns to normal by crisis; the fall in temperature is preceded and attened by profuse sweating or diarrhoea and after the interval of about a week the relapse occurs and temperature again remains for 3 or 4 days.
TREATMENT: Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Decoction of equal part of whole plant of Kirātatikta (chirata), rhizome of Kaṭukī, root of Mustaka (motha) and stem of Guḍūcī – 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken three times a day.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Sudaraśana Cūrṇa: 1 to 2 g. is to be taken three times a day with water or prepare its decoction and take in 14 to 28 ml. dose with Śarkarā two times a day.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Punarābartaka Jvara, Beng: Punarabortaka Jvara, Dogr: Dohre Dā Bhuhāra, Kan: Haralida Jvara, Maly: Onnaradan Pani, Mra: Punha Yeṇārā Tāpa, Ori: Pālijara, Tam: Murai Juram, Eng: Relapsing fever

Title: Viṣama Jvara
Sanskrit: विषम ज्वर
INTRO: Viṣama Jvara is an intermittent type of fever which comes at regular intervals of one, two or three days with rigors and patient feels excessive cold followed by the stage of hotness and then temperature falls to normal with profuse perspiration which may soak the bed clothes. Following are its commonly found three varieties.
REGIONAL NAMES:

Title: Anyedyuṣka Jvara
Sanskrit: (i). अन्येद्युष्क ज्वर
INTRO: A fever appearing once only in twenty four hours is called Anyedyuṣka Jvara.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Nita Jvara, Beng: Anyedyasa, Palā Jvara, Dogr: Canthā Canti, Guj: Tājo Tāva, Hind: Jurītāpa, Pārī Kā Bukhāra, Kan: Eradara Jvara, Maly: Viṣama Jvara, Mra: Dararoja Thandi, Vājūna Yenārā Tāpa, Ori: Dimikia, Tam: Viṣa Juram, Eng: Mixed malarial fever

Title: Tṛtīyaka Jvara
Sanskrit: (ii). तृतीयक ज्वर
INTRO: Fever appearing on alternate days with headache and pain in trunk and back is known as Tṛtīyaka Jvara.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Pāla Jvara, Beng: Tṛtīyaka, Pālā Jvara, Dogr: Trīayanak, Hind: Pārī Kā Bukhāra; Tijārī, Kan: Murara Jvara, Mra: Aik Divasāda Yenārā Tāpa, Ori: Didinia, Panj: Taiyā Bukhāra, Tel: Varasa Jvaramu, Tam: Muri Juram, Eng: Tertian fever

Title: Caturthaka Jvara
Sanskrit: (iii). चतुर्थक ज्वर
INTRO: The fever which appears on every on every fourth day and is preceded by headache and pain in the thigh is known as Caturthaka Jvara.
TREATMENT: The treatment of all types of Viṣama Jvara is as follows:
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Powdered fruit of Pippalī (long pepper) – 1 g. ghee – 1 g and Śarkarā (raw sugar) – 5 g. to be taken with 250 ml. warm milk and 5 g. honey, three times a day. 2. Decoction of Triphalā – 14 to 28 ml., to be taken wih equal quantity of milk or Guḍa (jaggery) three times a day. 3. Decoction of equal part of Śuṇṭhī (dried ginger), roots of Pippalī (long pepper) and Kṛṣṇa Mūsalī, fruit of Karkoṭī, fruit pulp of Āragvadha (cassia), rhizome of Bālaka (valerian) and fruit rind of Harītakī (chebulic myrobalan) – 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken with 1 g. Yavakṣāra three times a day. 4. Decoction of equal part of leaf of Paṭola (a variety of small cucumber – snake gourd), roots of Yaṣṭimadhu (glycyrrhiza) and Mustaka (motha), rhizome of Kaṭukī and fruit rind of Harītakī (chebulic myrobalan) – 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken three times a day. 5. Decoction of equal part of Triphalā, stem of Guḍūcī and Leaf of Vāsā – 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken three times a day. 6. Decoction of equal part of root of Mustaka (motha), Śuṇṭhī (dried ginger) and whole plant of Kaṇṭakārī (yellow berried night shade) – 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken with 250 mg. powdered fruit of Pippalī (long pepper) and 5 g. honey three times a day. 7. Decoction of equal part of root of Sahadevī (ash coloured fleabane) and Śuṇṭhī (dried ginger) – 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken three times a day. 8. Decoction of equal part of stem of Guḍūcī, bark of Nimba and fruit rind of Āmalakī (embelic myrobalan) – 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken with 5 to 10 g. honey three times a day. 9. Decoction of equal part of leaf of Paṭola (a variety of small cucumber – snake gourd), bark of Nimba, Drākṣā (raisin), Triphalā, root of Rāsnā (Indian groundsel) and leaf of Vāsā – 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken with 5 to 10 g. Śarkarā (raw sugar) and 5 to 10 g. honey, three times a day. 10. Decoction of equal part of roots of Yaṣṭimadhu (glycyrrhiza) and Uśīra (khas), wood of Rakta-Candana (red sandal), fruit rind of Āmalakī (embelic myrobalan), fruit of Dhānyaka (coriander), stem of Guḍūcī and leaf of Paṭola (a variety of small cucumber or snake gourd) – 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken with 5 to 10 g. honey or with 5 to 10 g. Śarkarā (raw sugar) three times a day. 11. Decoction of equal part of bark of Nimba, leaf of Paṭola (a variety of small cucumber of snake gourd), Drākṣā (raisin), Triphalā, fruit of Kāravellaka (bitter gourd) and Indrayava (kurchi seed) – 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken with 5 to 10 g. honey three times a day. 12. Decoction of equal part of whole plant of Kirātatikta (chirata), stem of Guḍūcī, wood of Rakta – Chandana (red sandal), and Śuṇṭhī (dried ginger) – 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken three times a day. 13. Decoction of equal part of stem of Guḍūcī, fruit rind of Āmalakī (embelic myrobalan), root of Mustaka (motha) and Drākṣā (raisin) – 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken three times a day. 14. Decoction of equal part of root of Vāsā, fruit rinds of Āmalakī (embelic myrobalan) and Harītakī (chebulic myrobalan), whole plant of Śālaparṇi wood of Devadāru (deodar) and Śuṇṭhī (dried ginger) – 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken with 5 to 10 g. Śarkarā (raw sugar) and 5 to 10 g. honey three times a day. 15. Decoction of equal part of root of Uśīra (khas) and Mustaka (motha), wood of Rakta – Gandana (red sandal), stem of Guḍūcī and fruit of Dhānyaka (coriander) – 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken three times a day. 16. Sudarśana Cūrṇa 1 to 2 g. is to be taken with honey three times a day. It may also be taken in decoction form in 14 to 28 ml. dose mixing with Śarkarā (raw sugar), two times a day.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Saptaparṇa Ghana Vaṭī: 2 to 4 Vaṭī, to be taken with 50 to 100 ml. water three times a day. 2. Mahā-Jvarāṅkuśa Rasa: 60 to 120 mg., to be taken with honey to make a paste three times a day. 3. Kṛṣṇa-Caturmukha Rasa: 60 to 120 mg., to be taken with honey to make a paste three times a day. 4. Candanādi Lauha: 250 to 500 mg., to be taken with honey to make a paste three times a day. 5. Viṣama-Jvarāntaka Lauha: 120 to 250 mg., to be taken with honey to make a paste three times a day. 6. Sarva-Jvara-Hara Lauha: 1 to 2 Vaṭī, to be taken with honey to make a paste three times a day.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Caturthaka Jvara, Beng: Caturthaka, Pālā Jvara, Dogr: Cautā, Guj: Cauthayo Tāva, Hind: Cauthā, Kan: Nalkara Jvara, Mra: Dona Divasāda Yenārā Tāpa, Ori: Tini Dinia, Panj: Chauthā Bukhāra, Tam: Muri Juram, Eng: Quartan fever

Title: Pralepaka Jvara
Sanskrit: प्रलेपक ज्वर
INTRO: Low fever with cold, feeling a coating of the whole body in sweat and heaviness of the body are the main symptoms of Pralepaka Jvara.
TREATMENT: Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Powder of equal part of rhizome of Vacā (sweet-flag) and Trikaṭu is to be taken in 2 to 4 g. dose with 5 to 10 g. honey three times a day. 2. Decoction of equal part of rhizome of Vacā (sweetflag) and Śuṇṭhī (dried ginger) – 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken three times a day.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Svarṇa-Vasantamālatī: 60 to 250 mg., to be taken with honey sufficient to make a paste three times a day. 2. Makaradhvaja: 60 to 250 mg., to be taken with 250 to 500 mg. powder of Trikaṭu and 5 to 10 g. honey three times a day. 3. Abhraka Bhasma: 120 to 250 mg., to be taken with honey sufficient to make a paste three times a day.
REGIONAL NAMES:

Title: Sannipātika Jvara
Sanskrit: सन्निपातिक ज्वर
SYMPTOMS: High fever with frequent change in feeling of cold and burning sensation i.e. sometimes patient feels cold and immediately after this feels hot; pain in joints limbs and head; excessive lacrimation, thirst, dry tongue, noises and pain in ear; cough, dyspnoea, blood in sputum; patient moves his head constantly; difficulty of speech; appearance of red and black coloured circular eruptions; delayed and scanty perspiration, urine and stool; loss of sleep, torpor, delirium, fainting etc. are the signs and symptoms of Sannipātika Jvara.
TREATMENT: This disease requires special attention of the physician and should be treated in the hospital. Treatment recommended for this disease is as follow.
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Powder of equal part of bark of Kaṭphala (box myrtle), root of Puṣkara (costus), fruit of Karkaṭaśṛṅgī (crab’s claw), Trikaṭu, whole plant Yavāsā (camel’s thorn) and fruit of Kṛṣṇa Jīraka (caraway) 1 to 3 g., to be taken with 5 to 10 g. honey three times a day. 2. Decoction of equal part of fruit pulp of Bilva (bael), fruits of Gambhārī and Gokṣura (small caltrop), leaf of Paṭola (a variety of small cucumber or snake gourd), roots of Agnimantha (wind killer) and Śyonāka, whole plants of Kaṇṭakārī (yellow berried night shade), Bṛhatī, Śālaparṇi (trick trfoil), Pṛśniparṇī and Kirātatikta (chirata), root of Mustaka (motha), stem of Guḍūcī and Śuṇṭhī (dried ginger) – 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken three times a day. 3. Decoction of equal part of Daśamūla, fruit of Karkaṭaśṛṇgī (crab’s claw), roots of Puṣkara (costus) and Bhāraṅgī, whole plant of Yavāsā (camel’s thorn), Indrayava (kurchi seeds), leaf of Paṭola (a variety of small cucumber or snake gourd) and rhizome of Kaṭukī – 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken three times a day. 4. Decoction of equal part of roots of Śaṭī (zedoary), Puṣkara (costus) and Pāṭhā (false pareira), fruit of Karkaṭaśṛṅgī (crab’s claw), whole plants of Kaṇṭakārī (yellow berried night shade), Yavāsā (camel’s thron) and Kirātatika (chirata), stem of Guḍūcī, Śuṇṭhī (dried ginger) and rhizome of Kaṭukī – 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken three times a day. 5. Warm decoction of Bṛhat Pañcamūla – 14 to 28 ml., to be taken three times a day. 6. Decoction of equal part of whole plant of Kirātatikta (chirata), root of Mustaka (motha), stem of Guḍūcī, Śuṇṭhī (dried ginger), leaf of Paṭola (a variety of small cucumber or snake gourd), and rhizome of Bālaka (valerian) – 14 to 28 ml., to be taken three times a day. 7. Decoction of equal part of whole plant Parpaṭa (five leaved fumitory), roots of Kuṣṭha (kooth), Uśīra (khas) and Mustaka (motha), bark of Kaṭphala (box myrtle), rhizome of Bālaka (valerian), Śuṇṭhī (dried ginger) and fruits of Karkaṭaśṛṅgī (crab’s claw) and Pippalī (long pepper) – 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken three times a day. 8. Prepare a Śīta Kaṣāya of woods of Rakta – Candana (red sandal) and Padma (wild cherry), rhizome of Kaṭukī and whole plant of Pṛśniparṇī by keeping over night in water. Its 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken three times a day. 9. Ṣaḍaṅga Pānīya: It is to be given frequently in small quantity in place of water.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Chinnaruhādi Kvātha (reduced to 1/8): 14 to 28 ml., to be taken with 120 to 360 mg. Sannipātabhairava Rasa and 5 to 10 g. honey twice a day. 2. Daśamūla-Kaṭutrayādi Kvātha: 28 to 56 ml., to be taken three times a day. 3. Saubhāgya Vaṭī: 120 to 250 mg., to be taken with honey to make a paste three times a day. 4. Mahā-Lakṣmī-Vilāsa Rasa: 120 to 250 mg., to be taken with 5 to 10 g. honey three times a day. 5. Ānanda Bhairava Rasa: 1 to 2 Vaṭī, to be taken with 1 g. Bhṛṣṭa fruit of Jīraka and 5 to 10 g. honey three times a day. 6. Śvāsa-Kāsa-Cintāmaṇi Rasa: 120 to 250 mg., to be taken with 5 to 10 g. honey three times a day. 7. Caturmukha Rasa: 60 to 120 mg., to be taken with 5 to 10 g. honey three times a day. 8. Vetāla Rasa: 60 to 120 mg., to be taken with 5 to 10 g. honey three times a day. 9. Bṛhat-Vāta-Cintāmaṇi Rasa: 60 to 120 mg., to be taken with 5 to 10 g. honey three times a day. 10. Bṛhat Kastūribhairava Rasa: 60 to 120 mg., to be taken with honey to make a paste three times a day.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Tridosika Jvara, Beng: Sannipātika Jvara, Dogr: Sannavātha, Hind: Sannipāta, Kan: Sannipāta Jvara, Maly: Sanni, Mra: Tridoṣaja Jvara, Ori: Sannipāta, Panj: Sannipāta Bukhāra, Tam: Sanni Juram

Title: Śvasanaka Jvara (Pneumonia)
Sanskrit: श्वसनक ज्वर
SYMPTOMS: High fever with rigors, pain in the chest and sides, frequent cough with thick tenacious phlegm, difficult and increased breathing, bloating of nostrils during breathing, soft, heavy and rapid pulse having ratio of 2:1 with breathing, sweating of the forehead, extremely moist body, lassitude, weakness, rough and dirty tongue, torpor, delirium, etc. are the signs and symptoms of Śvasanaka Jvara.
TREATMENT: Extreme rapid pulse and breathing are forewarning of crisis and in that case patient should immediately be shifted to hospital.
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Decoction of equal part of whole plants of Bṛhat-Kaṇtakārī and Yavāsā (camel’s thorn), root of Puṣkara (costus), Bhāraṅgī, rhizome of Śaṭī (zedoary), fruit of Karkaṭaśṛṅgī (crab’ claw), Indrayava (kurchi seed), leaf of Paṭola (a variety of small cucumber), and rhizome of Kaṭukī is to be taken three times a day.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Gorocanādi Vaṭī: 1 to 2 Vaṭī, to be taken with 5 to 10 g. honey one hour before meal two times a day. 2. Sañjīvanī Vaṭī: 1 to 2 Vaṭī, to be taken with 5 to 10 g. honey three times a day. 3. Siddha-Prāṇeśvara Rasa: 1 to 2 Vaṭī, to be taken with 5 to 10 g. honey three times a day. 4. Kaphaketu Rasa: 1 to 2 Vaṭī, to be taken with 5 to 10 ml. juice of Ārdraka (ginger) or 5 to 10 g. honey three times a day. 5. Svarṇabhūpati Rasa: 60 to 180 mg., to be taken with 28 to 56 ml. Daśamūla Kaṭutrayādi Kvātha and 5 to 10 g. honey before meal, three times a day. 6. Bṛhat-Kastūrī-Bhairava Rasa: 60 to 120 mg., to be taken with honey three times a day.
REGIONAL NAMES:

Title: Āntrika Jvara
Sanskrit: आन्त्रिक ज्वर
SYMPTOMS: Continuous fever or more than 7 days duration is generally taken as Santata Jvara (Āntrika Jvara). It may continue upto 4 to 5 weeks. Its other symptoms include constipation or loose motions, heavily coated tongue with white fur, comparatively slow pulse, appearance of small rose-coloured spots on 7th to 12th day of fever, intense feeling of burning outside and inside, thirst and heaviness in the body. In the third week patient may have extreme lethargy, drowsiness and fainting.
TREATMENT: Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Decoction of equal part of whole plant of Kirātatikta (chirata), roots of Mustaka (motha) and Pāṭhā (false pareira), stem of Guḍūcī, Śuṇṭhī (dried ginger), rhizome of Bālaka (valerian) and stem of Kamala (lotus) – 14 to 28 ml., to be taken three times a day. 2. Prepare Śīta Kaṣāya from equal part of fruit of Parūṣaka (asiatic grewia), Triphalā, woods of Devadāru (deodar), Rakta-Candana (red Sandal) and Padmaka (wild cherry), bark of Kaṭphala (box myrtle), rhizome of Kaṭukī and whole plant of Pṛśniparṇī. Liquid thus obtained is to be taken in 14 to 28 ml. dose three times a day.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Siddha Prāṇeśvara Rasa: 1 to 2 Vaṭī, to be taken with 5 to 10 g. honey or 50 to 100 ml. warm water three times day. 2. Saubhāgya Vaṭī: 120 t0 250 mg., to be taken with honey three times a day.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Antrika Jvara, Beng: Āntrika Jvara, Dogr: Meyādī, Guj: Muddadī Tāva, Hind: Miyādi Bukhāra, Mra: Āntrika Tāpa, Ori: Āntrika Jara, Panj: Miyādī Bukhāra, Tam: Ui Jvaram, Eng: Enteric fever

Title: Granthika Jvara
Sanskrit: ग्रन्थिक ज्वर
SYMPTOMS: Onset of high fever accompanied by shivering, vertigo, lethargy, limping, loss of sleep, delirium, delusion and fainting; on 2nd or 3rd day tender enlargement of lymph glands appear in inguinal, axillary or other regions depending upon the site of flea bite; the glands enlarge rapidly and have intense pain; these are the main signs and symptoms of Granthika Jvara. Three common forms of this disease are as follows: 1. Bubonic Plague: It is the commonest variety and glandular swelling is marked. 2. Fulminant Plague: This form of the disease is characterized by high fever, slight glandular enlargement, vomiting of blood and death within few hours. 3. Pneumonic Plague: In this variety of the diseases no glandular enlargement occurs but there is intense prostration and death occurs after 3 to 5 days.
TREATMENT: This  disease is of an epidemic nature calling for specialized attention.
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Decoction of bark of Śirīlṣa – 14 to 28 ml., to be taken three times a day.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Nimbādi Cūrṇa: 2 to 4 g., to be taken with warm water three times a day.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Granthika Jvara, Beng: Granthika Jvara, Dogr: Moldhī Thāpa, Guj: Gantha No Ṭāva, Hind: Tauna, Mahāmāri, Plega, Kan: Gadde Jvarda, Mra: Gāṭhicā Tāpa, Mahāmārī, Panj: Plega, Tauna, Tam: Narikatti Jvaram, Tel: Mahāmāri, Eng: Plague

Title: Pāṣāṇagardabha Jvara
Sanskrit: पाषाणगर्दभ ज्वर
TREATMENT: Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Gargle with the decoction of equal part of barks of Vaṭa (banyan), Udumbara (gular-fig tree), Pīpala (peepal), Pārasapīpala and Plakṣa.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Pañca-Tikta Ghṛta: 12 to 24 g., to be taken with 50 ml. warm water twice a day. 2. Mahā-Tikta Ghṛta: 12 to 24 g., to be taken with 50 ml. warm water twice a day. 3. Tikta Ghṛta: 12 to 24 g., to be taken with 50 ml. warm water twice a day.
PATHYA: Purāṇa Śāli (old red variety of rice), soup of seeds of Mudga (phaseolus beans), Masūra (lentil), Caṇaka (gram) and Makuṣṭha (aconite leaved kidney bean); Godugdha (cow’s milk), Goghṛta (cow’s ghee), Ajā Dugdha and Ghṛta (goat’s milk and ghee); Saḍaṅga Panīya, Uṣṇodaka (warm water); fruits of Vārtāka (brinjal), Śigru (horse radish) and Paṭola (a variety of small cucumber); leaves of Vāstūka (a variety of chenopodium – white goose foot) and Taṇḍulīya (amaranth), Drākṣā (raisin or grape fruit), fruit of Dāḍima (pomegranate), Lavaka Māṁsa (partridge meat), Śaśa Māṁsa (rabbit’s meat), Kakkuṭa Māṁsa (cock’s meat), Bartaka Māṁsa (swans meat) are the useful articles of diet for the patients suffering from various types of fever. Patient should take complete rest during the illness.
APATHYA: Guru, Asātmya and Vidāhi Anna, exercise, sexual intercourse, bath and walking are harmful for the patients of fever.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Siyālgāla, Jadumāṇi, Dogr: Phalbu, Guj: Galpāchārauṇe, Hind: Kānpeda, Kan: Gantlamma, Maly: Mundivikkam, Mra: Pāṣāṇa gardhabha, Galphuga, Ori: Galuā, Panj: Kanapeḍe, Tam: Poṭṭhālammai, Tel: Gavadabillalu, Eng: Mumps, parotitis, intro: Pāṣāṇgardabha Jvara is a condition where along with fever a smooth, immovable, tender gland appears behind the ear due to the swelling of parotid gland related with the formation of saliva. At first inflammation sets in one side with pain and moderately high fever but it may involve other side also. The attack last, four to six days and may lead to the complications like swelling of scrotum. It is a contagious disease and its incidence are common in children and young adults.

Title: Rājayakṣmā
Sanskrit: राजयक्ष्मा
SYMPTOMS: Rājayakṣmā is a wasting disease characterized by low grade fever, loss of appetite, night sweating and loss of weight. In all cases of unexplained fever, one of the cause may be tuberculosis. Its other symptoms depend upon the organ of the body involved. Lung is the most commonly involved organ and in that case patient may have the symptoms like evening rise of temperature, cough, haemoptysis, hoarseness of voice, night sweating, loss of appetite, loss of weight, pain in scapular region and ribs and burning sensation in sole and palm.
TREATMENT: Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Juice (Svarasa) of fresh leaf of Vāsā – 14 to 28 ml., to be taken with 5 to 10 g. honey three times a day. 2. Powder of root of Yaṣṭimadhu (glycyrrhiza) – 3 to 6 g. and wood of Rakta Candana (red sandal) – 3 to 6 g., to be taken with 250 ml. milk three times a day. 3. Powder of equal part of fruits of Kharjūra (date), Pippalī (long pepper), Drākṣā (raisin) and Karkaṭaśṛṅgī (crab’s claw), fruit rind of Harītakī (chebulic myrobalan) and whole plant of Durālabhā (camel’s thorn) – 3 to 6 g., to be taken with 5 to 10 g. honey three times a day. 4. Kalka (paste) of equal part of fruits of Kharjūra (date) and Drākṣā (raisin) – 12 to 24 g. is to be taken with 1 g. powdered fruit of Pippalī, 5 to 10 g. Śarkarā (raw sugar) and honey, three times a day. 5. Powder of equal part of fruit of Pippalī (long pepper), roots of Aśvagandhā and Yaṣṭimadhu (glycyrrhiza) and seed of Kapikacchū (cowage) – 3 to 6 g., to be taken with 100 to 250 ml. goat’s milk twice a day. 6. Powder of equal part of fruit of Pippalī (long pepper), Drākṣā (raisin) and Śarkarā (raw sugar) – 3 to 6 g., to be taken with 5 to 10 g. honey three times a day. 7. Powder of equal part of root of Aśvagandhā (winter cherry), fruit of Pippalī (long pepper) and Śarkarā (raw sugar) – 3 to 6 g., to be taken with 5 to 10 g. honey three times a day. 8. Powder of equal part of Triphalā, fruit of Pippalī (long pepper), root of Mustaka (motha), nut of Śṛṅgāṭaka (water chestnut) and Śarkarā (raw sugar) – 3 to 6 g., to be taken with honey three time a day. 9. Powder of equal part of roots of Kṣīra-Kākolī, Puṣkara (costus) and Śaṭī (zedoary), seed of Tulasī (sacred basil), Śarkarā (raw sugar) and Guḍa (jaggery) – 3 to 6 g., to be taken with 5 to 10 g. honey and 5 to 10 g. Ghṛta (ghee) three times a day. 10. Use of meat of pigeon, deer and goat (dried powder) – 12 to 24 g., to be taken with 250 ml. goat’s milk. 11. Decoction of equal part of fruit Dhānyaka (coriander) and Pippalī (long pepper), seed of Dāḍima (pomegranate) and Śuṇṭhī (dried ginger) – 14 to 28 ml., to be taken three times a day. 12. Decoction of equal part of roots of Aśvagandhā (winter cherry), Śatāvarī (wild asparagus), Atibalā (country mallow), Puṣkara (costus) and Ativiṣā (Indian atees), Daśamūla, stem of Guḍūcī, and leaf of Vāsā – 14 to 28 ml., to be taken three times a day. 13. Decoction of stem of Guḍūcī – 14 to 28 ml., to be taken with 1 g. powdered fruit of Pippalī (long pepper) three times a day. 14. Decoction of equal part of fruit rind of Harītakī (chebulic myrobalan) and Āmalakī (embelic myrobalan), fruit pulp of Āragvadha (cassia) and rhizome of Kaṭukī – 14 to 28 ml., to be taken three times a day. This preparation is useful when patient is having constipation
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Elādi Cūrṇa: 1 to 3 g., to be taken with 5 to 10 g. honey three times a day. 2. Sitopalādi Cūrṇa: 1 to 3 g., to be taken with 5 to 10 g. honey three times a day. 3. Tālīsādi Cūrṇa: 1 to 3 g., to be taken with 5 to 10 g. honey three times a day. 4. Mahā-Lakṣmī Vilāsa Rasa: 1 to 2 Vaṭī, to be taken with 5 to 10 g. honey three times a day. 5. Jayamaṇgala Rasa: 60 to 250 mg., to be taken with 5 to 10 g. honey three times a day. 6. Caturmukha Rasa: 60 to 250 mg., to be taken with 5 to 10 mg., to be taken with 5 to 10 g. honey three times a day. 7. Candrāmṛta Rasa: 120 to 250 mg., to be taken with 5 to 10 g. honey three times a day. 8. Svarṇa-Vasanta-Mālatī (Laghu): 1 to 2 Vaṭī, to be taken with 5 to 10 g. honey three times a day. 9. Amṛtaprāśa: 12 to 24 g., to be taken with 100 to 250 ml. warm milk three times a day. 10. Vāsāvaleha: 12 to 24 g., to be taken with 100 to 250 ml. warm milk three times a day. 11. Cyavanaprāśavaleha: 12 to 24 g., to be taken with 100 to 250 ml. warm milk three times a day. 12. Drākṣāsava or Drakṣāriṣṭa: 14 to 28 ml., to be taken with equal quantity of water twice a day after meal. 13. Dhanvantara Guṭikā: 1 g., to be taken three times a day with 14 to 28 ml. decoction of Jīraka. If the patient does not respond to the treatment refer to a specialist.
PATHYA: Śāli (red variety of rice), Godhūma (wheat), seeds of Yava (barley) and Mudga (phascolus bean); fruits of Dāḍima (pomegranate), Āmalakī (embelic myrobalan) and Āmra (mango); Ajā Dugdha (goat’s milk), Balā Siddha Dugdha, Suvāsita Jala (scented water), Madya (Wine with caution); Ajā or Mṛga Māṁsa (goat’s or deer’s meat), Karkaṭa Māṁsa (crab’s meat) and meat of wild animals are the useful articles of diet for the patient of Rāja-Yakṣmā.
APATHYA: Food prepared in Taila (oil), Vṛntāka (brinjal), fruits of Kāravellaka (bitter gourd), Bilva (bael) and Ajājī are harmful for the patient of Rājayakṣmā. Sexual intercourse, day sleep and anger should be avoided.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Yakṣmā Roga, Beng: Rajjakkha, Dogr: Rājoraga, Guj: Tapedika, Hind: Kṣaya, Kan: Kṣaya, Maly: Kṣaya Rogam, Mra: Kṣaya, Ori: Kāsma, Panj: Tapedika, Tam: Kayānoy, Tel: Kṣaya, Eng: Pthysis or tuberculosis

Title: Tṛṣṇā
Sanskrit: तृष्णा
SYMPTOMS: 1. Vātaja Tṛṣṇā: Its symptoms include dryness of the mouth, pricking pain in the temples and head, loss of thirst increases with cold water. 2. Pittaja Tṛṣṇā: In this type of Tṛṣṇā, the patient have the symptoms like loss ot appetite, bitter taste in the mouth, burning sensation, redness of the eyes, feeling of dryness in the whole body, liking for cold things and fainting. 3. Kaphaja Tṛṣṇā: Excessive sleep, sweet taste in the mouth and extreme emaciation are the symptoms of Kaphaja Tṛṣṇā. 4. Kṣayaja Tṛṣṇā: In this disease patient inspite of taking large amount of water does not feel satisfaction. Its other important symptom is loss of weight. 5. Āmaja Tṛṣṇā: Pain in the heart region, excessive salivation and uneasiness are the signs and symptoms of Āmaja Tṛṣṇā.
TREATMENT: Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Use of Siddha Jala prepared with roots of Mustaka (motha) and Uśīra (khas), whole plant of Parpaṭa (five leaved fumitory), wood of Rakta-Candana (red sandal), Śuṇṭhī (dried ginger), Śuṇṭhī (dried ginger) and rhizome of Bālaka (valerian). 2. Powder of equal part of Vaṭāṅkura (banyan shoots), Dāḍima (pomegranate fruit), Tvak-Dālacīnī (cinnamon bark), bark of Lodhra and root of Yaṣṭimadhu (glycyrrhiza) – 1 to 3 g. is to be taken with Taṇḍulodaka (rice washing) – 14 to 28 ml. three times a day. 3. Take equal part of fruit of Dhānyaka (coriander), Śuṇṭhī (dried ginger) and Drākṣā (raisin), make a Poṭṭalikā, keep it in water and boil. Cooled liquid thus obtained is to be taken in 14 to 28 ml. dose thrice a day. 4. Decoction of equal part of fruits of Dhānyaka (coriander) and Miśreyā (fennel), roots of Yaṣṭimadhu (glycyrrhiza) and Uśīra (khas) and fresh leaf of Āmra (mango) 14 to 28 ml., to be taken three times a day. 5. Make Pānaka of equal part of fluid obtained from the fruit of Nārikela (coconut) and fruits of Dhānyaka (coricander) and Miśreyā (fennel) –100 to 250 ml., to be taken three times a day.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Jambīra Pānaka: 14 to 28 ml., to be taken three times a day. 2. Guḍūcī-Satva: 1 to 2 g., to be taken with 5 to 10 g. honey three times a day. 3. Sūta-Śekhara Rasa: 120 to 360 mg., to be taken with 5 to 10 g. honey three times a day. 4. Pravāla Piṣṭī: 120 to 250 mg., to be taken with 5 to 10 g. honey three times a day. 5. Āmalakī Rasāyana: 1 to 3 g., to be taken with 5 to 10 g. honey three times a day.
PATHYA: Śāli Vilepī (gruel prepared from red variety of rice), Lājamaṇḍa, soup of seeds of Caṇaka (gram), Mudga (phaseolus bean) and Masūra (lentil); Godugdha (cow’s milk), Madhura Takra (butter milk); Siddha Jala prepared from rhizome of Bālaka (valerian) and fruit of Dhānyaka (coriander); fluid obtained from the fruit of Nārikela (coconut), Śarkarā (raw sugar); vegetable prepared from flower of Rambha (banana); fruits of Kharjūra (date), Dāḍima (pomegranate), Āmalakī (embelic myrobalan), Mātuluṅga (lemon), Karmarda, Jambīra (medicinal lemon) and Kūṣmāṇḍa (a variety of pumpkin gourd-white gourd) are the useful articles of diet for the patient of Tṛṣṇā.
APATHYA: Amla, Lavaṇa, Tikta, Kaṣāya Rasa and Guru Dravya; Dūṣia Jala, and Trikaṭu are harmful for the patient of Tṛṣṇā.
