REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Piyāh, Beng: Tṛṣṇā, Dogr: Thapadika, Guj: Piyāsa, Hind: Tāsa, Pyāsa, Kan: Bāyārike, Maly: Triksna, Mra: Tahānā, Ori: Śoṣa, Panj: Pyāsa Roga, Tam: Nirvetkai, Tel: Dappi, Eng: Polydipsia, excessive thirst, intro: Tṛṣṇā is a disease characterized by excessive thirst. It has been classified into 7 groups. Specific symptomatology of important types of Tṛṣṇā is as follow.

Title: DĀHA
Sanskrit: दाह
INTRO: Dāha is a condition characterized by the feeling of excessive burning sensation in the body. It may be caused by the prolonged use of alcohol, vitiation of Rakta and Pitta, suppression of urge of thirst, bleeding, wasting diseases and trauma of Marma (vital centres of the body). In Severe condition patient spurts out tongue, have copper coloured face and eyes, delirium, fainting, unconsciousness and coma.
TREATMENT: In Severe case of Dāha patient may be covered with wet sheet and spray of cold water may be given to the head. For other patients bath may be given with cold water which is medicated by adding the powder of rhizome of Sugaṅdha Bālā (valerian), woods of Padma (wild cherry) and Candana (sandal); and root of Uśīra (khas).
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Fluid obtained from the fruit of Nārikela (coconut) is to be taken frequently.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Guḍūcī Satva: 120 to 250 mg., to be taken with 50 to 100 ml. water three times a day. 2. Pravāla Piṣṭi: 120 to 250 mg., to be taken with 5 to 10 g. honey three times a day. 3. Uśirāsava: 14 to 28 ml. to be taken with equal quantity of water twice a day after meal.
PATHYA: Ṣaṣṭika Śāli (a variety of rice), seeds of Mudga (phaseolus bean) and Yava (barley), Maṇḍa, Lājā (pop of paddy); milk, butter, Śarkarā (raw sugar), Māṁsa Rasa (meat soup); fruits of Kūṣmāṇḍa (a variety of pumpkin gourd-white gourd), Kadalī (banana) and Paṭola (a variety of small cucumber-snake gourd), leaf of Parpaṭa (five leaved fumitory), fruits of Parūṣaka (Asiatic grewia), Priyāla (cuddapah almond) and Śṛṅgāṭaka (water chestnut), flower of Madhūka (mahuwa), Drākṣā (raisin or grape fruit), and fruit of Nārikela (coconut) and Tāla (date) are the useful articles of diet for the patient of Dahā.
APATHYA: Kaṭu and Tikta Rasa, Uṣṇa Dravya, Tāmbūla (betel), incompatible items of food in diet are harmful for the patient of Dāha. Suppression of calls of nature, riding, excessive walking, exercise, sexual intercourse and movement in sun should be avoided.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Porānī, Beng: Dahā, Dogr: Khāli, Dāha, Guj: Baḍaṭara, Hind: Dahā, Jalana, Kan: Uri, Maly: Pukāchila, Mra: Agahoṇe, Ori: Jalapoḍā, Panj: Jalanā, Tam: Erichala, Tel: Dhātu Kā Roga, Eng: Dehydration, burning sensation

Title: DHĀTUKṢAYA
Sanskrit: धातुक्षय
SYMPTOMS: Loss of memory, forgetfulness, dull intellect, lack of confidence, indecisiveness, inability to undertake sexual intercourse to the satisfaction or incapacity to fecundate the female, flaccidness, oedema, eruptions, enlargement of prepuces, burning sensation of the male organ are the signs and symptoms of Dhātu-Kṣaya.
TREATMENT: Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Powdered Vidāri kanda – 3 to 6 g., to be taken with ghee followed by a draught of 100 to 250 ml. milk twice a day. 2. Equal part of powdered root of Yaṣṭimadhu (glycyrrhiza), Goghṛta (cow’s ghee) and honey is to be taken in 12 to 24 g. dose three times a day with 100 to 250 ml. cow’s milk. 3. Equal part of Svarasa (juice) of root of Śatamūlī (wild asparagus) and leaf of Brāhmī (Indian penny wort) – 7 to 14 ml. is to be taken with 100 to 250 ml. Dugdha (fresh milk) twice a day. 4. Powder of equal part of decorticated seed of Kapikacchū (cowage), Kākolī and Kṣīrakākolī, Ṛsbhaka and roots of Aśvagandhā (winter cherry) and Śatāvarī (wild asparagus) – 3 to 6 g. is to be taken with 100 to 250 ml. milk and 25 to 50 g. Śarkarā (raw sugar) twice a day. 5. Powder of equal part of roots of Śālmalī (silk cotton tree) and Mūsali – 3 to 6 g. to be taken with 5 to 10 g. Śarkarā (raw sugar) and 5 to 10 g. Ghṛta (ghee) three times a day. 6. Powder of equal part of Kokilākṣa and Śarkarā (raw sugar) is to be taken in 3 to 6 g. dose followed by a glass of Dhāroṣṇa Dugdha (freshly milched milk of cow) twice a day. 7. Mix fine powder of equal part of seeds of Māṣa (black phaseolus bean), Kapikacchū (cowage), Godhūma (wheat) and Ṣaṣṭi (a variety of rice), tuber of Vidārī (giant potato), Kokilākṣa and Gokṣura with cow’s milk and prepare a liquid dough. Its 100 to 250 g. is to be taken with milk twice a day. 8. Take root of Śālmalī (Indian silk cotton tree) – 4 parts, root of Śatāvarī (wild asparagus) – 3 parts, root of Śaṭī (zedoary) – 2 parts, Vaṁśalocana (bamboo manna)-1/2 part and make the powder. Its 3 to 6 g. is to be taken with 5 to 10 g. honey and Śarkarā (raw sugar) three times a day. 9. Give seven Bhāvanā of Svarasa (juice) of fruit of Āmalakī (embelic myrobalan) to the powdered fruit rind of Āmalakī and take its 3 to 6 g. with 100 to 250 ml. milk and 25 to 50 g. Śarkarā (raw sugar) twice a day. 10. Yavāgu of Māṣa (black phaseolus bean) – 250 g. is to be taken with Ghṛta (ghee) – 12 g. followed by a draught of 250 ml. milk. 11. Decoction of fruit of Gokṣura – 14 to 28 ml. or its Svarasa (juice) – 7 to 14 ml. is to be taken with 50 to 100 ml. cow’s milk twice a day. 12. Make decoction of equal part of fruit of Gokṣura (small caltrops) and tuber of Vidārī (giant potato) and add four times of its weight of Godugha (cow’s milk) and 1/8th part of decorticated Māṣa (black phaseolus bean) and Ṣaṣṭī (a variety of rice) and boil. When ready after Kṣīra Pāka add 1/8th Goghṛta (cow’s ghee). Its 100 to 250 ml. is to be taken twice a day. 13. Prepare Kṣīra-Pāka of decorticated seed of Māṣa (black phaseolus bean) and seed of Kapikachhu (cowage) and on cooling add Ghṛta (ghee) and Śarkarā (raw sugar) to taste. Its 100 to 250 ml. is to be taken with powdered fruit of Pippalī (long pepper) – 1 g. twice a day.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Makaradhvaja Vaṭī: 1 to 2 Vaṭī, to be taken with honey to make a paste twice a day. 2. Śilājitvādi Vaṭī: 1 to 2 Vaṭī to be taken with honey to make a paste three times a day. 3. Makaramuṣṭi Yoga: 60 to 120 mg., to be taken with honey and Śarkarā (raw sugar) to make a paste twice a day. 4. Smṛtisāgara Rasa: 60 to 250 mg., to be taken with honey to make a paste three times a day. 5. Pūrṇacandra Rasa: 1 to 2 Vaṭī, to be taken with honey to makes a paste three times a day. 6. Amṛtaprāśāvaleha: 12 to 24 g., to be taken with 100 to 250 ml. milk three times a day. 7. Aśvagandhā Ghṛta: 12 to 24 g., to be taken with 100 to 250 ml. Dugdha (milk) three times a day. 8. Brāhmī Ghṛta: 12 to 24 g., to be taken with 100 to 250 ml. Dugda (milk) three times a day. 9. Bṛhat Chāglādi Ghṛta: 12 to 24 g., to be taken with 100 to 250 ml. Dugdha (milk) three times a day. 10. Mṛtasañjīvanī Surā: 7 to 14 ml., to be taken twice a day with equal quantity of water after meal.
PATHYA: Śāli (a red variety of rice), Godhūma (wheat), seeds of Masūra (lentil) and Caṇaka (gram); milk, butter, meat of deer, chicken, rabbit and goat; Drākṣā (raisin or grape fruit), fruits of Kharjūra (date), Āmra (mango) and Dāḍima (pomegranate) are the useful articles for the patient of Dhātukṣaya.
APATHYA: Chillies and sour food are harmful for the patient of Dhātu-Kṣaya. Frequent sexual intercourse should be avoided.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Dhātu-Kṣya, Baja, Beng: Dhātukhaya, Dogr: Nāmardī, Guj: Dhāta Paḍvo, Hind: Dhātu Kā Roga, Kan: Napuṁsakata, Saṇḍa, Maly: Ṣaṇḍathvam, Mra: Napuṁskatava, Ori: Anapuruṣa, Panj: Nāmardī, Tam: Ammaikuraivoy, Tel: Dhātunaṣṭamu, Nampuṁṣa, Eng: Neurasthenia, impairment of memory, impotency

Title: NĀSĀ-ROGA
Sanskrit: नासारोग
INTRO: General signs, symptoms and treatment of Pratiśyāya and Pīnasa are as follows.
REGIONAL NAMES: Beng: Nāsā Roga, Dogr: Nāsāroga, Guj: Nāka Nā Roga, Hind: Nāka Ke Roga, Kan: Mūginā Roga, Maly: Nāsā Rogam, Mra: Nākāce Roga, Ori: Tīkhapādipā, Panj: Nāka De Roga, Tam: Mukku Noy, Tel: Mukku Rogamulu, Eng: Diseases of the nose

Title: Pratiśyāya
Sanskrit: प्रतिश्याय
SYMPTOMS: Prodromal symptoms of Pratiśyāya are sneezing, heaviness in the head, stiffness and pain in the body. Specific symptoms of Vātika, Paittika, Kaphaja and Sannipātaja varieties of Praitiśyāya are as follows. 1. Vātika Pratiśyāya: Obstruction to the nasal passage due to inflammation, watery discharge from the nose, excessive sneezing. Change in the voice and dryness of throat are the common symptoms of Vātika Pratiśyāya. 2. Paittika Pratiśyāya: Yellow coloured warm discharge from the nose and feeling of hotness are the main symptoms of Paittika Pratiśyāya. 3. Kaphaja Pratiśyāya: White coloured cold discharge from the nose, heaviness in the head are the main symptoms of Kaphaja pratiśyāya. 4. Sannipātaja Pratiśyāya: Frequent attacks of coryza are due to Sannipātaja Pratiśyāya.
TREATMENT: Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Decoction of equal part of Drākṣā (raisin), Marica (black pepper), leaf of Vāsā (vasaka), Tvak-Dālacīnī (cinnamon bark) and root of Yaṣṭimadhu (glycyrrhiza) – 14 to 28 ml. is to be taken with 5 to 10 g. Śarkarā (raw sugar) thrice a day.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Tribhuvana Kīrtī Rasa: 1 to 2 Vaṭī, to be taken with honey sufficient to make a paste or with-7 to 14 ml. juice of Ārdraka (ginger), twice a day. 2. Nāga Guṭikā: 1 to 2 Vaṭī, to be taken with 7 to 14 ml. juice of leaf of Tulasī (sacred basil) and 60 to 120 mg. powdered bark of Kaṭphala (box myrtle) twice a day.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Pānīlāga, Beng: Pratiśyāya, Sardī, Dogr: Jukām, Reśā, Guj: Sardī, Hind: Sardī, Jukhāma, Kan: Negādi Śīta, Maly: Mūkh-Olichil, Mra: Sardī, Ori: Sardī, Panj: Jukāma, Tam: Nīra Kam Jalathodam, Tel: Jalubu, Eng: Coryza, Common cold

Title: Pīnasa
Sanskrit: पीनस
SYMPTOMS: In the initial stage of the disease patient has the symptoms of heaviness in the head, loss of appetite, discharge from the nose and change in the voice. Later on discharge from the nose becomes thick and it sticks in the sinuses of the nose. Loss of smell and taste may also occur.
TREATMENT: Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. 5 g. Ārdraka (ginger) fried in ghee, to be taken two times a day. 2. Boil 5 g. Ārdraka (fresh ginger) in 250 ml. milk and give douche to the nose with it. 3. Mix 1 to 3 g. powder of equal part of Trikaṭu, root bark of Citraka (leadwort) leaves of Tālīsa Patra (himalayan silver fir) and Tejapatra (tamal), fruit of Ciñcā (tamarind), Jīraka (cumin), Elā (cardamom), Amlavetasa, Cavya and. Tvak-Dālacīnī (cinnamon bark) with 5 g. old Gua (jaggery). It is to be taken thrice a day.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Vyoṣādi Vaṭī: 2 to 4 Vaṭī, to be taken with 50 ml. warm water twice a day. 2. Mahā-Lakṣmī-Vilāsa Rasa: 1 to 2 Vaṭī, to be taken with honey sufficient to make a paste thrice a day. 3. Citraka-Harītakī Avaleha: 12 to 24 g., to be taken with 50 ml. warm water twice a day. 4. Saḍa-Bindu Taila or Aṇu Taila: Instil its 2 to 4 drops in the nose 3 to 4 times a day.
PATHYA: Laghu Āhāra, warm water, old Śāli (red variety of rice), seeds of Kulattha (dolichos bean) and Mudga (phaseolus bean); fruits of Paṭola (a variety of small cucumber-snake gourd) and Śigru (horse radish); Mūlaka (radish), bulb of Rasona (garlic) and Trikaṭu are the useful articles of diet for the patient of Pratiśyāya and Pīnasa.
APATHYA: Abhiṣyandi and Guru Dravya, incompatible items of food in diet are harmful for the patient of Pratiśyāya and Pīnasa. Bath, suppression of calls of nature, sleep in the day and on the floor and anger should be avoided.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Yapya Pānīlāga, Beng: Sardī, Dogr: Nasa Śula, Hind: Pīnasa, Kan: Hale, Negādi, Maly: Pinasam (Jala Doṣam), Mra: Paḍasen, Ori: Pīnasī, Ghā, Panj: Purāṇā Jukāma, Tam: Pīnasam, Nasṭpaṭṭa Salippu, Eng: Ozaena, sinusitis

Title: NETRA ROGA
Sanskrit: नेत्र रोग
INTRO: The signs, symptoms and treatment of common eye diseases are as follows:
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Cakura Vemāra, Beng: Netra Roga, Dogr: Netra Roga, Guj: Ankha Na Roga, Hind: Ānkha Ke Roga, Kan: Kannina Roga, Maly: Kannudenam, Mra: Dolyance Roga, Tam: Kannoy, Tel: Kanṭi Rogamulu, Eng: Diseases of the eye

Title: Netrābhiṣyanda
Sanskrit: नेत्राभिष्यन्द
SYMPTOMS: Netrābhiṣyanda is an eye disease characterised by the inflammation and reduces of the conjunctiva accompanied by various types of pain and watery discharge from the eye. Its other symptoms include feeling of stiffness, burning sensation, heaviness or itching in the eyes and headache. In some cases pus may also form.
TREATMENT: Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Take 100 ml. Dugdha (milk) Siddha (prepared) in the decoction of Triphalā twice a day. 2. Ghṛta (ghee) – 12 to 24 g. Siddha in the decoction of Daśamūla or of Triphalā is to be taken twice a day. 3. Dugdha (milk) – 100 to 250 ml. Siddha with root of Śatāvarī (wild asparagus) – 12 to 24 g. and juice of Ārdraka (ginger) – 7 ml. is to be taken thrice a day.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Cakunāmā, Beng: Chokha-othe, Dogr: Ānkha Duk Lona, Guj: Ānkha Dukhavī, Hind: Ānkha Ānā, Kan: Kannina Haruvudu, Maly: Kannu Novu, Mra: Dole Yene, Ori: Ākhī Dharivā, Panj: Akha Ānā, Tam: Kanvali, Kannoi, Tel: Kaṇḍlakalaka, Eng: Conjunctivitis

Title: Kukūṇaka
Sanskrit: कुकूणक
SYMPTOMS: Kukūṇaka is a disease of the eye lids of children which particularly occurs at the age of breast feeding. In this disease the eye lids of the patient are swollen, red and full of discharge and itching. The child constantly rubs his forehead, eyes and nose and is unable to see the sunlight.
TREATMENT: 1. Foment the eyes of the patient with decoction of fruit rind of Āmalakī (embelic myrobalan), fruit of Lakuca (a kind of bread fruit) and leaf of Jambū (jamun).
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Decoction of equal part of fruit rind of Harītakī (chebulic myrobalan), Drākṣā (raisin) and fruit of Pippalī (long pepper) – 7 to 14 ml. is to be taken twice a day by the feeding mother. 2. Decoction of equal part of fruit of Paṭola (a variety of small cucumber-snake gourd), root of Mustaka (motha), Drākṣā (raisin), stem of Guḍūcī and Triphalā – 7 to 14 ml. is to be taken twice a day by the feeding mother.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Kukuṇaka, Dogr: Kukrea, Hind: Āṁkho Kī Jhillī Kā Pradāha, Kan: Makkala Aregannu, Maly: Kuttikalkulla Kannunovu, Kannudinaim, Mra: Kukkuṇaka, Tam: Yoginisavy Thabitham, Tel: Āviri, Eng: Conjunctivitis

Title: Arma
Sanskrit: अर्म
SYMPTOMS: Arma is a disease in which a triangular patch of mucous membrane grown in the conjunctiva usually from the nasal side of the eye and spreads towards the pupil.
TREATMENT: Treatment
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Arma, Jālāpāḍa, Beng: Arma, Guj: Velā, Hind: Tiryak Dṛṣṭi, Maly: Kannila Māṁsa Valarcā, Mra: Arma, Ori: Paralā, Tam: Padalam, Eng: Pterygium

Title: Pothakī
Sanskrit: पोथकी
SYMPTOMS: Pothakī is a contagious disease chracterised by appearance of small and red coloured papules in the conjunctiva of the lid and accompanied by itching, pain and lacrimation.
TREATMENT: Treatment
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Cakura Khajuyati (Puthaki), Dogr: Mahroa, Kukrea, Guj: Āṅkha Nā Khila, Hind: Rohuā, Rohe, Kuthuvā, Kan: Pothaki, Maly: Pothaki Pitaka, Mra: Khupaya, Panj: Rohe, Tam: Timiram, Padalam, Tel: Durmāmsamu, Eng: Trachoma

Title: Añjananāmikā
Sanskrit: अञ्जननामिका
SYMPTOMS: Añjananāmikā is a disease characterized by the appearance of a small, soft and copper coloured pustules in the lid near a hair follicle accompanied by mild pain like pricking and burning sensation.
TREATMENT: A. While pus has not set in, any one of the following preparations may be used externally on the pustule. 1. Apply Lepa (plaster) of seed of Eraṇḍa (castor), Sphaṭika (alum) and Taṅkana (borax). 2. Foment with cotton dipped in warm water and properly squeezed. 3. Rub leaf of Badara (jujube) on the affected part. 4. After washing the hands, rub two fingers of one hand on the palm of the other the when hot foment the abscess. B. If the pus has set in remove it by pressing and treat it as Vraṇa.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Acinai, Ajanī, Dogr: Nahālī, Guj: Añjanī, Hind: Bilanī, Gondani, Kan: Kannakutike, Maly: Añjanapitaka, Mra: Rañjan Vādī, Ori: Aknire Alu Utraiba, Tam: Kankattai, Tel: Mella, Eng: Stye or style

Title: Pakṣmaśāta
Sanskrit: पक्ष्मशात
INTRO: Falling of the eye lashes accompanied by itching and burning sensation is known as Pakṣmaśāta.
TREATMENT: Treatment
REGIONAL NAMES:

Title: Naktāndhya (Night Blindness) Evaṁ Nakulāndhya (Nyctalope)
Sanskrit: नक्तान्ध्य एवं नकुलान्ध्य
SYMPTOMS: Naktāndhya: It is a disease caused by the vitiation of Kapha and in which the patient is unable to see in the night but can see very well in the day light. Nakulāndhya (Nyctalope): It is a variety of night blindness in which patient in the day also sees peculiar outlines and his eyes (iris) shine like that of a mangoose (Nakula).
TREATMENT: 1. Leaf of Jīvantī fried in ghee to be taken in 6 to 12 g. dose thrice a day. 2. Leaf juice (Svarasa) of Agastya –7 to 14 ml. or its Kalka – 12 to 24 g. fried in 10 g. ghee is to be taken twice a day. 3. Preparation described for Dṛṣṭi-Daurbalya may also be given to the patient of night blindness.
REGIONAL NAMES:

Title: Divāndhya
Sanskrit: दिवान्ध्य
SYMPTOMS: Divāndhya is a disease in which the patient sees all objects yellow or is unable to see in the day but can see things well in the night.
TREATMENT: Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Ghṛta Siddha is decoction of Triphalā is to be taken in 12 to 24 g. does with 150 ml. warm water thrice a day.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Dibā, Andhā, Beng: Divāndhya, Guj: Divas Main Andhadā Paṇse, Hind: Dinodhi, Maly: Pakal, Mra: Divandhale, Ori: Dinakānā, Tel: Guḍḍi, Eng: Day blindness

Title: Savraṇa Śukla Evaṁ Avraṇa Śukla
Sanskrit: सव्रण शुक्ल एवं अव्रण शुक्ल
SYMPTOMS: 1. Savraṇa Śukla: It is moderately deep minute ulcer of the cornea with little warm discharge and pain. 2. Avraṇa Śukla: Due to Abhiṣyanda (conjunctivitis) or ulcer, a whitish spot of varying thickness appears in the cornea and due to which the vision of the patient is impaired and he sees things cloudy and has the burning sensation, this condition is known as Avraṇa Śukla.
TREATMENT: 1. Decoction of rootb-bark of Nīśotha (turpeth) 7 to 14 ml. is to be taken with Ghṛta (ghee) – 12 to 24 g. thrice a day.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Khatpara, Baga Dadā, Badanayukta, Beng: Saborna-o-Aborana Sukla, Hind: Phula, Maly: Vraṇamullatun Vraṇa, Vraṇa Vellā, Millathathun Kannila, Mra: Savarna Evam Avarna Sukla, Ori: Akīnire Phuṭa Pādikā, Panj: Pholā, Tam: Kān Pu, Eng: Adherent leucoma

Title: Dṛṣṭi Daurbalya
Sanskrit: दृष्टि दौर्बल्य
SYMPTOMS: Blurred vision; patient in from of his eyes sees imaginary things like cobwebs, hair, flies, mosquito, circle etc; and to him objects look cloudy, are the initial symptoms. In advanced stage of the disease, far objects are seen near and near objects seen far off, and loss of acuteness in vision like inability to thread a needle are the common symptoms.
TREATMENT: Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Decoction of fruit of Meṣaśṛṅgī (Indian screw tree) – 14 to 28 ml., to be taken with 5 to 10 g. Ghṛta (ghee) twice a day. 2. Decoction of Triphalā – 14 to 28 ml. to be taken with 5 to 10 g. Ghṛta (ghee) and warm water thrice a day. 3. Make an Añjana of root of Punarnavā (pigweed) in Ghṛta (ghee) and apply in the eyes twice a day. 4. Leaf of Brāhmī fried in ghee is to be taken in 3 to 6 g. dose with 1 g. Saindhava or powdered leaf of Brāhmī – 3 to 6 g. is to be taken with meal twice a day.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Triphalā Cūrṇa: 2 to 6 g., to be taken with 12 to 24 g. honey thrice a day. 2. Triphalā Ghṛta: 12 to 24 g., to be taken with powder of Triphalā and root of Yaṣṭimadhu mixed in honey two times a day. 3. Saptāmṛta Lauha: 1 g., to be taken with honey and ghee two times a day.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Dṛṣṭi Durbalatā, Beng: Dristri Khinata, Dogr: Najara Kamjora, Hind: Nigāha Ki Kamī, Kan: Kannu Manju, Maly: Kajhchakkuravu, Mra: Dṛṣṭimānda Hoṇe, Panj: Najara Kamajora, Tam: Parvaikkurivy, Tel: Dṛṣṭi Durbalam, Eng: Weak eye sight

Title: Timira
Sanskrit: तिमिर
SYMPTOMS: Partial or complete opacity of the eye lens may be known as Timira. In its initial stage vision of the patient is impaired and he sees imaginary things like cobweb. With the progress of the disease impairment of vision also increases. In the last complete loss of vision may occur.
TREATMENT: Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Triphalā Cūrṇa – 6 to 12 g., to be taken with 12 to 24 g. Ghṛta (ghee) thrice a day. 2. Ghṛta Siddha with rhizome of Haridrā (turmeric) and root of Uśīra (khas) – 12 to 24 g., to be taken twice a day. 3. Equal part of powder of Triphalā, root of Yaṣṭimadhu (glycyrrhiza) – 3 to 6 g. to be taken with honey or Ghṛta (ghee) thrice a day. 4. Ghṛta Siddha with equal part of decoction of leaf of Paṭola (a variety of small cucumber-snake gourd), juice of Nimbū (lemon) and stem of Guḍūcī is to be taken in 12 to 25 g. done thrice a day. 5. Ghṛta Siddha with decoction of root-bark of Niśotha (turpeth) is to be taken in 12 to 24 g. dose with Daśamūla Kvātha – 14 to 28 ml., thrice a day. 6. Ghṛta Siddha with the decoction of root of Uśīra (khas), leaves of Pīpala, Plakṣa, Pārasapīpala and Udumbara (gular-fig) with Prakṣepa of powder of rhizome of Haridrā (turmeric) and root of Uśīra (khas) is to be taken in 12 to 24 g. dose twice a day.
PATHYA: Yava (barley), Śāli (red variety of rice), Mudga (phaseolus bean), Tikta Dravya; Purāṇa Ghṛta (old ghee), Karpūra (camphor), Candana (sandal), Añjana of Nārīdugdha (human milk) are useful for the patients of eye diseases.
APATHYA: Vidhāhī, Tīkṣṇa and Kaṭu Āhāra; Uṣṇa and Guru Dravya; sprouted grains, articles prepared from Taila, curd, sour, salt; fish, meat and wine; leaf of Badara (jujube); Kalinda (water melon fruit) are harmful for the patient of eye diseases. Suppression of emesis, urge of sleep and calls of nature; grief, sexual intercourse, tears; constant seeing of minute objects and sunrays; dust, smoke, excessive walking, meals in the late night should be avoided.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Andhā, Beng: Timira, Dogr: Pholā, Mottiyā, Guj: Motiyo, Hind: Motiyābinda, Kan: Pare Baruvudu, Maly: Timiram, Mra: Dṛṣṭi Doṣa, Motībindu, Ori: Motiābindu, Panj: Motiābinda, Tam: Kan. Kasam, Tel: Śuklālu Peruguṭa, Eng: Cataract

Title: PRAMEHA
Sanskrit: प्रमेह
INTRO: Prameha is a group of urinary disorders characterised by the passing of turbid urine in excessive quantity. Depending upon the causative factors, colour, consistency and quantity of urine etc, twenty types of Prameha have been described. Signs and symptoms of common varieties of Prameha and their treatment are as follows.
SYMPTOMS: 1. Udakameha: In Udakameha patient passes large quantity of cold, colourless, odourless and slightly turbid and slimy urine. 2. Śukrameha: In Śukrameha patient passes semen during urination, or semen mixed urine or discharges with slight sexual excitement even due to emotion. 3. Ikṣumeha: Ikṣumeha is a disease in which the patient passes urine containing sugar and which resembles with the juice of sugar cane. 4. Hastimeha: Patient of Hastimeha passes voluminous urine of slimy consistency continuously for a long time without any obstruction. 5. Madhumeha (Diabetes mellitus): All the Prameha of long duration or which are neglected leads to the condition known as Madhumeha (diabetes mellitus). It may also occur independently. In this disease patient passes sweet urine like honey and his sugar level of blood rises considerably above the normal limits.
TREATMENT: Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Fruit juice of Āmalakī (embelic myrobalan) – 14 to 28 ml. and juice of rhizome of Haridrā (turmeric) – 14 to 28 ml. to be taken thrice a day. 2. Decoction of equal part of Triphalā, roots of Dāruharidrā (barberry), Indravāruṇī (colocynth) and Mustaka (motha) – 14 to 28 ml., to be taken with 3 to 6 g. powdered rhizome of Haridrā (turmeric) twice a day. 3. Decoction of equal part of barks of Lodhra and Kaṭphala (boxmyrtle), fruit rind of Harītakī (chebulic myrobalan) and root of Mustaka (motha) – 14 to 28 ml., to be taken with 3 to 6 g. powdered rhizome of Haridrā (turmeric) twice a day. 4. Decoction of equal part of leaves of Paṭola (a variety of small cucumber – snake gourd) and Nimba (neem), fruit rind of Āmalakī (embelic myrobalan) and stem of Guḍūcī – 14 to 28 ml., to be taken thrice a day. 5. Decoction of equal part of roots of Mañjiṣṭhā (madder), Śālmalī (Indian silk cotton tree), Kuśa, Kāśa (sacred grass), and Dantī (wild croton) and whole plant of Dūrvā (doob grass) – 14 to 28 ml., to be taken thrice a day. 6. Decoction of equal part of wood of Devadāru (deodar), roots of Dāruharidrā (barberry) and Mustaka (motha) and fruit rind of Āmalakī (embelic myrobalan) – 14 to 28 ml., to be taken thrice a day. 7. Decoction of equal part of barks of Śveta Khadira (white acacia) and Rakta Khadira (khair) and nut of Pūga (areca) – 14 to 28 ml., to be taken thrice a day. 8. Powder of stem of Sārivā (Indian sarsaparilla) – 1 part, Tejapatra (tamala leaf) – 1 part and root of Yaṣṭimadhu (glycyrrhiza) – 1 part, to be taken in 1 g. dose with 50 to 100 ml. water twice a day.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Meha Roga, Beng: Prameha, Dogr: Meha, Dhāturoga, Guj: Dhāta Padvī, Hind: Prameha, Kan: Bahumūthra Roga, Maly: Prameha, Mutramojhivu, Mra: Bahumūtrata, Prameha, Tam: Muttranoggal, Tel: Pramehamu, Eng: Urimary disorders leading to diabetes mellitus

Title: Piṣṭameha
Sanskrit: पिष्टमेह
INTRO: In Piṣṭameha patient passes excessive quantity of urine containing suspension of whitish particles and has horripilation during micturation.
TREATMENT: Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Decoction of Agaru – 14 to 28 ml., to be taken twice a day.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: (for all types of Prameha) 1. Narasiṁha Cūrṇa: 1 to 3 g., to be taken with 100 to 250 ml. milk twice a day. 2. Śuddha (purified) Śilājatu: 1 g., to be taken with sufficient honey to make a paste twice a day. 3. Candrakalā Vaṭī: 1 to 2 Vaṭī, to be taken with 50 ml. water thrice a day. 4. Candraprabhā Vaṭī: 1 to 2 Vaṭī, to be taken with leaf-juice of Bimbī (scarlet fruited gourd) – 7 to 14 ml. thrice a day. 5. Māmajjaka – Ghana Vaṭī: 1 to 2 Vaṭī, to be taken with leaf-juice of Nimba (neem) – 7 to 14 ml., thrice a day. 6. Śilājatvādi Vaṭī: 1 to 2 Vaṭī, to be taken with 100 to 250 ml. milk thrice a day. 7. Śukramātrikā Vaṭī: 1 to 2 Vaṭī, to be taken with 100 to 250 ml. milk thrice a day. It is useful in Śukrameha. 8. Tārakeśvara Rasa: 60 to 250 mg., to be taken with honey sufficient to make a paste thrice a day. 9. Vaṅgeśvara Rasa: 120 to 250 mg., to be taken with honey sufficient to make a paste thrice a day. 10. Vasanta-Kusumākara Rasa: 1 Vaṭī, to be taken with honey sufficient to make a paste thrice a day. 11. Svarṇa Vaṅga: 120 to 250 mg., to be taken with 100 to 250 ml. milk thrice a day. 12. Vaṅgabhasma: 120 to 250 mg., to be taken with 100 to 250 ml. milk twice a day. 13. Gokṣurādi Guggulu (Prameha Adhikāra): 1 to 2 pills, to be taken with 100 to 250 ml. milk twice a day.
PATHYA: Seeds of Yava (barley), Godhūma (wheat), Kodrava (a variety of grain), Kaṅgunī (Italian millet), Mudga (phaselous bean), Kulattha (dolichos bean) and Āḍhakī (pigeon grain); fruit and leaf of Paṭola and Śigru (horse radish); fruits of Kāravellaka (bitter gourd), Udumbara (gular-fig), Kapittha (wood apple) and Jambu; leaf and stem of Guḍūcī and Triphalā are the useful articles of diet for the patient of Prameha.
APATHYA: Amla, Madhura and Lavaṇa Rasa; Navīna Anna (freshly harvested grains), rice, Ikṣu-Rasa (sugarcene juice), Guḍa (jaggery), curd, excessive ghee and oil are harmful for the patient of Prameha. Sedentary occupation, day sleep, suppression of urination, excessive diet, riding and walking should be avoided.

Title: Prameha Piḍakā
Sanskrit: प्रमेह पिडका
INTRO: The neglected patient of Prameha may develop various types of boil (Piḍakā) affecting joints, muscles, Marma, which are collectively known as Prameha Piḍakā. These Piḍakā may also develop in a patient who is not having Prameha. In that case causative factor is Duṣṭi of Meda. The brief description of each is as follows. 1. Śarāvikā: A Piḍakā with prominent periphery and depressed centre to known as Śarāvikā. 2. Sarṣapikā: A boil of the shape and size of white Sarṣapa (mustard) is called as Sarṣapikā. 3. Kacchapikā: A smooth Piḍakā like the back (dorsal) of tortoise with burning sensation is called as Kacchapikā. 4. Jālinī: The boil with extreme burning sensation and net work of capillaries is called as Jālinī. 5. Vinitā: Very painful, large pulpy, blue boil which generally appears on sides and abdomen is called Vinitā. 6. Putriṇī: A big boil having small pimples around it is known as Putriṇī. 7. Masūrikā: A boil having the shape and size resembling to that of Masūra (lentil) is known as Masūurikā. 8. Alaji: This is an acute condition in which many red and white coloured boils appear at a place. 9. Vidārikā: A round and hard boil looking like Vidāri-Kanda is known as Vidārikā. 10. Vidradhikā: A boil with the signs and symptoms of an abscess is known as Vidradhikā.
TREATMENT: 1. Sārivādyāsava: 14 to 28 ml., to be taken with equal quantity of water thrice a day after meal. 2. The boil should be treated in the inflammatory stage as Śotha, after bursting as Vraṇa or Vidradhi. 3. If the patient is suffering from Prameha, he should also be treated for the same.
PATHYA: Pathya described for Prameha may also be followed for the Prameha Piḍakā.
APATHYA: Abhiṣyandi, Rūkṣa, Tīkṣṇa and Duṣpācya (heavy) Dravya; bulbs of Rasona (garlic) and Palāṇḍu (onion); Matsya (fish) and Madya (wine) are harmful for the patient of Prameha Piḍakā. Suppression of natural urges, exposure to sun, hard exercise, sexual intercourse and awaking at night should be avoided.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Mehaja Braṇa, Beng: Mūtrameha Pīḍika, Guj: Pāthuna Upati, Hind: Prameha Pīḍikā, Maly: Prameha Kuru, Mra: Prameha Pīḍikā, Tam: Pirāmiyakkali, Tel: Rācapuṇḍu, Rācakurupu, Eng: Carbuncle

Title: PĀṆḌU ROGA
Sanskrit: पाण्डुरोग
INTRO: Pāṇḍu is a disease in which the colour of the patient changes to pale due to significant qualitative or quantitative reduction in the red blood cells of the blood (Rakta). Its prodromal symptoms are palpitation, dryness, absence of sweating and fatigue.
SYMPTOMS: Pallor, diminished digestive power, aversion of food, excessive salivation, fatigue, weakness, loss of body lustre, giddiness, irritability, fever, disliking for cold things, pain and cramps in limbs, heaviness in the body, breathlessness during exercise like climbing are the common signs and symptoms of Pāṇḍu Roga. Mṛd-Janya Pāṇḍu (Anemia due to Worm): in this type of anemia patient has oedema over cheeks, eyelids, pits of the eyes, legs etc; passes worms in the stool, and develops diarrhoea with mucus and blood in the stool.
TREATMENT: For Mṛd-Janya Pāṇḍu Roga, treatment described for Kṛmi Roga should also be given with the following general treatment of Pāṇḍu Roga (anemia).
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Maṇḍūra Bhasma: 1 g., to be taken with honey sufficient to make a pass thrice a day. 2. Punarnavādi Maṇḍūra: 1 g., to be taken with 100 to 250 ml. milk thrice a day. 3. Dhātrī Lauha: 2 to 4 pills, to be taken with 100 to 250 ml. milk twice a day. 4. Lohāsava: 14 to 28 ml., to be taken with equal quantity of water thrice a day after meal. 5. Kumāryāsava: 14 to 28 ml., to be taken with equal quantity of water thrice a day after meal. 6. Rohītakādyāriṣṭa: 14 to 28 ml. to be taken with equal quantity of water thrice a day after meal.
PATHYA: Godhūma (wheat), Yava (barley), Śāli variety of rice, Mudga (phaseolus bean), Masūra (lentil), Āḍhakī (pigeon pea); leaf and fruit of Paṭola (a variety of small cucumber – snake gourd), leaves of Taṇḍulīya (a variety of amaranth) and Punarnavā (pigweed), Gārjara (carrot); leaf and rhizome of Mūlaka (radish), fruit and tender leaf of Bṛhatī (yellow berried night shade), fruits of Kadali (banana), Jambū (jamun). Drākṣā (raisin or grape fruit), Āmalakī (embelic myrobalan), Dāḍima (pomegranate), Dṛḍhabīja (guava), Āmra (mango) and Papītā, buld of Rasona (garlic), rhizome of Haridrā (turmeric), Takra (butter milk) and curd are the useful articles of diet for the patients of Pāṇḍu Roga.
APATHYA: Lavaṇa and Amla Rasa, Guru Dravyas; seed of Satīna (pea), Māṣa (black phaseolus bean), leaf of Sarṣapa (mustard) and Madya (wine) are harmful for the patient of Pāṇḍu Roga. Excessive intake of water, exposure to sun, hard work, exercise, anger, excessive walking, suppression of calls of nature and blood letting should be avoided.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Pāṇḍu, Beng: Pāṇḍu, Dogr: Pāṇḍu, Phuśā, Hind: Raktālpa, Kan: Billicikolluva Roga, Maly: Vilarca, Mra: Pāṇḍu Roga, Ori: Cutāpāṇḍu, Tam: Sogai, Tel: Netturulekapovuṭa, Pālipovuṭa, Eng: Anaemia

Title: BĀLA-ROGA
Sanskrit: बालरोग
INTRO: The child cannot explain his ailments, therefore, following points may be useful for the diagnosis. 1. The severity of the pain can be judged from the intensity and continuity if his crying. 2. The part which child tries to touch constantly and if touched by others increases his crying, this means that part is affected. 3. In headache the child moves his head frequently, closes eyes, cries in the night and has loss of appetite and sleep. 4. If the child grinds his teeth, closes fist and takes breath with difficulty then it may be supposed that his lungs are affected. 5. Before the onset of fever, the child yawns, refuses the feed, suffers from excessive salivation and has hot face and cold feet. 6. Rumbling noises in the abdomen, vomiting, flatulance, cutting of mothers breast with teeth, bending of legs indicate that the child is having trouble in a abdomen. 7. If the child looks dazed and restless, it suggests that disturbance is due to retention of faeces, urine and flatus.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Śiśu Roga, Bālaka Roga, Beng: Bāla Roga, Dogr: Bāla Roga, Guj: Bāḍa Roga, Hind: Bālkon Ke Roga, Kan: Makkala Roga, Maly: Bāla Rogam, Mra: Bāla Roga, Śiśu Roga, Panj: Bāla Roga, Tam: Kujhandai Noy, Tel: Bāla Rogamulu, Pillala Rogamulu, Eng: Diseases of children and infants

Title: Bāla-Jvara
Sanskrit: बालज्वर
SYMPTOMS: Increase in temperature, constipation, loss of appetite, nausea, eructation, thirst, headache, fainting, laziness, fatigue, giddiness, emotional inhibition etc. are general signs are symptoms of Bāla Jvara.
TREATMENT: For dose please consult the table where the doses for children of different ages are described (Table 3).
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Ṣaḍaṅgapānīya: it is to be given frequently. 2. Decoction of equal part of root of Mustaka (motha), fruit rind of Harītakī (chebulic myrobalan), leaf of Paṭola (a variety of small cucumber-snake gourd) and root of Yaṣṭimadhu (glycyrrhiza), to be taken thrice a day.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Balacāturbhadra Cūrṇa: It is to be taken with honey thrice a day. 2. Godantī Bhasma: It is to be taken with honey, Dugdha (milk) or Ghṛta (ghee) twice a day.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Bālaka Jvara, Beng: Bālajvara, Guj: Chokrao Nā Tāva, Hind: Baccon Kā Bukhāra, Kan: Makkala Jvara, Maly: Bāla Jvaram, Mra: Bāla Jvara, Ori: Pilanku Jara, Panj: Bacciyān Dā Bukhāra, Tam: Kajhandai Jvaram, Eng: Infantile fever

Title: Bālātisāra
Sanskrit: बालातिसार
SYMPTOMS: The child passes pink, yellow, red or white coloured and foul smelling stool frequently with noise. The stool may be gritty, viscid, acidic, soapy, oily or mucoid depending upon the Doṣa involved. Patient suffers from thirst, burning sensation, horripilation and fainting. Ulceration and sepsis around the anus may also occur.
TREATMENT: Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Mix powder of Lājā (paddy pop) in the decoction of root of Bilva (bael). If is to be taken with 5 to 10 g. Śarkarā (raw sugar) thrice a day. 2. Powder of equal part of fruit pulp of Bilva (bael), flower of Dhātakī (downy grislea), rhizome of Bālaka (valerian), bark of Lodhra and Gaja-Pippalī, to be taken with honey two or three times a day. 3. Powder of equal part of Āmrātaka, fruit of Jambu (jamun) and fruit pulp of Āmra (mango), to be taken with honey thrice a day. 4. Decoction of 12 g. fruit pulps of Bilva (bael) and Āmra (mango) prepared in 250 ml. water and reduced to 125 ml. to be taken 2 to 3 times in a day. 5. Decoction of equal part of Śuṇṭhī (dried ginger), roots of Ativiṣā (Indian atees) and Mustaka (motha), rhizome of Bālaka (valerian) and Indrayava (kurchi seed) to be taken thrice a day. 6. Make a Vaṭī of 4 g. from equal part of powdered Rāla (oleo-resin of Śāla), Guḍa (jaggery) and Caṇaka (gram) and administer twice a day.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Bālātisāra, Beng: Bālātisāra, Guj: Baḍko Nā Jhāḍā, Hind: Baccon Ke Dasta, Kan: Makkala Bhedhi, Maly: Bālāthisāram, Mra: Bālātisāra, Ori: Bachera Jnada, Panj: Bacciyān De Dasta, Tam: Kujhandai Bedhī, Eng: Infantile diarrhea

Title: Bāla-Raktātisāra
Sanskrit: बाल-रक्तातिसार
SYMPTOMS: In this disease, the child passes yellow, blue or blood mixed loose stools with considerable loss of water. Other accompanied symptoms are thirst, burning sensation, fainting and ulceration of the anus.
TREATMENT: Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Take Svarasa (juice) of leaf of Bilva (bael) – 6 ml. and add to it powdered seed of Śveta Jīraka (cumin) – 8 g. and powdered Rāla (oleo-resin of Śāla) – 8 g. This is specially useful for infants passing blood in stool. The dose is according to the age. 2. Decoction of equal part of bark of Kuṭaja (kurchi), root of Ativiṣā (Indian atees), fruit pulp of Bilva (bael) and Śuddha Gairika (purified ochre), to be given according the age of the child. 3. Kṣīrapāka of equal part of fruit pulp of Bilva (bael), Indrayava (kurchi seed), Mocarasa (gum of silk cotton tree) and root of Mustaka (motha) prepared in Ajā Dugdha (goat’s milk), to be taken thrice a day.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Raktātisāra, Beng: Raktātisāra, Raktāmāsa, Guj: Lohī Nā Jhāḍā, Hind: Baccon Ke Khūnī Dasta, Kan: Makkala Rakta Bhedhī, Maly: Raktāthisāram, Mra: Raktī Julāba, Ori: Raktanogā, Tam: Raktha Bedhī, Eng: Dysentery

Title: Bāla-Jvarātisāra
Sanskrit: बाल-ज्वरातिसार
INTRO: Diarrhoea accompanied with fever is known as Jvarātisāra.
TREATMENT: 1. Balcāturbhadra Cūrṇa: It is to be taken twice or thrice a day.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Jvarātisāra, Beng: Jvarātisāra, Hind: Baccon Kā Bukhāra Ke Sātha Dasta, Guj: Tāva Man Thata Jhāḍā, Kan: Makkala Jvarakudida Bedhi, Maly: Jvarātisāram, Mra: Tapatīlajulāba, Tam: Jura Bedhī, Eng: Diarrhoea with fever

Title: Bāla-Pravāhikā
Sanskrit: बाल-प्रवाहिका
INTRO: In this disease the child passes small quantity of mucoid stool frequently with pain in abdomen.
TREATMENT: Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Fine powder of equal part of Kṛṣṇa Tila (black sesame) and root of Yaṣṭimadhu (glycyrrhiza), to be taken with honey three times in a day. 2. Rub Jātī-Phala (mace fruit) in water and make a Kalka (paste). It is to be taken thrice a day. 3. Īṣadagola Hima to be taken thrice a day.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Peṭā Kamoraṇī, Beng: Prabāhikā, Āmaśa, Guj: Maroḍo, Peciśa, Hind: Baccon Ke Peciśa, Kan: Makkala Āmāśanke, Maly: Vayarukaṭi, Mra: Āmānśa Julāba, Ori: Nalajnada, Nalaraktanda, Tam: Sītha Bedhī, Tel: Virecanamulu, Eng: Dysentery

Title: Bāla-Malāvarodha
Sanskrit: बाल-मलावरोध
INTRO: In this disease frequency of motion is reduced and the child passes formed and hard stool.
TREATMENT: Treatment
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Mala Baddha, Beng: Koṣṭha Baddhatā, Guj: Kabajiyāta, Hind: Kabja, Kan: Malakaṭṭu, Malabadhathe, Maly: Mala Bandham, Mra: Malāvarodha, Poṭa Phūgi, Ori: Jhaḍābanda, Tam: Malācacaikkal; Malakkattu, Mala Bantham, Tel: Mandamu, Eng: Constipation

Title: Bāla-Kāsa Evaṁ Śvāsa
Sanskrit: बाल-कास एवं श्वास
SYMPTOMS: Kāsa: Irritation in the chest and throat, cough with viscid expectoration, fever, dryness in the mouth, thirst, bitter vomit of yellow colour with bile, burning sensation in the whole body, coating of the throat with phlegm, lethargy, headache, aversion to food are the general signs and symptoms of Kāsa of children. Śvāsa: In Śvāsa the child has symptoms of cough, dyspenea, dryness in the mouth, sweating in the forehead and tension in the eyes.
TREATMENT: Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Fry rhizome of Haridrā (turmeric) in saucepan to near burning, then powder and given with honey thrice a day. 2. Śuddha Ṭaṅkaṇa (purified borax), to be taken with honey 2 to 3 times a day. 3. A segment of bulb of Rasona (garlic) boiled in water to be taken with 5 to 10 g. Śarkarā (raw sugar) twice a day. 4. Fine powder of equal part of root of Ativiṣā (Indian atees), fruit of Karkaṭaśṛṅgī (crab’s claw), and roots of Pippalī (long pepper) and Kuṣṭha (koot), to be taken with honey to make a paste thrice a day. 5. Fine powder of equal part of Drākṣā (raisin), leaf of Vāsā (vasaka) and fruit rind of Harītakī (chebulic myrobalan), to be taken with honey to make a paste thrice a day. 6. Fine powder of equal part of Drākṣā (raisin), whole plant of Durālabhā (camel’s thorn), fruit rind of Harītakī (chebulic myrobalan) and fruit of Pippalī (long pepper), to be taken with honey and Ghṛta (ghee) to make a paste thrice a day.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Bālacāturbhadra Cūrṇa: It is to be given twice a day.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Kāhā Śvāsā, Beng: Śvāsakāsa, Dogr: Mangi Dena, Guj: Damā Aṇe Khāṅsī, Hind: Khāṅsī, Sānsa, Kan: Kemmu, Dammu, Maly: Cumayum Valium, Mra: Damā Khoklā, Tam: Trumal, Iruppu, Eng: Cough and asthma

Title: Kukkura-Kāsa
Sanskrit: कुक्कुरकास
SYMPTOMS: Kukkura-Kāsa is a disease which is frequent in children and characterised by a peculiar paroxysm of cough ending in a loud whooping inspiration. Other symptoms are pain in the chest, sides and abdomen, headache and feeble voice.
TREATMENT: Specific treatment for the patients of whooping cough has been described along with the treatment of Śuṣka Kāsa of adult. Treatment recommended for Śvāsa and Kāsa of children may also be given to the patient of Kukkura-Kāsa.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Vātajakāsa, Beng: Bātaja Kāsa, Dogr: Sūkī Kaṅga, Guj: Vāntiyo Modiādaraśā, Hind: Kukkura Khānsi, Kālī Khānsi, Kan: Ona Kemmu, Maly: Varaṭṭu Cūma, Mra: Vātika Khoklā, Ori: Lanārakāsa, Panj: Kāli Khanga, Tam: Kakkuvanirumal, Tel: Korintadaggu, Eng: Whooping cough

Title: Bāla-Yakṛt Evaṁ Plīha Vṛddhi
Sanskrit: बाल-यकृत एवं प्लीह वृद्धि
SYMPTOMS: Aversion to food, dyspepsia, thirst, loss of taste, retention of flatus, constipation, drowsiness, lassitude, mild fever, cough, loss of weight, pain in joint and distension of abdomen with appearance of blue or yellow coloured veins. The liver lies in the right side and spleen lies in the left side and their enlargement as the case may be occur in the respective side of the abdomen.
TREATMENT: Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Powder of equal part of fruit of Pippalī (long pepper) and fruit rind of Harītakī (chebulic myrobalan), and 1/4th of Viḍa Lavaṇa (a variety of salt), to be taken with warm water thrice a day. 2. Powder of equal part of bark of Rohītaka and fruit rind of Harītakī (chebulic myrobalan), to be taken with Gomūtra (cow’s urine) and water three times a day. 3. Decoction of bark of Śigru, to be taken with powder of Saindhava (rock salt) and root of Citraka (leadwort) thrice a day.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Yakṛdāri Lauha: It is to be taken thrice a day. 2. Kumāryāsava: It is to be taken with equal quantity of water twice a day after feed. 3. Abhayāriṣṭa: to be taken with equal quantity of water twice a day after feed. 4. Rohitakāriṣṭa: to be taken with equal quantity of water twice a day after feed.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Jakṛta Plīhāra, Beng: Jakṛta Plīhā Bṛdhi, Dogr: Jigra Bāḍanā, Guj: Baḍovridhi, Tillī Ane Jigara Baḍhvūṅa, Hind: Jigara Baḍhanā; Tillī Baḍhanā, Maly: Yakṛta Plīha Valarcā, Mra: Yakṛta Plīha Vṛddhi, Tam: Kallirala, Mannīrala Valarcācī, Tel: Ānasvyādhi, Eng: Enlargment of liver and spleen, infantile cirrhosis

Title: Bāla Chardi
Sanskrit: बाल छर्दि
TREATMENT: Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Powder of equal part of fruit of Pippalī (long pepper) and Marica (black pepper), to be taken with fruit-juice of Āmalakī (embelic myrobalan) and honey thrice a day. 2. Powder of wood of Śveta Candana (white sandal) – 1 part and fruit rind of Āmalakī (embelic myrobalan) – 4 parts, to be taken with honey twice a day. 3. Power of equal part of seed of Ciñcā (tamarind). Lājā (pop of paddy) and Saindhava (rock-salt), to be taken with honey thrice a day. 4. Powder of equal part of fruit rind of Āmalakī (embelic myrobalan), seed of Jīraka (cumin), Lavaṅga (clove), Marica (black pepper) and Śarkarā (raw sugar), to be taken with honey thrice a day. 5. Śīta Kaṣāya of fruit rind of Āmalakī (embelic myrobalan), Drākṣā (raisin), Śarkarā (raw sugar) and honey in four times of its weight of water to be taken as required.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Yavānī-Arka: It is to be taken twice a day. 2. Kapardikā Bhasma: It is to be taken with honey twice a day. 3. Śaṅkha Bhasma: It is to be taken with honey twice a day. 4. Mayūra-Puccha Bhasma: It is to be taken with honey three times a day. For Dugdha Vamana (vomiting of feed) 1. Powder of equal part of decorticated seed (Majjā) of Āmalakī (embelic myrobalan) and Saindhava (rock-salt), to be taken with honey thrice a day. 2. Svarjikā-Kṣāra: It is to be taken with honey twice a day.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Vomi, Beng: Bami, Dogr: Ulṭṭī, Guj: Ulṭī, Hind: Ulṭī, Kan: Vānti, Maly: Chardhi, Mra: Ulṭī, Vanti, Ori: Banti, Tam: Vandhi, Tel: Vāntulu, Eng: Vomiting

Title: Bāla-Udaraśūla
Sanskrit: बाल उदरशूल
TREATMENT: Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Powder of equal part of Śuṇṭhī (dried ginger), Saindhava (rock-salt), seed of Elā (cardamom), Bhāraṅgī and Ghṛta Bhṛṣṭa Hiṅgu, to be taken with water three times a day.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Daśamūla-Kvātha: It is to be taken with Eraṇḍa Taila (castor oil) three times a day.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Peṭārā Viṣa, Beng: Peṭa Byathā, Udara Śūla, Dogr: Peḍa Derda, Guj: Peṭno Dukhavo, Hind: Peṭa Darda, Kan: Hoṭṭe Novu, Maly: Vayaṭṭunovu, Mra: Poṭa Dūkhī, Ori: Peṭatānibā, Tam: Vayitruvali, Eng: Pain in abdomen

Title: Phakka-Roga
Sanskrit: फक्करोग
TREATMENT: Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Kṣīra-Pāka prepared from the equal part of roots of Rāsnā (Indian groundsel), Yaṣṭimadhu (glycyrrhiza), Punarnavā (pigweed), Eraṇḍa (castor) and Ekaparṇī-Banasaṭi, fruits of Miśreyā (fennel), Drākṣā (raisin) and Pīlū and root bark of Trivṛt (turpeth), to be taken twice a day.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Laghu-Vasanta-Mālatī: It is to be taken with honey thrice a day. 2. Kacchapa-Pṛṣṭa Bhasma: It is to be taken with honey thrice a day. 3. Karkaṭaka Bhasma: It is to be taken with honey thrice a day. 4. Pravāla Pañcāmṛta: It is to be taken with honey thrice a day. 5. Śatāvaryādi-Avaleha: It is to be taken with butter two or three times a day. 6. Pravāla-Bhasma or Muktā-Śukti Bhasma: it is to be taken three times a day.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Phakka Roga, Dogr: Sokaḍā, Guj: Sukho Roga, Hind: Sūkhā Roga, Kan: Alle Roga, Kash: Kūtilavāta, Maly: Kānā, Mra: Mudāduṣa, Tam: Kannam kannai, Tel: Pittabaruṭā, Eng: Rickets

Title: Pārigarbhika
Sanskrit: पारिगर्भिक
INTRO: The breast feeding by a woman who is pregnant causes in the child, the symptoms like vomiting, loss of appetite, indigestion, enlargement of the abdomen, drowsiness, loss of weight, cough and illusion and this condition is known as Pārigarbhika.
TREATMENT: Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Powder of equal part of fruit rind of Harītakī (chebulic myrobalan) and Tvak-Dālacīnī (cinnamon bark), to be taken with honey thrice a day. 2. Powder of equal part of fruits of Yavānī (ptychotis) and Kṛṣṇa Jīraka (caraway) and Śuṇṭhī (dried ginger), to be taken with honey thrice a day.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Pravāla Bhasma: it is to be taken with honey three times a day.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Pāyālāgā Roga, Guj: Pārāgoḍo, Hind: Garbhiṇī Stanyapāna Janya Roga, Kan: Earogolluvike, Maly: Garbhiṇīyuṭe Paluṭikkuna Thinalundavunna Chardhi, Mra: Pārigarbhika, Garodara, Matecā Dudhaṇe Honāra Roga, Ori: Lairaṭā, Tam: Charalai

Title: Tālupāta
Sanskrit: तालुपात
SYMPTOMS: In this disease the floor of the palate sinks down causing difficulty in sucking of milk by the child and this condition is known as Tālupāta. Other symptoms are vomiting, watery motions, thirst and pain in eyes, throat and mouth. The neck of the child becomes flaccid and he refuses to mother’s teat.
TREATMENT: Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Pañcāmṛta Miśraṇa, to be taken with honey twice a day.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Tālupāta, Guj: Tadupādavan, Gaḍupādavan, Hind: Tālugiranā, Kan: Angala Hunnū, Maly: Thonṭā Pakam, Thonta Pajhupu, Mra: Tālupāta, Tam: Annaharācī, Tel: Noṭipūta

Title: BHAGANDARA
Sanskrit: भगन्दर
INTRO: Appearance of a deep rooted boil without any opening within the two fingers around the anus with pain and fever is known as Bhagandara-Piḍakā (anorectal abscess). When this ano-rectal abscess breaks through the perineum, anus or bladder and have an opening then it is called Bhagandara (fistula-in-ano).
SYMPTOMS: Itching, pain in the waist, burning sensation and inflammation near the anus are the symptoms and signs which patient has before the appearing of Bhagandara. After forming Bhagandara intense pain, oozing of reddish frothy discharge from the channels are the main signs and symptoms.
TREATMENT: Generally the disease required surgical intervention. Application of Kṣāra Sūtra by an expert is very successful and chances of recurrence are rare, As soon as the swelling appears care should be taken that pus does not form. After the formation of pus, it should be treated as Vraṇa. Following oral preparations are useful if taken along with the application of Kṣāra Sūtra or surgical treatment.
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Decoction of wood of Khadira (khair) as much as possible for quenching thirst. 2. Decoction of equal part of fruit rinds of Harītakī (chebulic myrobalan), Vibhītaka (balerie myrobalan) and Āmalakī (embelic myrobalan), Śuddha Guggulu, Viḍaṅga, Śuddha Lākṣa (purified lac) – 14 to 28 ml. to be taken thrice a day. 3. Take Triphalā – 12 g., Śuddha Guggulu – 60 g. and Ghṛta (ghee) 10 g. and make pills of 1 g.; one pill is to be taken twice a day with warm water.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Pañca Tikta Ghṛta: 12 to 24 g. to be taken with 100 to 250 ml. milk thrice a day.
PATHYA: Mudga (phaseolus bean); leaf of Vāstūka (a variety of chenopodium) and other leafy vegetables, light foods are useful for the patient of Bhagandara.
APATHYA: Incompatible items of food in diet, too frequent meals, irregular gaps in meals, exercise and riding are harmful for the patient of Bhagandara (fistula-in-ano).
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Nalighā, Beng: Bhagandara, Dogr: Geḍu Vidradhi, Bhagandara, Guj: Bhagandara, Hind: Bhagandara, Kan: Jaraḍi Hunnu, Nāli Hunnu, Maly: Mūlanāli Vraṇam, Mra: Bhagandara, Ori: Bhagandara, Tam: Pavuthra Noy, Tel: Bhagandaramu, Eng: Fistula-in-ano

Title: BHRAMA
Sanskrit: भ्रम
INTRO: Bhrama is a condition in which the patient has a sensation of unsteadiness with a feeling of movements within the head.
TREATMENT: During the attack wash the face and head of the patient with cold water. In case of frequent attacks of prolonged duration, a specialist may be consulted and blood pressure may also be get checked.
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Decoction prepared from Bṛhat Pañca Mūla to be taken in 14 to 28 ml. dose with 5 to 10 g. honey thrice a day. 2. Decoction prepared from Daśamūla to be taken in 14 to 28 ml. dose with 5 to 10 g. honey thrice a day. 3. Decoction prepared from the whole plant of Durālabhā (camel’s thorn) to be taken in 14 to 28 ml. dose with milk and 5 to 10 g. Śarkarā (raw sugar) at night. 4. In case of Udarastha Vāyu, take 1 g. each of bulb of Rasona (garlic), Ārdraka (ginger) and powdered root of Pippalī with honey twice a day or Trikaṭu 3 g. with honey twice a day.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Rasa Sindūra: 120 to 250 mg. to be taken with honey to make a paste twice a day. 2. Jahara-Moharā Piṣṭī: 120 to 250 mg. to be taken with honey to make a paste thrice a day. 3. Haritāśma Piṣṭī: 120 to 250 mg. to be taken with honey to make a paste thrice a day. 4. Śatāvaryādi Ghṛta: 12 to 24 g. to be taken with 100 to 250 ml. milk thrice a day. 5. Śārasvatāriṣṭa: 14 to 28 ml. to be taken with equal part of water thrice a day after meal. 6. Balāriṣṭa: 14 to 28 ml. to be taken with equal part of water after meal thrice a day. 7. In case attack sets in after feeling of vacantness in the head, weakness and depression or Udarastha Vāyu then 2 pills of Agnituṇḍī Vaṭī to be taken with 100 to 250 ml. milk twice a day. 8. In Udarastha Vāyu, Makaramuṣṭī Yoga may be taken in 120 to 250 mg. dose with 100 to 250 ml. milk twice a day.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Murghurāni Candrāyaṇa, Dogr: Cakkar, Guj: Cakkara, Hind: Sara Cakarānā, Kan: Teletirugū, Maly: Talacuṭṭal, Mra: Cakkara Yeṇe, Garane, Ori: Munḍabhrama, Panj: Cakkara, Tam: Thalai Cehutrāl, Tel: Talatiruguṭa, Eng: Giddiness

Title: MADĀTYAYA
Sanskrit: मदात्यय
INTRO: Madātyaya is a condition caused by the excessive use of alcohol. Signs, symptoms and treatment of the diseases caused by excessive use of alcohol viz. Madātyaya, Paramada and Pānājīrṇa are as follows.
SYMPTOMS: Madātyaya: Nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, thirst, diarrhoea, torpor, incoherent talk, loss of sleep, hiccough, dyspnoea, tremors in the head, burning sensation, perspiration, giddiness and fainting are the general signs and symptoms of Madātyaya. Paramada: Heaviness in the body, loss of taste, aversion to food, thirst, pain in joints, headache, torpor and retention of faeces and urine are the symptoms of Paramada. Pānājīrṇa: Acute distension of abdomen, burning sensation, nausea and vomiting are the signs and symptoms of Pānājīrṇa.
TREATMENT: Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Pānaka of Drākṣā (raisin or grape fruit), fruit of Kapittha (wood apple), fruit juice of Dāḍima (pomegranate) to be taken with Śarkarā (raw sugar) thrice a day. 2. Pānaka of Drākṣā (raisin or grape fruit), fruits of Kharjūra (date), Piṇḍakharjūra (a variety of date) and Ciñcā (tamarind), fruit pulp of Āragvadha (cassia). Seed of Dāḍima (pomegranate), fruits of Parūṣaka (asiatic grewia), Bījapūra (lemon) and Yavānī (ptychotis), and fruit juice of Āmalakī (embelic myrobalan) to be taken thrice a day.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Kalyāṇa Ghṛta: 12 to 24 g. to be taken with 100 to 250 ml. milk thrice a day.
PATHYA: Ṣaṣṭi (a variety of rice), Yava (barley), Māṣa (black phaseolus bean), Godhūma (wheat), Satīna (pea); leaf of Taṇḍulīyaka (a variety of amaranth), leaf and fruit of Paṭola (a variety of small cucumber-snake gourd), fruits of Bījapūra (Lemon), Kharjūra (date), Parūṣaka (asiatic grewia) and Dāḍima (pomegranate); fruit juice of Āmalakī (embelic myrobalan); Drākṣā (raisin or grape fruit), fruit of Nārikela (coconut), Dugdha (Milk) and Purāṇa Ghṛta (old ghee) are the useful articles of diet for the patient of Madātyaya.
APATHYA: Svedana, Añjana, brushing the teeth, Tambūla and smoking are harmful for the patient of Madātyaya.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Madapī, Dogr: Naśā, Guj: Naśo, Hind: Mada, Kan: Kuḍitādā Amālū, Maly: Madya Jata Rogam, Mra: Kaipha, Dhundī, Tam: Madhuveri, Tel: Tappatragūṭa, Eng: Alcoholism

Title: MASŪRIKĀ
Sanskrit: मसूरिका
INTRO: Masūrikā (small pox) is a highly contagious disease characterised by abrupt onset of high fever with appearance of general eruptions on the third day, which pass through the stages of papule, vesicle, pustule and scale with subsequent scarring.
SYMPTOMS: Sudden onset of high fever with shivering, loss of appetite, bodyache, restlessness, giddiness, gray coloured face, and redness of the eyes are the initial symptoms. After 2 days temperature falls and on the third day Masūra (lentil) like eruptions first appear on the forehead and front of the wrist followed by eruptions on the whole body, but least on the chest, abdomen, groins and legs. Each vesicle enlarges and by the seventh or eighth day it becomes pustular. In the second week secondary suppurative fever may occur. In third week, the lesions begin to dry and after which the scabs are shedded.
TREATMENT: In Masūrikā (small pox) if infection of the eyes, throat and lungs occurs, then a specialist should immediately be consulted.
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Decoction of Nāgabalā and root of Yaṣṭimadhu (glycyrrhiza) to be used for Pariṣeka (fomentation) of eyes. 2. Kajjalī of Śuddha Pārada (mercury) – 1 part and Śuddha Gandhaka (sulphur) – 2 parts to be taken in 60 to 120 mg. dose with leaf juice of Tambūla (betel) twice a day.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Amṛtādi Kvātha: 14 to 28 ml. to be taken thrice a day. 2. Khadirāṣṭaka Kvātha: 14 to 28 ml. to be taken thrice a day. 3. Nimbādi Kvātha: 14 to 28 ml. to be taken thrice a day. 4. Paṭolādi Kvātha: 14 to 28 ml. to be taken thrice a day. 5. Triphalā Cūrṇa: 3 to 6 g. and Śuddha Guggulu 3 to 6 g. to be taken thrice a day.
PATHYA: It is better to keep the patient on milk or liquid diet. Godhūma (wheat), Mudga (phaseolus bean), Masūra (lentil), Tuvarī (pigeon pea); fruits of Kāravellaka (bitter gourd fruit), Paṭola (a variety of small cucumber-snake gourd), Dāḍima (pomegranate), Drākṣā (raisin or grape fruit) and Āmalakī (embelic myrobalan) may also be given taking in view the stage of the disease.
APATHYA: Guru Anna, wine, Kulattha (dolichos bean), Māṣa (black phaseolus bean) and Tila (sesame) are harmful for the patient of Masūrikā. Exposure to heat, sun and cold wind, sitting up at night and walking should be avoided.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Basanta, Śītalā, Beng: Basanta, Dogr: Modha, Guj: Śītalā, Mātā, Hind: Mātā, Kan: Sidibū, Maly: Masūrī, Vasuri, Mra: Devī, Panj: Mātā, Tam: Ammai Noy, Tel: Masūrijāḍyamu, Eng: Smallpox

Title: MŪRCCHĀ EVAṀ SANYĀSA
Sanskrit: मूर्च्छा एवं सन्यास
INTRO: Mūrcchā is a disease characterized by the transient loss of consciousness and after sometime the patient may become conscious even without treatment.
TREATMENT: A. At the time of Attack 1. Give Nasya of powdered bark of Kaṭphala (box myrtle). 2. Rasa-Sindūra-60 to 250 mg. or Kastūrī – 7.5 to 15 mg. to be given sublingually. B. Between the Attacks 1. Decoction of whole plant of Yavāsā (camel’s thorn) – 14 to 28 ml. to be taken with Ghṛta (ghee) – 10 g. twice a day. 2. Triphalā Cūrṇa – 1 to 3 g. to be taken with equal quantity of Guḍa (jaggery) and Ārdraka (fresh ginger) thrice a day. 3. Kalka (paste) of root and stem of Kamala (lotus), fruit of Pippalī, fruit rind of Harītakī (chebulic myrobalan) prepared in water to be taken in 12 to 24 g. dose with honey thrice a day. 4. Kṣīrapāka prepared from the powder of equal part of roots of Śatāvarī (wild asparagus) and Balā (country mallow), and Drākṣā (raisin or grape fruit) – 100 to 200 ml. to be taken with Śarkarā (raw sugar) thrice a day. 5. Powder of equal part of Badara Majjā (jujube seed decorticated), Marica (black pepper), root of Uśīra (khas), Nāgakeśara (Indian iron wood tree stemen) – 3 to 6 g. to be taken with cold water thrice a day. 6. Pānaka of leaf of Brāhmī (Indian pennywort), wood of Candana (sandal), root of Uśīra (khas), Karpūra (camphor), and Keśara (saffron) to be taken twice a day. 7. Candrāvaleha – 10 g. to be taken with 100 to 250 ml. milk thrice a day.
PATHYA: Rakta Śāli (red variety of rice), Taṇḍula (rice), Mudga (phaseolus bean), Satīna (pea), Yava (barley); Dugdha (milk); fruit of Dāḍima (pomegranate); soup of meat of wild animals and birds are the useful articles of diet for the patient of Mūrcchā.
APATHYA: Kaṭu Dravya, leaf of Sarṣapa (mustard), Tambūla Patra (betel leaf), Takra (butter milk), are harmful for the patient of Mūrcchā. Scanty intake of water, walking in the sun, sexual intercourse and suppression of calls of nature and urge to sleep should be avoided.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Mūrchā, Beng: Mūrchā, Dogr: Ye, Guj: Besudha Thāvuṅa, Hind: Mūrchā, Behośī, Kan: Jnānāppavuḍu, Maly: Ormayillayma, Mohalasyam, Mra: Besudhī, Ori: Kānpāṭi Pādiyibā Monā, Panj: Behosī, Tam: Mayakkan, Tel: Mūrcha, Eng: Syncope

Title: Sanyāsa
Sanskrit: सन्यास
INTRO: Sanyāsa is a very deep type of unconsciousness and requires immediate treatment to make the patient conscious. In this condition patient lies like a dead or a log of wood.
TREATMENT: Following external measures may be tried as a first aid and a specialist should be consulted as early as possible.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Sanyaṅsa, Beng: Sanyaṅsa, Guj: Bebhāna, Hind: Murchā, Kan: Sañjñā Nāśa, Maly: Gurutharā, Mohalasyam, Mra: Gambhīra Besudhi, Tam: Murchai, Tel: Kāki Somma, Eng: Coma

Title: MUKHA ROGA
Sanskrit: मुख रोग
INTRO: Mukha Roga are the diseases of oral cavity which occur at the seven sites viz. lips, gums, teeth, tongue, palate, throat and whole oral cavity. Signs, symptoms and treatment of the commonly occurring oral diseases are as follows.

Title: Oṣṭha Roga (Diseases of Lip)
Sanskrit: ओष्ठ रोग
SYMPTOMS: According to Doṣa involved the lips may become rough, hard, rigid, chaffed; or appearing of painful or painless pimples on lips with burning sensation and sepsis.
TREATMENT: Treatment
