Title: Danta-Mūla Roga
Sanskrit: दन्तमूल रोग
INTRO: A boil which appears at the root of the teeth causing intense inflammation is known as Dantappuṭaka. In this disease discharge of pus and blood occur from the root of the teeth, thereby infecting the alveolar tissue leading to looseness of the teeth and foul smelling. Sauṣira is a disease characterized by the inflammation and pain of the gums and excessive salivation.
TREATMENT: Treatment Treatment 1. Mouth wash (Kavala) with the decoction of Valkala (bark) of Pañcakṣīri.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Triphalā Guggulu: 4 to 8 g. to be taken with warm water twice a day.
REGIONAL NAMES:

Title: Danta Roga
Sanskrit: दन्त रोग
INTRO: In this condition an additional tooth comes up between the age of 17 and 21 years with intense pain which subsides as soon as the tooth emerges. On account of vitiation of Vāta a black cavity is formed in the tooth causing its decay and which leads to inflammation, discharge and looseness of the tooth and patient have acute pain in the tooth. In this condition the teeth do not tolerate cold, rough and acid substances, and strong wind. Hard insoluble deposit upon the teeth specially at the junction of the gum and teeth is known as Danta-Śarkarā.
TREATMENT: Treatment Gaṇḍūṣa of any of the following preparations 1. Take decoction of equal part of whole plant of Bṛhatī and Kaṇṭakārī, bark of Bhūkadamba (smaller kadam) and root of Eraṇḍa (castor), add to it Tila Taila (gingelly oil) – one fourth part, and use as Gaṇḍūṣa. 2. Solution of Yavakṣāra – 1 g. in 50 ml. water. 3. Fill cavity of the tooth with Hiṅgu (asafoetida) fried in ghee. 4. Apply Lavaṅga Taila (clove oil) on the tooth. 5. Apply Irimedādi Taila on the tooth. Treatment Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Decoction of equal part of Saptaparṇa, root of Uśīra (khas), Rohītaka, leaf of Paṭola (a variety of small cucumber-snake gourd), roots of Mustaka (motha) and Yaṣṭimadhu (glycyrrhiza), and fruit pulp or Āragvadha (cassia) – 14 to 28 ml. to be taken thrice a day.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Khadirādi Vaṭī: 1 to 2 Vaṭī for sucking.
PATHYA: Kaṭu and Tikta Dravya; seeds of Kaṅgu (Italian millet), Śyāmā (a variety of millet), Tṛṇa Dhānya (millets of different types), Yava (barley), Mudga (phaseolus bean), Kulattha (dolichos bean), and Methikā (fenugreek seed); ghee; root of Śatāvarī (wild asparagus), leaf and fruit of Paṭola (a variety of small cucumber-snake gourd), Mūlaka (radish), fruit of Kāravellaka (bitter gourd), leaf of Tāmbūla (betel) are the useful articles of diet for the diseases of oral cavity (Mukha-Roga).
APATHYA: Rūkṣa Anna; Amla, Guru and Abhiṣyaṇdi Dravya, Māṣa (black phaseolus bean), curd, milk and Guḍa (jaggery) are harmful for the patients of Mukha Roga. Brushing of teeth, chewing of hard substances, lying on the belly day sleep, fish, meat of wild animals should be avoided.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Dāhapoke Khoyā, Beng: Dānte Hoke, Dogr: Kodantā, Guj: Dānta Sarvuṅ, Hind: Dānta Men Kīḍā Laganā, Kan: Huluku, Hallu, Maly: Pujhu Pallu, Mra: Dānta Kiḍāṇe, Ori: Dānta Pākā Kaṭibā, Tam: Soththa ippal, Tel: Pippi Pannu, Eng: Caries of the teeth

Title: MŪTRA ROGA
Sanskrit: मूत्ररोग
INTRO: The signs, symptoms and treatment of the urinary disorders like Mūtra Kṛcchra, Mūtrāghāta, Vasti-Kunḍalikā and Rakta-Meha are as follows.
REGIONAL NAMES: Guj: Peśāba Ni Bimārī, Hind: Mūtra Ke Roga, Maly: Mūtra Rogam, Panj: Peśāba De Roga, Tam: Sirunīra Nogal, Eng: Diseases of the urinary system

Title: Mūtra Kṛcchra
Sanskrit: मूत्रकृच्छ्र
INTRO: Mūtra Kṛcchra is a condition resulting from various causes leading to painful micturation.
SYMPTOMS: In this condition the patient passes frequently small quantity of urine with difficulty, pain and burning sensation. The urine may also contain blood.
TREATMENT: Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Equal part of Śarkarā (raw sugar) and Yavakṣāra to be taken in 2 g. dose with 50 ml. water thrice a day. 1. Powdered fruit of Gokṣura (smaller caltrops) - 3 to 6 g. to be taken with 1 g. Yavakṣāra and 50 ml. water thrice a day. 2. Decoction of equal part of Tṛṇa Pañcamūla - 14 to 28 ml. to be taken thrice a day. 3. Decoction of equal part of fruits of Gokṣuru (small caltrops) and Dhānyaka (coriander) - 14 to 28 ml. to be taken thrice a day. 4. Kṣira Pāka of stem of Guḍūcī, Śuṇṭhi (dried ginger), fruit rind of Āmalakī (embelic myrobalan) and fruit of Gokṣuru (small caltrops) – 250 ml. to be taken twice a day. 5. Make Kalka of equal part of fruit rind of Harītakī (chebulic myrobalan), stem of Dāruharidrā (barberry), root of Yaṣṭimadhu (glycyrrhiza). Its 12 to 24 g. to be taken with Taṇḍulodaka (rice washing) -100 to 250 ml. thrice a day. 6. Make powder of seed of Elā (lesser cardamom) - 1 part, rhizome of Pāṣṇabheda (saxifrage) - 1 part, Śuddha Śilājatu - 1/2/ part, fruit of Pippalī (long pepper)- 1/2 part. Its 3 to 6 g. to be taken with 100 to 250 ml. Taṇḍulodaka (rice washing) thrice a day 7. Make fine powder of 12 to 24 g. seed of Karkaṭī (cucumber), bruise in Kāñjī. It is to be taken with 1 g. Saindhava (rock-salt) thrice a day.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Elādi Cūrṇa: 1 to 2 g. to be taken with honey to make a paste thrice a day. 2. Śuddha Śilājatu: 500 mg. to 1 g. to be taken with honey to make a past twice a day. 3. Tārakeśvara Rasa: 60 to 120 mg. to be taken with honey to make a paste thrice a day. 4. Candraprabhā Vaṭi: 1 to 2 Vaṭī to be taken with milk thrice a day. 5. Pravāla Bhasma: 60 to 250 mg. to be taken with 100 to 250 ml. Taṇḍulodaka (rice washing) twice a day. 6. Śatāvari Ghṛta: 12 to 24 g. to be taken with 5 to 10 g. Śarakarā (raw sugar) twice a day.
PATHYA: Purāṇa Śāli (old rice), Mudga (phaseolus bean), Yava (barley); Takra (butter milk), curd, ghee, cold water; fruits of Kūśmāṇḍa (a variety of pumpkin gourd-white gourd), Āmalakī (embelic myrobalan), Kharjūra (date) and leaf pith of Ghṛta-Kumarī (aloe) are the useful articles of diet for the patient of Mūtra Kṛccra.
APATHYA: Rūkṣa and Amla Dravya; Lavaṇa Rasa; leaves of Tāmbūla (betel), Ārdraka (ginger), Hiṅgu (asafeotida), leaves of Sarṣapa (mustard), Madya (wine), are harmful for the patient of Mūtra Kṛccra. Avoid riding and suppression of urge for urination.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Kaṣṭa Mūtra, Beng: Mūtra Kṛccha, Dogr: Mūtra-Kṛccha, Guj: Peśāba Mā Badatara, Kaṭhara Ke Peśāba Avuṅ, Hind: Ruka Ruka Kara Ke Peśāba Ānā, Kan: Mūthra Kaṭṭū, Maly: Vedanayoṭū Kūṭiyamūthraṭhaṭavū, Mra: Kālmāruna Lāghavila Hoṇe, Tam: Soṭṭu Mūtram, Eng: Dysurea

Title: Mūtrāghāta
Sanskrit: मूत्राघात
INTRO: In Mutrāghāta patient is unable to pass the urine or passes little urine with difficulty though the bladder is full of urine.
TREATMENT: Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Cūrṇodaka (lime water) - 14 to 28 ml. to be taken with Dhāroṣṇa Dugdha (freshly milched milk) - 250 ml. twice a day. 2. Decoction of equal part of roots of Nala (nodding reed), Kāśa (kans), Kuśa (sacred grass) and Ikṣu (sugarcane root) - 14 to 28 ml. to be taken when cold with 5 to 10 g. Śarkarā (raw sugar) thrice a day. 3. Decoction of Kṛṣṇa Mūsalī - 14 to 28 ml. to be taken with 5 ml. Tila Taila (gingelly oil), 5 g. ghee and 100 to 250 ml. milk thrice a day. 4. Daśamūla Kvātha: 14 to 28 ml. to be taken with 500 mg. to 1 g. Śuddha Śilājatu and 12 g. Śarkarā (raw sugar) thrice a day. 5. Śuddha Śilājatu - 0.5 to 1.0 g. to be taken with 4 to 6 g. honey and 5 to 10 g. Śarkarā (raw sugar) thrice a day. 6. Kṣīra Siddha with Tṛṇa Pañca Mūla, fruit of Gokṣuru (small caltrops), roots of Eraṇḍa (castor) and Śatāvarī (wild asparagus) - 100 to 200 ml. to be taken with Guḍa (jaggery) and ghee thrice a day. 7. Powder of equal part of Sūryakṣāra (salt petre), fruit of Kaṅkola (cubeb), Elā (cardamom seed) and root of Amlaparṇī (rhubarb) - 1 to 3 g. to be taken with milk thrice a day.
PATHYA: Purāṇa Śāli (old rice), Māṣa (black phaseolus bean), fruits of Kūṣmāṇḍa (a variety of pumpkin gourd-white gourd), Nārikela (green coconut), Pūga (areca nut), fruit of Kharjūra (date), milk, curd and massage are useful for the patient of Mūtrāghāta.
APATHYA: Rūkṣa, Vidāhī and Viṣṭambhi Dravyas, fruit of Karīra (caper) are harmful for the patient of Mūtrāghāta. Suppression of calls of nature, sexual intercourse and walking should be avoided.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Mūtrabarodha, Beng: Mūtravarodha, Guj: Mūtra Mā Āghāta, Peśāda Mā Dikkata, Hind: Peśāba Kā Nā Ānā, Kan: Mutraṭaḍe, Maly: Paripūrna Mūthra Taṭāvū, Mra: Laghvī Akhaḍaṇe, Ori: Prāsārekībā, Tam: Nīrdagal, Tel: Onṭelaḍḍuṭa, Eng: Retention of urine

Title: Raktameha
Sanskrit: रक्तमेह
INTRO: In this condition patient passes foetid, saline, warm urine with blood and pain in bladder region.
TREATMENT: A specialist should be consulted as soon as possible.
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Kṣīra Siddha with Drākṣā (raisin or grape fruit), roots of Balā (country mallow) and Yaṣṭimadhu (glycyrrhiza), fruit of Gokṣura (small caltrops) and root of Śatāvarī (wild asparagus) – 100 to 200 ml. to be taken thrice a day.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Tepīcābo, Beng: Raktameha, Guj: Lohī No Peśāba, Hind: Khūna Kī Peśāb, Peśāba Men Khūna Ānā, Kan: Raktamūtra, Maly: Raktamūthram, Mra: Raktameha, Laghvitūna Vaktajaṇe, Tam: Raktha Mūtram, Tel: Onṭelulo/Mūtramulo Netturu Povuṭa, Eng: Haematuria

Title: MEDO-VṚDDHI
Sanskrit: मेदावृद्धि
INTRO: Excessive accumulation of fat in the region of breast, hip, belly etc. of the body leading to various complications is known as Medovṛddhi or Medo-Roga.
SYMPTOMS: The patient of Medo-Vṛddhi suffers from much sweating, hunger and thirst, emits bad smell, feels weakness and difficulty in sexual intercourse and movement. The disease may lead to many complications e.g. diabetes, heart disease, hemiplegia and arthritis.
TREATMENT: Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Powder of equal part of seeds of Viḍaṅga and Yava (barley), Śuṇṭhī (dried ginger), Yavakṣāra, Loha Bhasma, fruit rind of Āmalakī (chebulic myrobalan) – 1 to 3 g. to be taken with 4 to 6 g. honey twice a day. 2. Powder of equal part of Cavya, fruit of Jīraka (cumin), Trikaṭu, Bhṛṣṭa Hiṅgu (asafoetida), root of Citraka (leawort), Kṛṣṇa Lavaṇa – 1 to 3 g. to be taken with 100 to 250 ml. of curd water and 50 to 100 g. Saktu twice a day. 3. Powder of 2 part each of Trikaṭu, root of Citraka (leadwort), Triphalā Mustaka (motha) and Viḍaṅga mixed with 1 part of Śuddha Guggulu (bdellium) to be taken in 3 to 6 g. dose with 1 to 2 g. honey twice a day. 4. Kṣāra prepared from leaf of Eraṇḍa (castor) – 4 to 5 g. and Hiṅgu (asafoetida) fried in ghee – 1 g. to be taken with 4 to 6 g. honey twice a day. 5. Control appetite by gradually reducing the diet. In case obesity is not due to over eating or if complications occur, then a specialist should be consulted.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Amṛtādi Guggulu: 1 to 3 g. to be taken with 100 ml. warm water twice a day. 2. Triphalā Guggulu: 1 to 2 g. to be taken with 4 to 6 g. honey twice a day. 3. Navaka Guggulu: 1 to 2 g. to be taken thrice a day with warm water.
PATHYA: Purāṇa Śāli (old rice), Mudga (dolichos bean), Yava (barley), Masūra (lentil), Āḍhakī (pigeon pea); Bhṛṣṭa Vārtāka (fried brinjal); Takra (butter milk) and walking are useful for the patient of Medo-Vṛddhi.
APATHYA: Navīna Śāli Dhānya (all types of freshly harvested rice), Godhūma (wheat), Māṣa (black phaseolus bean); milk and its products, sugar products, cold bath are harmful for the patient of Medo-Vṛddhi.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Śirā Medaja, Beng: Medhābṛddhi, Dogr: Moṭāpā, Guj: Carvī Vadhāvī, Hind: Moṭāpā, Kan: Bojju, Maly: Medojanya Maya Muṣka Vṛddhi, Mra: Carbī Vaḍaṇe, Ori: Denasicirvi Janibā, Tam: Ūjharehadai, Tel: Lāvekkuṭa, Eng: Obesity and diseases resulting there to

Title: RAKTAPITTA
Sanskrit: रक्तपित्त
INTRO: Raktapitta is a condition in which bleeding occurs from the upper or lower channels of the body.
SYMPTOMS: Bleeding from the upper channels like nose, mouth etc. or from lower channels like anus, urinary passage, female genital organ etc. or petechial haemorrhage, aesthania, cough, dyspnoea, fever, loss of appetite, indigestion, vomiting, thirst, burning sensation, nervousness, frequent motions, pallor and unconsciousness are the main signs and symptom of Raktapitta.
TREATMENT: Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Green Udumbara (fig-gular) ground and wrapped in Poṭṭalikā, sqeezed to yield a Svarasa (juice) – 7 to 14 ml., to be taken with 4 to 6 g. honey twice a day. 2. Take 100 to 200 ml. Dugdha Siddha in Drākṣā (raisin or grape fruit) with powdered flower of Priyaṅgu twice a day. 3. Dugdha Siddha with almond of Priyāla (cuddapah) or with root of Yaṣṭimadhu (glycyrrhiza) or with fruit of Gokṣura (small caltrop) or with root of Śatāvarī (wild asparagus) – 100 to 200 ml. to be taken twice a day. 4. Ghṛta Siddha with decoction of whole plant of Vāsā and Kalka (paste) of flower of Vāsā to be taken in – 12 to 24 g. dose twice a day. 5. Decoction of equal part of fruit of Dhānyaka (coriander), fruit rind of Āmalakī (embelic myrobalan), Drākṣā (raisin or grape fruit), leaf of Vāsā, whole plant of Parpaṭa (five leaved fumitory) – 14 to 28 ml. to be taken thrice a day. 6. Decoction of equal part of leaf of Vāsā, Drākṣā (raisin or grape fruit), fruit rind of Harītakī (chebulic myrobalan) – 14 to 28 ml. to be taken with honey and Śarkarā (raw sugar) twice a day. 7. Powder of wood of Rakta Candana (red sandal), root of Yaṣṭimadhu (glycyrrhiza) – 3 to 6 g. to be taken with 100 to 250 ml. milk thrice a day. 8. Powder of equal part of wood of Rakta Candana (red sandal), Drākṣā (raisin or grape fruit), leaf of Vāsā (vasaka), fruit rind of Harītakī (chebulic myrobalan) – 3 to 6 g. to be taken with 4 to 6 g. honey twice a day. 9. Fine powder of Śuddha Lākṣā (purified lac) – 4 g. to be taken with honey and Śarkarā (raw sugar) and water twice a day. 10. Peyā prepared from Laghu Pañcamūla to be taken thrice a day. 11. Vaṭa Patra Śṛṅga (banyan tender leaf of bud), contused with milk to be taken in 3 to 6 g. dose thrice a day. 1. Powder of Śuddha Lākṣā (purified lac), leaf of Vāsā (vasaka), root of Yaṣṭimadhu (glycyrrhiza) – 2 parts each and Karkaṭaśṛṅgī (crab’s claw), Yaśada Bhasma, Abhraka Bhasma – 1 part each to be taken in 1 to 2 g. dose with 100 to 250 ml. milk thrice a day. 2. Powder of Lājā (pop of paddy) – 12 to 24 g. to be taken with 4 to 6 g. honey thrice a day. 3. Siddha Jala prepared with powder of root of Yaṣṭimadhu (glycyrrhiza), Śuddha Lākṣā (purified lac), fruit of Parūṣaka (asiatic grewia), to be taken as required. 4. Svarṇa Gairika (ochre) – 120 to 500 mg. To be taken with 4 to 6 g. honey or 5 to 10 g. Śarkarā (raw sugar) thrice a day. 5. Kalka of wood of Candana (sandal) in water – 12 to 24 g. to be taken with powdered root of Yaṣṭimadhu (glycyrrhiza) and 4 to 6 g. honey twice a day.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Bola Parpaṭī: 500 mg. to 1.5 g. to be taken with Vāsāvaleha – 6 to 12 g. twice a day. It is specially useful in Guda Rakta Śrāva (bleeding from the anus). 2. Kuṣmāṇḍāvaleha: 12 to 24 g. to be taken with 100 to 250 ml. milk twice a day. 3. Uśīrāsava: 14 to 28 ml. to be taken with equal part of water after meal thrice a day. 1. Candanādi Cūrṇa: 3 to 6 g. to be taken with 100 to 250 ml. milk thrice a day. 2. Powdered and purified Dugdhapāṣāṇa (talc) to be taken in 120 to 500 mg. dose with 7 to 14 ml. juice of Dūrvā (doob grass) twice a day.
PATHYA: Tikta Dravya, Purāṇa Śāli (old rice), Taṇḍula (rice), seeds of Yava (barley), Mudga (phaseolus bean), Masūra (lentil), Caṇaka (gram), Āḍhakī (pigeon pea) and Makuṣṭha (aconite leaved kidney bean); Śarkarā (raw sugar), honey, products of sugar cane, Śatadhauta Ghṛta; Kadalī-Phala (banana), fruit of Priyāla (cuddapah almond), fruit and leaf of Paṭola (a variety of small cucumber-snake gourd), Vetasa Śuga (shoot of willow), leaf of Vāsā (vasaka), fruit of Śṛṅgāṭaka (water chest-nut), whole plant of Kirātatikta (chirata), stem of Kamala (lotus), leaves of Nimba, fruits of Dāḍima (pomegranate), Nārikela (coconut), Kapittha (wood apple) and Drākṣā (raisin or grape fruit); Abhyaṅga (massage), Lepa (plaster), Snāna (bath) are useful for the patient of Raktapitta.
APATHYA: Amla, Lavaṇa and Kaṭu Rasa; seeds of Kulattha (dolichos bean) and Tila (sesame); Śimbi Phala (legumes); leaf of Sarṣapa (mustard), fruit of Vārtāki (brinjal), curd, bulb of Rasona (garlic) are harmful for the patient of Raktapitta.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Raktapitta, Beng: Raktapitta, Dogr: Raktapitta, Guj: Raktapitta, Hind: Raktapitta, Kan: Rakthāriyavudū, Maly: Raktha-Pittam, Mra: Raktapitta, Ori: Raktapitta, Tam: Pulangalilraththa Kaśīvū, Eng: Haemorrhagic diseases

Title: Nāsāgata Raktapitta
Sanskrit: नासागत रक्तपित्त
INTRO: Bleeding from the nose is called Nāsāgata Raktapitta.
TREATMENT: Treatment
PATHYA: Śīta Dravya, Purāṇa Śāli (old red variety of rice), cold water are useful for the patient of epistaxis (Nāsāgata Raktapitta).
APATHYA: Amla, Lavaṇa, Tīkṣṇa, Kṣāra and Uṣṇa Dravya are harmful for the patient of Nāsāgata Raktapitta (epistaxis).
REGIONAL NAMES: Dogr: Naksīra, Guj: Nakodi Phuṭvī, Hind: Naksīra, Mra: Gholnā Phūṭaṇe, Kan: Muginindo Rakta Garuvudu, Eng: Expistaxis

Title: ROMĀNTIKĀ
Sanskrit: रोमान्तिका
INTRO: Romāntikā is a disease generally affecting the children and characterised by fever accompanied by eruptions of minute elevated papules.
SYMPTOMS: Abrupt high fever, sneezing, redness of conjunctiva, dry cough, loss of appetite are the initial symptoms. On the third or fourth day minute reddish elevated eruptions appear first behind the ears, temples and neck, and within a few hours whole face is involved and then whole body is affected. There is tendency of pimples to coalesce. Within 4 or 5 days of its appearance the rashes completely disappear.
TREATMENT: For doses of children according to their age consult table of doses for children (Table 3).
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Sponge of seed of Methikā (fenugreek) boiled in water is useful in cutting short the eruptive state. 2. Kajjalī – 30 to 60 mg. to be taken with fruit juice of Kāravellaka – 5 to 10 ml., twice a day. 3. Decoction of leaf of Tuṇḍulīyaka (a variety of amaranth) – 5 to 15 ml. to be taken with 1 g. powder of equal part of fruit of Paṭola (a small variety of cucumber-snake gourd), rhizome of Haridrā (turmeric), and of Āmalakī (embelic myrobalan), twice a day. 4. Decoction of equal part of Khadira (khair), Triphalā, leaf of Nimba (neem), whole plant of Paṭola (a variety of small cucumber-snake gourd), stem of Guḍūcī and leaf of Vāsā (vasaka) – 5 to 15 ml. to be taken twice a day. 5. Decoction of Kṛṣṇa Jīraka (caraway) – 5 to 10 ml. to be taken with powdered rhizome of Haridrā (turmeric) – 250 mg. to 1 g. thrice a day.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Karpūrādi Cūrṇa: 250 mg. to 1 g. to be taken with honey thrice a day. 2. Khadirāṣṭaka Kvātha: 5 to 15 ml. to be taken twice a day. 3. Parpāṭādi Kvātha: 14 to 28 ml. to be taken twice a day. 4. Lakṣmī-Vilāsa Rasa: 60 to 120 mg. to be taken with honey twice a day. 5. Mṛtuñjaya Rasa: 60 to 120 mg. to be taken with honey twice a day.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Lutiai, Beng: Hama, Dogr: Cancela, Guj: Oḍi. Khasrā, Hind: Khasarā, Kan: Thoṭṭu, Dādarada, Maly: Pongann, Manal, Mra: Govara, Ori: Milīmilā, Tam: Manalvārī Ammai, Tel: Cinnāmavārū, Eng: Measles

Title: Vāta Vyādhi
Sanskrit: वात व्याधि
INTRO: The specific diseases which can only be caused by Vāta are known as Vāta Vyādhi. Signs, symptoms and treatment of the common diseases are as follows.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Vāta Bemāra, Vāyaroga, Beng: Bāta Roga, Dogr: Vāya Kī Bimārī, Guj: Vā Ni Bimārī, Hind: Vāyu Kī Bimāriyā, Kan: Vāyuroga, Maly: Vāta Rogam, Panj: Vāyu De Roga, Tam: Vāta Rogam, Tel: Vāta Rogamulu, Eng: Diseases of nervous system

Title: Ardita
Sanskrit: अर्दित
INTRO: Paralysis in which only one half of the face is involved is known as Ardita.
SYMPTOMS: Twisting of one half of the face including neck towards the normal side, trembling of the head, impairment of voice, tremor, stiffness or pain in the neck, inability to close the eye or to show the teeth of the affected side are the main signs and symptoms of Ardita.
TREATMENT: Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Kalka of bulb of Rasona (garlic) fried in Tila Taila is to be taken in 6 to 12 g. dose twice a day. 2. Māṁsa of Vaṭaka followed by 100 to 250 ml. milk and 14 to 28 ml. decoction of Daśamūla to be taken twice a day. 3. Meat soup followed by 14 to 28 ml. decoction of Daśamūla to be taken twice a day.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Samīrapannaga Rasa: 60 to 120 mg. to be taken with honey to make a paste twice in a day. Foment with a hot leaf prepared from Māṣa (black phaseolus bean) and bandage the affected parts. Milk diet or liquid diet is useful.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Ardita, Beng: Ardita, Dogr: Lakavā, Guj: Aradī, Hind: Mūha Kā Lakavā, Kan: Mukhada Lakavā, Maly: Mukhā Vāta Sannī, Ardita, Chirikotivatam, Mra: Tonda Vakade Hone, Ori: Muhānmdā, Panj: Mūnha Da Lakvā, Tam: Mukāpā Savāyu, Mukhvātam, Eng: Facial paralysis

Title: Pakṣāghāta
Sanskrit: पक्षाघात
INTRO: Paralysis of one side of the body is called Pakṣāghāta or Pakṣāvadha.
SYMPTOMS: Loss of motor function of one side, numbness and pain in the affected side or in the whole body, inability to walk i.e. limping, sometimes impairment of speech are the general signs and symptoms of Pakṣavadha. If Pitta is involved patient may also become unconscious.
TREATMENT: Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Decoction of equal part of seeds of Māṣa (black phaseolus bean) and Kapikacchū (cowage), roots of Eraṇḍa (castor) and Atiabalā (country mallow) – 14 to 28 ml. to be taken with 2 g. of fried Hiṅgu (asafoetida) and 1 g. Saindhava (rock-salt) twice a day. 1. Māṣa Modaka with Daśamūla Kvātha – 14 to 28 ml. to be taken twice a day. 2. Tila Taila (gingelly oil) – 12 to 24 g. to be taken with bulb of Rasona (garlic) – 2 g., Saindhava (rock-salt) – 1 g. twice a day.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Mahābalādi Kvātha: 14 to 28 ml. to be taken thrice a day. 2. Mahārasnādi Kvātha: 14 to 28 ml. to be taken thrice a day. For acute attack 1. Ekāṅgavīra Rasa: 60 to 250 mg. to be taken with honey to make a paste thrice a day. 2. Rasarāja Rasa: 60 to 250 mg. to be taken with honey to a make a paste thrice a day. 3. Mṛgmada (Kastūrī): 40 to 60 mg. to be taken with bulb of Rasona (garlic) – 1 g. and Tila Taila (gingelly Oil) – 12 to 24 g. twice a day. 4. Mahāyogarāja Guggulu: 1 to 2 Vaṭī to be taken thrice a day. 5. Yogarāja Guggulu: 2 to 4 Vaṭī to be taken thrice a day. 6. Granthikādi Taila: 6 to 12 g. to be taken with 100 to 250 ml. milk in the morning. 7. Māṣa Taila: 6 to 12 g. to be taken with 100 to 250 ml. milk twice in a day. 8. Rasona Piṇḍa: 12 to 24 g. to be taken with the decoction of root of Eraṇḍa (castor) – 14 to 28 ml. twice a day. 9. Lasunādi Vaṭī: 2 to 4 pills to be taken twice a day. The drugs useful for Virecana (Purgation) 1. Leaf powder of Svarṇapatrī (senna) – 3 to 6 g. to be taken with warm water once a day. 2. Triphalā Cūrṇa – 3 to 6 g. to be taken with warm water twice a day. 3. Eraṇḍa Taila (castor oil) – 14 to 28 ml. to be taken with warm water once a day.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Pakṣāghāta, Beng: Pakṣāghāta, Dogr: Pāsā Maraṇā, Pakṣavāta, Pakṣāghāta, Guj: Lakavo, Hind: Lakavā, Maly: Pakṣāvātam, Mra: Lakavā, Pakṣāvadha, Panj: Lakvā, Tam: Parisāvāyu, Eng: Paralysis

Title: Khañjavāta
Sanskrit: खञ्जवात
INTRO: Paralysis of one leg caused by Vāta leading to lameness is known as Khañja. When the Vāyu affects both the legs the patient becomes a cripple and this condition is known as Paṅgu.
TREATMENT: Treatment
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Agnituṇḍī Vaṭī: 1 to 2 Vaṭī to be taken with warm water thrice a day. 2. Sarpagandhā-Ghana Vaṭī: 1 to 2 Vaṭī for acute pain only. 3. Treatment under Pakṣāghāta may also be followed.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Khoḍā, Beng: Khañjatva, Guj: Langrā Paḍavūṅ, Hind: Paṅguta, Kan: Kuṇṭu, Maly: Oru Kālu Muṭamthān, Mra: Langaḍepaṇa, Ori: Khaliā, Panj: Laṅgaḍā, Eng: Lameness

Title: Gṛdhrasī
Sanskrit: गृध्रसी
INTRO: The pain which start from lower back and runs through anterior surface of thigh, medial aspect of the lower leg and medial side of foot is called Gṛdhrasī.
TREATMENT: Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Eraṇḍa Taila (castor oil) – 7 to 14 ml. to be taken with Gomūtra (cow’s urine) – 7 to 14 ml. and 1 g. powdered fruit of Pippalī (long pepper) twice a day. 2. Powder of equal part of Daśamūla, root of Balā (country mallow), root of Rāsnā (Indian groundsel), Guḍūcī, Śuṇṭhī (dried ginger) – 3 to 6 g. to be taken with Eraṇḍa Taila (castor oil) – 7 to 14 ml. thrice a day. 3. Decoction of leaf of Nirguṇḍī – 14 to 28 ml. to be taken thrice a day. 4. Bṛhatī fried in Eraṇḍa Taila (castor oil) to be taken three times a day. 5. Decoction of equal part of leaf of Vāsā and root of Dantī (wild croton) – 14 to 28 ml. to be taken with Eraṇḍa Taila (castor oil) three times a day. 6. Decoction of Bṛhat Pañcamūla – 14 to 28 ml. to be taken with Eraṇḍa Taila (castor oil) – 7 to 14 ml. three times a day. 7. Decoction of equal part of Rasona, Guḍūcī, fruit pulp of Āragavadha (cassia), wood of Devadāru (deodar), fruit of Gokṣura (small caltrops), roots of Eraṇḍa (castor) and Punarnavā (pigweed) – 14 to 28 ml. to be taken with 1 g. powder of Śuṇṭhī (dried ginger) thrice a day. 8. Take powdered root of Rāsnā (Indian groundsel) – 50 g., Śuddha Guggulu – 25 g. and add little ghee to make a Vaṭī of 1 g. Such 1 to 2 Vaṭī is to be taken with 50 ml. warm water thrice a day.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Trayodaśāṅga Guggulu: 2 to 4 Vaṭī to be taken with 50 ml. warm water thrice a day. 2. Rasona Piṇḍa: 1 g. to be taken with 100 to 250 ml. milk thrice a day.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Grdharaṇa Vāta, Beng: Gṛdhrasī, Dogr: Ringmu Vāya, Guj: Rājano Vāyu, Hind: Rānga Bāya, Kan: Bondiśūle, Maly: Vedanayoṭu Kuṭiyā, Kalintāi Sthambham, Mra: Gṛdharasi, Panj: Ringaḍvā, Tam: Pakka Vātham, Eng: Sciatica

Title: Viśvācī
Sanskrit: विश्वाची
INTRO: The vitiated Vāyu by involving the muscles and tendons from scapula to the back of fingers leads to the loss of motor function of the arm and fingers, and this condition is known as Viśvācī.
TREATMENT: Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Decoction of equal part of Daśamūla, root of Balā (country mallow), Māṣa (black phaseolus bean) – 14 to 28 ml. to be taken with 6 to 12 g. ghee, after meal, twice a day.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Vaṭā-Vidhvanasana Rasa: 2 to 4 Vaṭī to be taken with warm water three times a day. 2. Yogarāja Guggulu: 2 to 4 Vaṭī to be taken with warm water three times a day.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Viśvācī, Beng: Viśvācī, Dogr: Riha, Hind: Hātha Paḍa Jānā, Maly: Kai Sthambhana, Mra: Viśvācī, Tam: Tholā Paṭṭao Vāyu, Eng: Brachial neuralgia

Title: Sandhigata-Vāta
Sanskrit: सन्धिगत वात
INTRO: Vitiated Vāyu affecting the joints causes pain swelling and impairment of the function of the joints and this is known as Sandhigata-Vāta. In this condition big joints like knee are particularly affected.
TREATMENT: Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Take leaf of Sambhālū - 2 g., leaf of Bilva (bael)- 2 g., root of Pṛśniparṇī (china flower)- 2 g. Juice of Ārdraka (ginger)- 5 to 10 ml. and make Kalka. It is to be taken with 1 g. Saindhava (rock-salt) thrice a day. 2. Decoction of equal part of bulb of Rasona (garlic)- 6 g., root of Eraṇḍa (castor) 6 g., leaf of Nirguṇḍī-4 g., Śuṇṭhī (dried ginger)-5 g., fruit of Śatapuṣpā (fennel)-3 g. to be taken in 14 to 28 ml. dose thrice a day. 3. Tila Taila Siddha with Kalka of bulb of Rasona (garlic)-12 to 24 g. to be taken with warm water three times a day.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Vātagajāṅkuśa: 1 to 3 Vaṭī to be taken with warm water thrice a day. 2. Yogarāja Guggulu: 1 to 2 g. to be taken thrice a day with warm water.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Joḍa Vāta, Gaṭhī Vāta, Beng: Sandhi Vāta, Dogr: Joḍa Judaṇā, Guj: Sāndhano Vā, Hind: Sandhivāta, Kan: Kiluvāyu, Maly: Sandhi Vātam, Mra: Sandhi Vāta, Sandhe Dharṇe, Ori: Anthīganthā Vatā, Tam: Sandhu Vatha Sūlai, Tel: Kīlla Noppullu, Eng: Arthiritis

Title: Kroṣṭuka–Śīrṣa
Sanskrit: क्रोष्टुक शीर्ष
INTRO: Kroṣṭuka Śīrṣa is a condition characterized by acute pain and swelling of the knee joint. In this conditions the shape of the joint becomes like the head of jackal.
TREATMENT: Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Eraṇḍa Taila (castor oil)-7 ml. to be taken with 250 ml. cow’s milk once a day. 2. Śuddha Guggulu-2 to 6 g. to be taken with Tittira Mānsa (partridge meat) or with equal part of Guḍa (jaggery) and decoctin of Triphalā- 14 to 28 ml. three times a day. 3. Decoction of equal part of Guḍūcī and Triphalā – 14 to 28 ml. to be taken thrice a day.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Kaiśora Guggulu: 2 to 4 Vaṭī to be taken with warm water twice a day. 2. Amṛtādi Guggulu: 2 to 4 Vaṭī to be taken with warm water twice a day. 3. Yogarāja Guggulu: 2 to 4 Vaṭī to be taken with 50 ml. warm water thrice a day.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Siyāla Muriyā Vāta, Beng: Kroṣṭuka Śīrṣa, Guj: Ghuṭaṇa No Vā, Hind: Ghutane Kā Bāya, Kan: Mānḍa, Maly: Perumuṭṭu Vātam, Mra: Guḍghī, Ori: Menḍhamāndiā Vāta, Tam: Kīl Vāyu, Tel: Debrakāmu Kāna, Eng: Arthritis of knee joint

Title: Manyā-Stambha
Sanskrit: मन्यास्तम्भ
INTRO: Vitiated Vāta by involving the muscles of the neck causes rigidity and immobility of neck and this condition is known as Manyāstambha.
TREATMENT: Treatment
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Yogarāja Guggulu: 2 to 4 pills to be taken with warm three times a day.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Śikā Lārā, Beng: Manyāstambha, Dogr: Munḍi Belā, Hind: Gardana Jakaḍanā, Kan: Ulugoralū, Maly: Kajhuṭhinle Piṭutham, Mra: Mana Jakhaḍaṇe, Ori: Bekā Rakta, Tam: Sagana Vatham, Eng: Torticolis

Title: Hanu-Stambha
Sanskrit: हनुस्तम्भ
INTRO: Hanu Stambha is a condition in which the patient is unable to open or close the jaw leading to difficulty in speaking and chewing.
TREATMENT: 1. Gargle with salt water. 2. Take a Kavala (mouth wash) of Tila Taila (gingerly oil).
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Take bulb of Rasona (garlic)-6 to 12 g., Saindhava (rock-salt)-1 g., Tila taila (gingelly oil)-6 to 12 g. thrice a day. 2. Make Vaṭaka in Tila Taila (gingelly oil) by adding Rasona (garlic)-1 g. and Māṣa (decorticated black phaseolus bean)-100 g. mixed Saindhava-2 g., Ārdraka (ginger)-5 g. It is to be taken thrice a day.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Mahā-Yogarāja Guggulu: 2 to 4 Vaṭī be taken with honey or Śarkarā (raw sugar) and Navanīta (butter)-4 to 6 g. twice a day. 2. Prasāraṇī Taila: 12 to 24 g. to be taken with warm water once a day.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Hanusandhi, Beng: Hanustambha, Dogr: Thoḍi Ugḍṇā, Guj: Sāndhano Vā, Hind: Jabaḍā Kāsaṇā, Kan: Bāyī Hidīthā, Maly: Tatiyanakan Vayyayaka, Mra: Jabaḍe Dhārṇe, Tam: Taraḍvī Irukkam, Tel: Ankillu Paṭṭukonuṭa, Eng: Lock jaw

Title: Vāta-Kaṇṭaka
Sanskrit: वातकण्टक
INTRO: Vātakaṇṭaka is a painful condition of ankle joint caused by unsteady step or excessive walking.
TREATMENT: Treatment
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Triphalā Guggulu: 2 to 4 Vaṭī to be taken with warm water thrice a day. 2. Yogarāja Guggulu: 2 to 4 Vaṭī to be taken with warm water thrice a day.
REGIONAL NAMES: Beng: Vāta kanṭaka, Dogr: Gokuro, Hind: Paira Kī Moca, Kan: Himmadi Vāyu, Mra: Vāta Kaṇṭaka, Lacākaṇe, Ori: Pāda Rākā Mebā, Panj: Moca, Tam: Sulukku, Eng: Sprain of the ankle

Title: Kaṭi-Śūla
Sanskrit: कटि शूल
INTRO: Pain and swelling of lower part of the back is known as Kaṭiśūla.
TREATMENT: Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Decoction of Daśamūla- 14 to 28 ml. to be taken with Eraṇḍa Taila (castor oil)- 7 to 14 ml. thrice a day. 2. Decoction of Śuṇṭhī (dried ginger)- 14 to 28 ml. to be taken with Eraṇḍa Taila (castor oil)- 7 to 14 ml. thrice day.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Trayodaśāṅga Guggulu: 2 to 4 Vaṭī to be taken with warm water thrice a day.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Kaṭiśūla, Beng: Kaṭiśūla, Dogr: Lekapuda, Guj: Kendadukhavūṅ, Hind: Kamara Kā Darda, Kan: Sontadā Novu, Maly: Oṭidesāvedanā, Iduppu Vedana, Mra: Kambara Dūkhī, Ori: Antādhāra, Panj: Kamara Darda, Tam: Iduppu Valī, Tel: Naḍumu Noppi, Eng: Lumbago

Title: Kampavāta
Sanskrit: कम्पवात
INTRO: Vitiated Vāta causes tremors of muscles leading to a continuous kickey movement of the head or hands or a peculiar tremor in the whole body and this condition is known as Kampavāta.
TREATMENT: Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Kalka (paste) of bulb of Rasona (garlic)- 6 to 12 g. to be taken with Tila Taila (gingelly oil)-6 to 12 g. and Saindhava (rock-salt)-1 to 2 g. twice a day. 2. Decoction of equal part of root of Rāsnā (Indian groundsel), stem of Guḍūcī, Śuṇṭhī (dried ginger), and roots of Punarnavā (pigweed) and Eraṇḍa (castor), 14 to 28 ml. to be taken thrice a day.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Sarpagandhā-Ghana Vaṭī: 2 Vaṭī to be taken with water twice a day. 2. Vātagajāṅkuśa Rasa: 1 to 2 Vaṭī to be taken with honey to make a paste twice a day. 3. Yogarāja Guggulu: 2 to 4 Vaṭī to be taken twice a day with warm water. 4. Mahā-Nārāyaṇa Taila: 7 to 14 ml. to be taken with 100 to 250 ml. milk twice a day. 5. Mahā-Māṣa Taila: 7 to 14 ml. to be taken with 100 to 250 ml. milk twice a day. 6. Mahā-Māṣa Taila: May also be used for massage.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Kapānīvāta, Beng: Kampavāta, Dogr: Kāmāvāsa Chola Oldhāramda, Guj: Kampa Vā, Hind: Kampa Vāta, Kan: Naḍukavāyū, Maly: Virāyalotukutiya Vātam, Mra: Kampa Vāyu, Ori: Tharavāta, Tharthariāvāta, Tam: Naḍukkam, Tel: Vanukuṭa, Eng: Tremors

Title: Ākṣepaka
Sanskrit: आक्षेपक
INTRO: Vitiated Vāyu causes convulsions in the body and this condition is known as Ākṣepāka. On the first appearance of convulsion, a specialist should be consulted.
TREATMENT: Treatment
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Sarpagandha-Ghana Vaṭī: 1 to 2 Vaṭī to be taken with Aśvagandhā Ghṛta- 6 to 12 g. three times a day. 2. Kṣīrabalā Taila: 12 to 24 g. to be taken with 100 to 250 ml. milk thrice a day.
PATHYA: Purāṇa Śāli (old rice), Godhūma (wheat), seeds of Māṣa (black phaseolus bean), Kulattha (dolichos bean); leaves and fruit of Śigru (horse-radish), fruit of Vārtāka (brinjal), fruit of Dāḍima (pomegranate), ripe fruits of Tāla (palm) and Āmra (mango); fruits of Jambīra (lemon), Drākṣā (raisin or grape fruit) and Nāraṅga (orange); flower of Madhūka (mahuva), fruits of Badara (jujube) and Ciñcā (tamarind); Nārikela Jala (coconut water), leaves of Tambūla (betel); Gomūtra (cow’s urine); poultice, nasal drops and sleeping on the flat floor; bacon, partridge meat are the useful articles of diet for the patients of Vātavyadhi.
APATHYA: Seeds of Yava (barley), Satīna (pea) Kodrava (a variety of millet); fruit of Kāravellaka (bitter gourd); stalk and root of Kamala (lotus), seed of Snuhī (milk) hedge), fruit of Udumbara (gular-fig), green fruit of Tāla (palm), Pūga (areca nut), fruit of Jambū (jamun), Kaśeruka, Śāka, cold water, Śuṣka Māṁsa (lean and dry meat) are harmful for the patients of Vāta Vyādhi. Riding, laziness, sitting up at night, anger, fast, bath and grinding of teeth should be avoided.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Ākṣepa, Beng: Ākṣepa, Dogr: Dhema Ponā, Guj: Aaki Tamā, Hind: Kampānā, Kan: Elāvu Vāyu, Maly: Veṭṭal Vātam, Mra: Jhaṭakāyeṇe, Ori: Vātāmāribā, Tam: Vālippu Noy, Eng: Convulsions

Title: VĀTARAKTA
Sanskrit: वातरक्त
INTRO: Vātarakta is a disease characterised by sudden attack of acute pain and swelling of joints which generally begins from the small toe and later on spread to the other joints.
SYMPTOMS: Acute pain and inflammation of joints which generally beings from the small toe or finger, and then gradually spreads to the other joints of the body like the poison of rat, extreme tenderness and burning sensation in the involved joints, excessive sweating, rigidity, numbness, discoloration of the skin on the affected joint, are the main signs and symptoms of Vātarakta.
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Decoction of Guḍūcī-14 to 28 ml. to be taken with Śuddha Guggulu-2 to 4 g. thrice a day. 2. Decoction of equal part of leaf of Vāsā, stem of Guḍūcī, fruit pulp of Āragvadha (cassia)-14 to 28 ml. to be taken with Eraṇḍa Taila (castor oil)-7 to 14 ml. twice a day.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Navakārsika Kvātha: 14 to 28 ml to be taken thrice a day. 2. Amṛtādi Guggulu: 2 to 4 Vaṭī to be taken with warm water thrice a day. 3. Kaiśora Guggulu: 2 to Vaṭī to be taken with warm water thrice a day. 4. Punarnavādi Guggulu: 2 to 4 Vaṭī to be taken with warm water thrice a day.
PATHYA: Śāli variety of rice, Godhūma (wheat), seeds of Caṇaka (gram) and Āḍhakī (pigion pea); leaf of Upodikā (Indian spinach), fruit of Kākamācī (negro coffee), Suniśaṇṇaka, leaves of Vāstūka (a variety of chenopodium) and Taṇḍulīyaka (a variety of amaranth); ripe fruit of Kūṣmāṇḍa (white gourd); Guḍūcī, woods of Candana (sandal) and Devadāru (deodar), are the useful articles of diet for the patient of Raktapitta.
APATHYA: Seeds of Māṣa (black phaseolus bean), Kulattha (dolichos bean) and Satīna (pea); Saktu, Śimbi (legumes); Mūlaka (radish), Ikṣu Dravya (sugarcane products); Madya (wine) and curd are harmful for the patients of Vātarakta. Day sleep, Exposure to heat, excessive exercise and sexual intercourse, should be avoided.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Vāta Rakta, Beng: Bāta Rakta, Dogr: Vātha Rekta, Guj: Gathiyo, Hind: Gaṭhiā, Kan: Vātarakta, Maly: Vātaraktam, Mra: Vāta Rakta, Ori: Ambilipitī, Tam: Vāta Raktam, Eng: Gout

Title: VIṢA
Sanskrit: विष
INTRO: The conditions caused by the ingestion of poisonous plants (Sthāvara Viṣa) or by biting of poisonous animals (Jaṅgama Viṣa) or intake of unpurified minerals or high dose of less poisonous substances or by the drug taken for unwarranted period, are known as Viṣa Roga. All the cases of suspected poising should promptly be entrusted to the care of a specialist.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Viṣa, Beng: Viṣa, Dogr: Jahara, Guj: Jhabaḍo, Jhahara Caḍavūṅ, Hind: Jahara, Kan: Viṣa, Maly: Viṣam, Mra: Viṣa Bādhā, Tam: Viḍam, Eng: Poisoning

Title: Sthāvara viṣa
Sanskrit: स्थावर विष
INTRO: The ingestion of root, leaf, fruit, flower, bark, latex, gum, bulb etc. of poisonous plants leads to the symptoms known as Sthāvara Viṣa Roga.
SYMPTOMS: Feeling of obstruction in the throat followed by vomiting of foamy material, hiccough, sensitiveness of teeth, loss of appetite, fever, unnatural breathing and fainting are the general signs and symptoms of Sthāvara viṣa.
TREATMENT: General Measure 1. Before commencing treatment ensure efficient emesis with salt water- 1 litre prepared by adding 50 g. salt in 1 litre water or decoction of Madanaphala (emetic nut) and Pippalī-1 liter or powered seed of Rājikā (black mustard)-12 to 24 g. with salt water.
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Mix honey - 50 g., milk-1 lit., cow’s ghee- 50 g., juice of Ikṣu (sugar cane)- 1lit., black muck soil- 50 g. with water -250 ml. and root juice of Guñjā (wild liquorice)-50 to 100 ml. it is to taken as early as possible after ingestion of poison, many times a day. 2. Equal part of powder of fruit of Pippalī (long pepper), Kaṭa-Tṛṇa, rhizome of Jatāmānsi (spikenard), Sāvara Lodhra, Sauvarcala Lavaṇa, seed of Elā (lesser cardamom), Śuddha Svarṇa Gairika (purified ochre)-3 to 12 g. to the taken with honey two times a day. 3. Ghra Siddha with equal part of Kalka of roots of Yaṣṭimadhu (glycyrrhiza), Tagara (valerian), Kuṣṭha (kooth) and Mustaka (motha), wood of Devadāru (deodar), fruit rind of Harītakī (chebulic myrobalan,) seed of Elā (lesser cardmom), Elavāluka (aloe), fruit of Surpunnāga (Alexandrian laurel), rhizome of Haridrā (turmeric), stem of Dāruharidrā (barberry), fruit of Bṛhatī (yellow berried night shade), root of Sārivā (Indian sarsaparilla), whole plants of Mudgaparṇi and Pṛśniparṇī-6 to 24 g. to be taken two times a day. 4. Kalka of equal part of seed of Kapikacchū (cowage), leave of Tulasī (sacred basil), seed of Indravāruṇī (colocynth), bark of Śigru (horse-radish), roots of Kākamāci (black night shade) and Punarnavā (pigweed) and fruit of Śirīṣa -6 to 12 g. to be taken with 250 ml. milk twice a day, or make powder of these drugs and take its 1 to 2 g. as Nasya (snuff).
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Udbhidā Viṣa, Beng: Sthāvara Viṣa, Dogr: Jadī Buṭīyān De Jahara, Guj: Jhāḍṇo Jhahara, Hind: Sthāvara Viṣa, Kan: Mulikadi Viṣa, Maly: Sthāvara Viṣam, Mra: Sthāvara Viṣa, Tam: Muligai Viḍam, Eng: Poisoning from vegetable products

Title: Jaṅgama Viṣa
Sanskrit: जङ्गम विष
INTRO: The condition caused by the bite, sting, skin contact or ingestion of the parts like teeth, nails, urine, semen or discharge of the body of the poisonous animals like snake, lizard, spider, scorpion and leech etc. is known as Jaṅgama Viṣa Roga.
SYMPTOMS: Burning sensation, horripilation, generalized or local swelling, diarrhoea, drowsiness, unusual sleep, vertigo are the general signs and symptoms of Jaṅgama Viṣa. The specific symptoms and treatment are as follow.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Jaibika Viṣa, Beng: Jangānī Viṣa, Dogr: Sappu Bicchū De Jahara, Guj: Prāṇi No Jhahara, Hind: Jaṅgama Viṣa, Kan: Prāni Viṣa, Maly: Jaṅgama Viṣam, Mra: Jaṅgam Viṣa, Prāṇiya Ce Viṣa, Tam: Pirāṇi Viḍam, Eng: Poisoning from animals and animal products

Title: Mūṣaka Viṣa
Sanskrit: मूषक विष
SYMPTOMS: Oozing of yellowish discharge from the site of rat bite, pallor, appearance of erythematous patches with burning sensation, discolouration, horripilation, headache, vomiting, excessive salivation and fever arc the symptoms caused by the rat bite.
TREATMENT: Following preparation may be used for emesis 1. Powder of seed of Śimbi (broad bean), fruit of Kaṭutumbī (bitter gourd), seed of Madanphala (emetic nut), fruit of Devadālī (bristly luffa) -5 to 10 g. to be taken with 50 g. curd.
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Powder of fruit, Kṣāra and bark of Śirīṣa-3 to 6 g. to be taken with 4 to 6 g. honey two times in a day. 2. Powder of equal part of Tvak (cinnamon bark) and Śuṇṭhī (dried ginger)- 3 to 6 g. to be taken with water twice a day. 3. Powder of equal part of Indrayava (kurchi seed), wood of Devadāru (deodar), rhizome of Tagara (valerian), fruit of Kaṭutumbī (bitter luffa)-3 to 6 g. to be taken with water. 4. Ghṛta Siddha with root of Sārivā (Indian sarsaparilla)-12 to 24 g. to be taken with water twice a day. 5. Ghṛta Siddha with the decoction of equal part of leaf flower, root and bark of Kapittha (wood apple) to be taken in 12 to 24 g. dose with warm water twice a day. 6. Kalka (paste) of equal part of Śirīṣa, Iṅgudī (zachum oil seed) in water to be taken in 6 to 12 g. dose with honey twice a day.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Andura Viṣa, Beng: Mūṣika Viṣa, Dogr: Cūhe De Jahara, Guj: Undara Viṣa, Hind: Cūhe Ka Jahara, Kan: Ilī Viṣa, Maly: Elī Viṣam, Mra: Undra Ce Viṣa, Ori: Mūṣaka Mudā, Tam: Eli Viḍam, Tel: Eluka Kāṭu, Eng: Rat bite poisoning

Title: Sarpadaṁśa
Sanskrit: सर्पदंश
INTRO: Patient may immediately he shifted to the hospital. Following first aid may be given 1. Give 2 strong ligatures at a distance of 7.5-10 cm. of snake bite to stop circulation of poison to the whole body. 2. Cauterize the site of snake bite.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Sarpa Viṣa, Beng: Sarpa Viṣa, Dogr: Sappu Dc Jahara, Guj: Sarpa No Jhahara, Hind: Sānpa Kā Jahara, Kan: Sarpa Viṣa, Maly: Sarpa Viṣam, Mra: Sarpa Viṣa, Ori: Sarpa Kā Mudā, Tam: Pāmbu Viḍam, Tel: Pāmu Kāṭu, Eng: Snake bite poisoning

Title: Vṛścika Viṣa
Sanskrit: वृश्चिक विष
SYMPTOMS: Intense burning and pain in the body which spread from the site of bite upwards and ultimately concentrate at the site of bite arc the main signs and symptoms of scorpion sting poisoning. Swelling of the tongue, difficulty in swallowing and unconsciousness may also occur in some cases.
TREATMENT: Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Ghee-50 g. and honey-100 g. to be taken with 250 ml. of milk and 5 to 10 g. Śarkarā (raw sugar) once a day. 2. Decoction of fruit of Ariṣṭaka (soap nut)-14 to 28 ml. or its powder-3 to 6 g. to be taken with water once a day.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Briścika Viṣa, Beng: Bṛścika Viṣa, Dogr: Bicchū Jeḍa Jahara, Guj: Bichī No Jhahara, Hind: Bicchū Danka Jahara, Kan: Chelina Viṣa, Maly: Thel Viṣam, Mra: Vincavache Viṣa, Tam: Theikādi, Tel: Telu Kāṭū, Eng: Scorpion sting poison

Title: Lūtā Viṣa
Sanskrit: लूता विष
SYMPTOMS: Decay at tissue and oozing of discharge with blood from the site of bite, appearance of pimples of varying size and shape with round and large periphery, intense inflammation which is soft to touch and black in colour, feeling of burning sensation and diarrhoea are the signs and symptoms caused by the spider biting.
TREATMENT: Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Powdered fruit or Lakuca (bread fruit tree)-3 to 6 g. to be taken with water twice a day. 2. Decoction of Śirīṣa-14 to 28 ml. to be taken with latex of Vaṭa (banyan) twice a day. 3. Powder of equal part of Tvak-Dālacīnī (cinnamom bark), Śuṇṭhī (dried ginger) 2 to 4 g. to be taken three times a day with 50 ml. water. 4. Powder of equal part of flower of Priyaṅgu , fruit of Badara (jujube), root of Kuṣṭha (kooth) bark of Jalavetasa (salix), fruits of Miśreyā (fennel) and Pippalī (long Pepper) and Vaṭaśunga (shoot of banyan) -6 to 12 g. to be taken with 50 mi. water twice a Jay.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Makaḍa Viṣa, Dogr: Kerli De Jahara, Guj: Makri No Jhahara, Hind: Makrī Kā jaharar, Kan: Jedina Viṣa, Maly: Chilanthi Viṣam, Mra: Katinice Viṣa, Ori: Mankanḍara Mūṭikā, Tam: Silaṇdī Viḍam, Tel: Sālepurugu Kāṭū, Eng: Spider bite poisoning

Title: Alarka Viṣa
Sanskrit: अलर्क विष
SYMPTOMS: Rabidity in dog is indicated by the drooping of head and tail of the animal, excessive salivation, and unnatural wandering. The site of bite by a rabid dog becomes numb and it bleeds black blood. The patient complains of headache, fever, vertigo and unconsciousness.
TREATMENT: The patient should be given anti-rabies vaccination for which the hospital should be contacted. The following first aid may be given at the time of bite. 1. Clean wound and apply the Lepa (plaster) of chilies in water. 2. Apply a Lepa (plaster) of Dhattūra (datura) in Taṇḍulodaka (rice washing).
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Pāgāla Kukura, Syālara Viṣa, Beng: Pāgala Kukkura Viṣa, Guj: Haḍaka Vā Thikutra No Jhahara, Hind: Pāgala Kuttc Kā Kāṭanā, Kan: Nayi Viṣa, Maly: Pepaṭṭi Viṣam, Mra: Pāgala Kutrayā Ce Viṣa, Tam: Verinoy Kadi Viḍam, Tel: Piccikukka Kāṭu, Eng: Bite of rabid dog (rabies)

Title: Mākṣika Viṣa
Sanskrit: माक्षिक विष
SYMPTOMS: As soon as a fly bites, a discharge oozes from the site of bite and a swollen bluish vesicle develops which is full of burning sensation and irritation. In case of excessive bite the person may have high fever and becomes unconscious.
TREATMENT: Treatment
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Maumākhī Viṣa, Beng: Madhu Makṣika Viṣa, Dogr: Makkhī Jhahara, Guj: Madha Makkhi Nū Jhahara, Hind: Makhī Kāṭanā, Kan: Jenu Nonājā Viṣa, Maly: Thenacā Viṣam, Mra: Mava Madhamāśi Ce Viṣa, Tam: Tenikkadi Vidam, Kankaddi, Tel: Teneṭīga Kāṭū, Eng: Fly bite, insect bite

Title: Pārada Vikāra
Sanskrit: पारद विकार
INTRO: The chronic condition caused by the use of unpurified or excessive dose of purified mercury (Pārada) may be known as Pārada Vikāra.
SYMPTOMS: Sinking of the nose bridge, sinusitis, premature falling of teeth, ulceration of nose and eyes, erysipelas, round elevated patches, headache, discolouration of the skin, formation of tender nodules with swelling in the scrotum, paralysis, extreme burning sensation in the bones, rigidity, fistula etc. are the signs and symptoms caused by the mercury poisoning.
TREATMENT: Sprinkling of cold water or ice bag on the hand, if the patient is restless
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Nārikela Jala (coconut water )-100 to 500 ml. to be taken many times a day. 2. Taṇḍula (rice) with Dadhi (curd) as much as required. 3. Soup of Mudga (phaseolus bean) -250 to 500 ml. to be taken with 100 to 200 g. Śarkarā (raw sugar) two time in a day 4. Decoction of equal part of Triphalā, rhizome of Kaṭukī root of Śatāvarī (wild asparagus), leaf of Paṭola (a variety of small cucumber-snake gourd), stem of Guḍūcī, whole plant of Parpaṭa (five leaved fumitory)-14 to 28 ml. to be taken twice in a day. 5. Śuddha Gandhaka-250 mg. to be taken with 4 to 6 g. honey twice a day.
PATHYA: As given under Vātarakta or Kuṣṭha.
APATHYA: Seeds of Māṣa (black phaseolus bean), Masūra (lentil), Satīna (pea) and Kulattha (dolichos bean); Tila Piṣṭi (sesame paste); Kūṣmāṇḍa (a variety of pumpkin gourd-white gourd), fruit of Kāravellaka (bitter gourd), leaf of Sarṣapa (mustard) and Kadalī (plantain), fruit and leaf of Karkoṭaka; fruit of Pippalī, (long pepper), seed of Nirmalī (clearing nut), fruit of Kṛṣṇa Jīraka (caraway), Tāmra (copper), Taila (oils), and taking of food in Kānsya (bronze) vessels are harmful for the patient suffering from mercury poisoning.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Pāra Viṣa, Beng: Pārada Viṣa, Dogr: Pārā Viṣa, Guj: Pārā No Jhahara, Hind: Pārā Viṣa, Kan: Pādarasa Viṣa, Maly: Rasa Vikāram, Mra: Pārā Viṣa, Tam: Pādarasa Vidam, Tel: Pādarasa Vikāramulu, Eng: Mercurial poisoning

Title: Nāga Viṣa
Sanskrit: नाग विष
SYMPTOMS: Loss of appetite, paroxysms of emesis, sweet and irony taste in the mouth, blue line in the gums, extreme burning in the abdomen, irritation of the throat, flatulence, colicy pain in the abdomen, black clay stools, cold sweat, vertigo, tremors mental derangement, paralysis and unconsciousness are the sign and symptoms of Nāga Viṣa. In the female abortion occurs frequently.
TREATMENT: Ensure emesis by the use of 1 litre decoction of seed of Madanaphala (emetic nut). It should be under take n in the guidance of the physician.
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Mix Śuddha Gandhaka (purified sulphur)- 1 g. in 1 litre of water and take in draughts many times a day. 2. Eraṇḍa Taila (castor oil)- 50 ml. to be taken with 250 ml. milk once a day, 3. 50 g. ghee to be taken with warm water or 250 ml. milk three times a day. 4. Yaśada Puṣpa (Zinc oxide purified)- 60 to 120 mg. to be taken with honey three times a day. 5. Use sulphur spring water for bath and internally.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: Following items may be used under expert guidance:- 1. Śuddha Ahiphena (purified opium)- 30 to 60 mg. to be taken with 100 to 250 ml. milk and 10 to 25 g. ghee. 2. Ahiphenāsava: 7 to 14ml. to be taken with equal quantity of water after meal two times a day. 3. Kanakāsava: 14 to 28 ml. to be taken with equal quantity of water after meal two times a day.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Sīsā Viṣa, Beng: Nāga Viṣa, Dogr: Sikkā Viṣa, Guj: Sīso No Jhahara, Hind: Sīse Kā Viṣa, Kan: Siṣā Viṣa, Maly: Nakam Viṣam, Mra: Siṣā Ce Viṣa, Ori: Sīṣā Viṣa, Tam: Karu Vaṅga Vidam, Eng: Lead poisoning

Title: Malla-Vikāra (Arsenic Poisoning)
Sanskrit: मल्लविकार
SYMPTOMS: Within half an hour of ingestion of arsenic, headache blurred vision, swelling in the pit of eyes; acute burning in the throat, stomach and intestines accompanied with violent vomits, colicy pain in the abdomen and diarrhoea; spasm in the body, excessive thirst, tremors, patches in the skin occur with slowing down of breathing and sinking of the heart and collapse.
TREATMENT: Call a specialist as early as possible and meanwhile give the following preliminary treatment. 1. Warm the patient with hot water Bottle. 2. Ensure emesis with:- A. Decoction of seed of Madanaphala (emetic nut)- 1 lit. B. Warm water 1 lit. and salt 50 g. C. Eraṇḍa Taila (castor oil)-100 ml. with warm water 1 lit. D. Give ice for sipping.
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. 50 ml. of Tila Taila (gingelly oil), 50 ml. of Eraṇḍa Taila (castor oil) with 250 ml. Dugdha (milk) to be taken once a day. 2. 50 g. ghee in 250 ml. milk to be taken three times a day. 3. Mṛgamada (Musk) 30 to 60 mg. to be taken with honey sufficient to make a paste.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Makaradhvaja Vaṭī: 1 to 3 Vaṭī to be taken with honey sufficient to make a paste.
REGIONAL NAMES:

Title: Dūṣī Viṣa
Sanskrit: दूषी विष
INTRO: The use of mild poisons for a longer period leads to the condition known as Dūṣī Viṣa.
SYMPTOMS: Diarrhoea, discolouration, unusual feeling of small and taste, thirst diminished voice, vomiting, giddiness, fainting are the symptoms caused by the slow poisoning.
TREATMENT: Induce emesis (Vamana) with 1. Decoction of seed of Madanaphala (emetic nut)-1 liter to be taken with Saindhava (rock salt)-50 g. and honey- 50 g. 2. Eraṇḍa Taila (castor oil)-12 to 24 g. to be taken with 100 to 250 ml. milk.
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Powder of equal parts of fruit of Pippalī (long pepper), Kaṭa Tṛna, rhizome of Jaṭāmānsī (spikenard), Kaivarta Mustaka and Sauvarcala Lavaṇa-3 to 6 g. to be taken with 4 to 6 g. honey and ghee. 2. Ghṛta Siddha with equal part of Kalka (paste) of fruit of Pippalī (long pepper), Gandhatṛṇa, rhizorne of Jaṭāmānsī (spikenard), bark of Lodhra, seed of Elā (lesser cardamom), roots of Mustaka (motha), Tagara (valerian), Kuṣṭha (koot) and Yaṣṭimadhu (glycyrrhiza), wood of Candana (sandal), Śuddha Gairika (purified ochre), and Sauvarcala Lavaṇa to be taken in 12 to 24 g. dose with 100 ml. warm water.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Dūṣī Viṣa, Kan: Kame Sagu Meḍḍeḍu, Maly: Alpavīryathodum, Kutiya Viṣam, Mra: Dūṣi Viṣa, Tam: Valukkunriyā Viḍam, Tel: Peṭṭuḍu/Mattu Mandu, Eng: Slow cumulative poisoning

Title: Āhāra Viṣa
Sanskrit: आहार विष
SYMPTOMS: If a person suffers from chronic food poisoning, his body becomes pale, thin, and he has drowsiness, swelling in the limbs, pain in the Marmas like heart and head, fever, diarrhoea, distension of abdomen. In case of the acute poisoning vomiting or diarrhoea and collapse may also occur.
TREATMENT: 1. Eraṇḍa Taila (castor oil)-14 to 28 ml. to be taken with 100 ml. warm water for purgation. 2. Decoction of seed of Madanaphala (emetic nut) 1 litre to be used for emesis. 3. Saindhava Lavaṇa (rook salt)-50 g. in warm water 1 litre, to be used for emesis. 4. Increase use of ghee in food. 5. Massage with Ghṛta Siddha with the decoction of root of Aṅkoṭha.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Nāgadantī Ghṛta: 14 to 28 g, to be taken with 100 ml. warm water. 1. Ajīta Agada: l2 to 24 g. to be taken with 100 to 250 ml. milk twice a day. 2. Daśāṅga Agada: 12 to 24 g. to be taken with 100 to 250 ml. milk twice a day. It is specially useful in poisonous symptoms resulting from helminths. 3. Gandhahasti Agada: 6 to 12 g. to be taken with 100 to 250 ml. milk twice a day. 4. Mahā Gandhahasti Agada: 6 to 12 g. to be taken with 100 to 250 ml. milk twice a day. 5. Mahā Sugandhi Agada: Lepa (plaster) for external use in Sarpa Daṁśa (snake bite). 6. Amṛta Ghṛta: 12 to 24 g. to be taken with 100 to 250 ml. milk twice a day. 7. Taṇḍulīyaka Ghṛta: 12 to 24 g. to be taken with 100 to 250 ml. milk twice a day. 8. Mṛtasañjīvanī Agada: Lepa (plaster) for external application. 9. Śirīṣāriṣṭa: 14 to 28 ml. to be taken with equal quantity of water after meal twice a day.
PATHYA: Taṇḍula (rice) particularly of Śāli and Ṣaṣṭi varieties, Seed of Āḍhakī (Pigeon pea and Satīna (pea); leaves of Taṇḍulīyaka (a variety of amaranth), Maṇḍūkaparṇī (pennywort) and Cāṅgerī (wood sorrel); leaf and fruit of Paṭola (a variety of small cucumber-snake gourd), Nāḍī Śāka, Candana (sandalwood), leaf of Śigru (horse radish), fruit of Āmalakī (embelic myrobalan), rhizome of Haridrā (turmeric), Keśara (saffron); Takra (butter milk), ghee, honey, Mṛgamada (musk); meat of peacock, partridge, falcon, deer, lizard; urine of cow and goat, and Saindhava (rock salt) are the useful articles of diet for the patients suffering from poisoning.
APATHYA: Amla, Lavaṇa Dravya; incompatible items of food very frequent meals are harmful. Avoid anger, exercise, fasting, smoking, day sleep, sweating and sexual intercourse and intake of betel and strong winds.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Āhāra Viṣa, Beng: Ahāraviṣa, Dogr: Khāne Se Jahara, Guj: Bhojana Nu Viṣa, Hind: Āhāra Viṣa, Kan: Āharādha Viṣa, Maly: ĀhāraViṣam, Mra: Āhāra Viṣa, Anna Tun Viṣa Leādhā, Tam: Ūnavū Viḍam, Tel: Āhāra Viṣam, Eng: Food poisoning

Title: VISŪCIKĀ
Sanskrit: विसूचिका
INTRO: Sudden onset of acute vomiting and diarrhoea accompanied by other constitutional symptoms may be due to Visūcikā.
SYMPTOMS: Acute vomiting and diarrhoea, thirst, Burning sensation, colicy pain in the abdomen, yawning, giddiness, spasm in the body, discolouracion of the skin, tremor, pain in the region of heart and hammering headache are the main signs and symptoms of Visūcikā.
TREATMENT: Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Kalka of root of Apārmārga (prickly chaff) -3 to 6 g. in sufficient water to be taken thrice a day. 2. Siddha jala with equal part of Lavaṅga (clove), root of Mustaka (motha), Jātīphala (nutmeg fruit) to be taken in 25 ml. dose or as required. 3. Juice of Palāṇḍu (onion)-7 to 14 ml. to be taken with powder of Marica (black pepper)-1 g. and Saindhava (rock-salt)-l g., thrice a day. 4. Decocrion of equal part of fruit pulp of Bilva (bad), Śuṇṭhī (dried ginger) and bark of Kaṭphala (box myrtle)-14 to 28 ml. to be taken thrice a day. 5. Pānaka of equal part of fruit pulp of Harītakī (chebulic myrobalan), fruit of Yavānī (ptychotis) and Trikaṭu to be taken frequently. 6. A Vaṭī made from equal part of Karpūra (camphor), Hiṅgu (asafoetida) fried in ghee, Marica (black pepper), bulb of Rasona (garlic), Purāṇa Guḍa (old jaggery) Weighing 250 mg. to be taken with warm water twice a day
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Citrakādi Vaṭī: 2 to 4 pills to be taken with warm water twice a day. 2. Śaṅkha Vaṭī: 2 to 4 Vaṭī to be taken with warm water twice a day. 3. Agnikumāra Rasa: 2 to 4 Vaṭī to be taken with warm water twice a day. 4. Rāma-Bāṇa Rasa: 60 to 120 mg. to be taken with 7 to 14 ml. leaf juice of Bilva (bael) twice a day.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Veda Bāmī, Beng: Visūcikā, Ola Oṭhā, Dogr: Haja, Guj: Visūcikā, Hind: Āntra Śotha, Kan: Vāntibhedhī, Maly: Visūcikā, Kolarā Rogam, Mra: Visūcikā, Tam: Vanthi Bedhi, Tel: Kalarā, Eng: Gastroenteritis

Title: VISARPA EVAṀ VISPHOṬA
Sanskrit: विसर्प एवं विस्फोट
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Purā Ratnā Mala, Beng: Visarpa, Visphoṭaka, Dogr: Kālarātra, Guj: Rātava, Phoḍko, Hind: Phapholā Paḍanā, Kan: Sarpasuṭṭu, Bokke Akkī, Maly: Polukan, Visarpam, Mra: Ghavarc, Jalalya Sārkhe Phoḍa, Ori: Bisīphoṭaka, Tam: Koppulam, Tel: Sarpi, Eng: Erysipelas and eruptions

Title: Visarpa
Sanskrit: विसर्प
SYMPTOMS: Rapid spreadings inflammation of skin, with throbbing or prickly or stabbing pain, lassitude, horripilation, deep pink coloured patches with itching and waxy to touch are the general sign and symptoms of Visarpa.
TREATMENT: Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: l. Decoction of equal part of Madanaphala (emetic nut), root of Yaṣṭimadhu (glycyrrhiza), bark of Nimba (neem) root of Indravāruṇī (colocynth)-14 to 28 ml. to be taken for Vamana (emesis). 2. Decoction of equal part of leaf of Paṭola (a variety of small cucumber-snake gourd), bark of Nimba (neem), wood of Rakra Candana (red sandal), roots of Mustaka (motha) and Mūrvā, rhizome of Kaṭukī, whole plants of Pātāla Garuḍī and Yavāsā (camel's thorn), stem of Guḍūcī-14 to 28 ml. to be taken twice a day.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Amṛtādi Kvātha: 14 to 28 ml. to be taken twice a day. 2. Bhūnimbādi Kvātha: 14 to 28 ml. to be taken thrice a day. 3. Gandhaka Rasāyana: 120 to 250 mg. to be taken with 4 to 6 g. honey twice a day. 4. Navakārṣika Guggulu: 2 to 4 pills to be taken with warm water twice a day 5. Tikta Gṛuta: 12 to 24 g. to be taken with warm water twice a day.
PATHYA: Seeds of old Yava (barley), Godhūma (wheat), Ṣaṣṭi and Śāli varieties of rice, seeds of Masūra (lentil), Caṇaka (gram) and Kaṅgu (a variety of coarse grain), fruit of Kāravellaka (bitter gourd), Śirīṣa, Drākṣā. (raisin or grape fruit), fruit of Dāḍima (pomegranate), fruit rind of Āmalakī (embelic myrobalan), Butter, milk, ghee and meat soup are the useful articles of diet for the patient of Visarpa.
APATHYA: Amla, Lavaṇa and Kaṭu Rasa, Guru Dravya, Kulattha (dolichos bean), Tila (Sesame seed); bulb of Rasona (garlic) are harmful for the patient of Visarpa. Anger and grief; suppression of calls of nature, unnatural postures, exercise, sexual intercourse, walking, exposure to sun and day sleep should be avoided.
REGIONAL NAMES:

Title: Visphoṭa
Sanskrit: विस्फोट
INTRO: Visphoṭa is characterised by the bullous eruptions on the skin accompanied by fever. Its other symptoms are headache intense pain in the body and joints, loss of appetite itching, burning sensation and pus formation.
TREATMENT: Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Decoction of equal part of whole plant of Kirātatikta (chirara), rhizeme of Vacā (sweet flag), leaf of Vāsā (vasaka) Fruit rinds ot Vibhītaka (beleric myrobalan), Harītakī (cheublic myrobalan) and Āmalakī (embelic myrobalan), bark of Kuṭaja (kurchi), leaves of Paṭola (a variety of small cucumber-snake gourd) and Nimba (neem)-14 to 28 ml. to be taken wiih 5 to 10 g. honey twice a day. 2. Decoction of equal part of Pañcamūla, stem of Dāruharidrā (barberry) and Guḍūcī, root of Uśīra (khas), whole plant of Yavāsā (camel's thorn), fruit of Dhānyaka (coriander), root of Mustaka (motha)-14 to 28 ml. to be taken thrice a day. 3. Decoction of equal part of Guḍūcī, leaf of Paṭola (a variety of small cucumder-snake gourd), whole plant of Kirātatikta (chirata) and Parpaṭa (five leaved fumitory), Khadira (khair), and root of Mustaka (motha) 14 to 28 ml. to be taken thrice a day.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Paṅcatikta Ghṛta: 12 to 24 g. to be taken with warm water twice a day.
PATHYA: Ṣaṣṭi variety of rice, seeds of Yava (barley), Mudga (phaseoius bean), Masūra (lentil) and Makuṣṭha (aconite leaved kidney bean); fruit of Kāravellaka (bitter gourd), Vetsāgra (cane shoot), leaves of Nimba (neem) and Paṭola (snake gourd); ghee and soup of bird's meat are useful for Visphoṭa,
APATHYA: Amla, Lavaṇa and Kaṭu Rasa, Rūkṣa and Uṣṇa Dravya; seeds of Māṣa (black phaseolus bean), Kulattha (dolichos bean) and Tila (sesame) leafy vegetables incompatible items of food are harmful for the patient of Visphoṭa. Avoid fomentation, exercise, Sexual intercourse, anger, exposure to sun, suppression of emesis, day sleep and exposure to eastern wind.
REGIONAL NAMES:

Title: VṚKKA ROGA
Sanskrit: वृक्क रोग
SYMPTOMS: The cardinal symptom of kidney disorders is alteration in the urine. Other important symptoms are pallor of the body and oedema particularly around the eyelids. Pain and symptoms connected with the passing of urine viz. increased frequency of micturation, incontinence of urine, retention of urine, suppression or the passage of large quantity of urine or the passage of blood with urine may also be present. In the chronic stage toxic symptoms appear and patient may become unconscious.
TREATMENT: Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Decoction of seed of Kulattha (dolichos bcan)-14 to 28 ml. to be taken twice a day. 2. Decoction of fruit of Gokṣura (small caltrops)-14 to 28 ml. to be taken twice a day. 3. Decoction of root of Pāṣāṇabheda (saxifrage)-14 to 28 ml. to be taken twice a day. 4. Decoction of bark of Varuṇa-14 to 28 ml. to be taken twice a day.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Śuddha Śilājatu: 1 g. to be taken with 4 to 6 g. honey twice a day. 2. Maheśvara Vaṭī: 60 to 120 mg. to be taken 4 to 6 g. honey twice a day. 3. Śivā Guṭikā: 1 to 2 Vaṭī to be taken with warm water twice a day. 4. Punarnavā-Maṇḍūra: 2 to 4 Vaṭī to be taken with warm water twice a day. 5. Gokṣurādi Guggulu: 1 to 2 Vaṭī to be taken with warm water twice a day.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Virikha Śotha, Beng: Vṛka Vikāra, Dogr: Gurde Ke Roga, Guj: Gurdā Nā Raga, Sojo, Hind: Gurde Kī Bīmārī, Kan: Mūtra Koṣa Roga, Maly: Vṛkka Rogam, Mra: Mūtra Pinḍa Śotha, Panj: Gurda De Raga, Tam: Kunḍikkay Noy, Eng: Diseases of the kidney

Title: VRAṆA-ŚOTHA
Sanskrit: व्रण-शोथ
SYMPTOMS: Vraṇa has three stages viz. Āma, Pacyamāna and Pakva. In Āma stage there is swelling, tenderness and low fever. In Pacyamāna stage there is a change in the colour of the skin, stabbing or throbbing pain, intense burning with fever and accumulation of pus. In the Pakva stage pain is comparatively less, and shrinking of the skin over the boil and bursting occur.
TREATMENT: Treatment
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Triphalā Kvātha: 14 to 28 ml. to be taken with Śuddha Guggulu 2 to 4 g. twice a day. 2. Saptāṅga Guggulu: 1 to 2 Vaṭī to be taken with warm water twice a day.
PATHYA: Madhura, Tikta and Kaṣāya Rasa; Uṣṇa and Snigdha Dravya; old Śāli and Ṣaṣti varieties of rice, Yava (barley), Godhūma (wheat), Lājāmaṇḍa (pop of paddy), seeds of Masūra (lentil), Āḍhakī (pigeon pea), Mudga (phaseolus bean) and Tila (sesame); Vārtāka (brinjal), Karkaṭī, (a variety of small cucumber), fruits of Paṭola and Kāravellaka (bitter gourd); leaf of Nimba (neem); Mūlaka (radish), leaves of Vāstūka (a variety of chenopodium) and Jīvanti; Kadalī (banana), fruit of Dāḍima (pomegranate), Drākṣā (raisin or grape fruit), Sarṣapa Taila (mustard oil), ghee, honey and Saindhava (rocksalt) are the useful articles of diet for the patients of Vraṇa Śotha.
APATHYA: Amla, Lavaṇa and Kaṭu Rasa; Śimbi (legumes); Navīna Anna (freshly harvested grain), Satīna (pea bean), seeds of Māṣa (black phaseolus bean) and Kulattha (dolichos bean); Patra Śāka (leafy vegetables), Vilepī; milk products, curd, sugarcane products, wines, Tāmbūla (betel leaf) incompatible food are harmful for the patient of Vraṇa Śotha. Excessive long walks, sedantary habits, exposure to sun and wind, anger, excessive joy, fright, talking in high pitch, Nasya and Vamana should be avoided.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Braṇaja Śotha, Beng: Braṇa Śotha, Guj: Gaḍgumbārā Sojo, Hind: Sūjana, Kan: Hunnīna Bavū, Maly: Vrana Vīkam, Mra: Sūja, Ori: Bātha, Tam: Vīkkam, Tel: Vraṇa Vāpu, Eng: Inflammation

Title: VṚṢAṆA VṚDDHI EVAṀ ŚOTHA
Sanskrit: वृषण वृद्धि एवं शोथ
INTRO: Inflammation or enlargement of the scrotum occurs due to involvement of the sacs, the spermatic cord, tunica vaginalis is and testis. Sometimes, enlargement also occurs due to hernia.
TREATMENT: Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Śuddha Guggulu-2 to 4 g. to be taken with Gomūtra (cow's urine)-7 to 14 ml. twice a day. 2. Daśamūla Kvātha -14 to 28 ml. to be taken with Eraṇḍa Taila (castor oil)- 7 to 14 ml. once a day. 3.Decoction of Triphalā-14to 28 ml. to be taken with Gomūtra (cow’s urine)- 7 to 14 ml. twice a day. 4. Harītakī boiled in Gomūtra (cow's urine)-1 to 3 g. and Eraṇḍa Taila (castor oil)-7 to 14 ml. to be taken with Saindhava (rock-salt)-1 g. twice a day. 5. Kalka of fruit rind of Harītakī (chebulic myrobalan)-6 to 12 g. fried in Eraṇḍa Taila (castor oil)-7 to 14 ml. to be taken with powdered fruit of Pippalī (long pepper)- 1 g. and Saindhava (rock-salt)-1 g. twice a day.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Rāsnādi Kvātha: 14 to 28 ml. to be taken thrice a day.
PATHYA: As for Śotha.
APATHYA: Snigdha Dravya, Māṣa (black phaseolus bean), Upodikā Śāka, curd and milk are harmful for the patient of Vṛṣaṇa Vṛddhi and Śotha. Riding, exercise, touring, fasting, sexual intercourse, suppression of calls of nature and sitting posture should be avoided.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Koṣa Vṛdhi, Koṣa Śotha, Beng: Vṛṣaṇa Śotha, Dogr: Padalū Sojana, Guj: Vadra Bharaka, Pothavo Sujon, Hind: Phote Kā Sūjana, Kan: Andavāyu, Anḍavṛdhi, Maly: Muska Vikkam, Āntravayu, Mra: Anḍakoṣa Bṛdhi , Anḍakoṣa Suja, Ori: Kurunḍā, Koṣabṛddhi, Tam: Virai Vikkam, Eng: Inflammation and enlargement of the scrotum, orchitis

Title: ŚIRO-ROGA
Sanskrit: शिरोरोग
INTRO: The feeling of any type of discomfort or pain in the head may be defined as Śiro Roga. The symptoms and treatment of common types of headache (Śiraḥ Śūla) and other related conditions of the skull are as follows.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Muranvisa, Murāra Kamorani, Beng: Śiro Roga, Dogr: Śire De Roga, Guj: Mathā Nā Roga, Hind: Sira Ke Roga, Kan: Tāleya Roga, Maly: Śiro Rogam, Mra: Siro Roga, Ori: Munḍo Bādha, Tam: Mandai Noy

Title: Śiraḥ Śūla (Headache)
Sanskrit: शिरःशूल
INTRO: Headache may be caused by the vitiation of Vāta, Pitta, Kapha and Rakta or it may be due to Kṣaya and Kṛmi. Vātika Śiraḥ Śūla: This type of headache generally occurs without any obvious cause, increases in the night and is relieved by the warm application and bandage. Paittika Śiraḥ Śūla: The headache which is relieved in the night or by the cold applications, patient has the burning sensation in the eyes, nose and feeling of heat in the head is known as Paittika Śiraḥ Śūla. If the patient in addition to the above symptoms have tenderness in the head this condition is known as Raktaja Śiraḥ Śūla. Kaphja Śiraḥ Śūla: Pecular feeling of stiffness and heaviness in the head, swelling of the eyes and face are the symptoms of headache cause by Kapha.
TREATMENT: Treatment
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Pathyādi Kvātha: 14 to 28 ml. to be taken thrice a day. 2. Godantī Bhasma: 1 g., Pravāla Bhasma-180 mg. to be taken with 4 to 6 g. honey thrice a day. 3. Mahālakṣmī Vilāsa Rasa: 60 to 120 mg. to be taken with 4 to 6 g. honey twice a day. 4. Śiraḥ-Śūlādi-Vajra Rasa: 1 Vaṭī to be taken with 4 to 6 g. honey twice a day.
REGIONAL NAMES:

Title: Ardhāva-Bhedaka
Sanskrit: अर्धावभेदक
INTRO: The pain which occurs only on one side of the head is known as Ardhāva Bhedaka. In this condition patient has acute pain in head like splitting, cutting or burning confined to one side of the head, particularly in the regions of temple, ear, eye brow and half of the forehead.
TREATMENT: Treatment
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Tribhuvanakīrtī Rasa: 1 to 2 Vaṭī to be taken two times with milk 100 to 250 ml. 2. Godantī Bhasma: 1 g. to be taken with Laghu Pañcamūla Kvātha 12 to 24 ml. twice a day. 3. Godantī Miśraṇa: 1 g. to be taken with 100 to 250 ml. milk twice a day.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Adhā Kapāli Nurāra Viṣa, Beng: Ādhā Kapālī, Dogr: Ardha Śira Pīḍa, Guj: Ādha Śīṣī, Hind: Ādhā Kapāla, Ādhā Śīśī, Kan: Areṭale Novu, Maly: Orūchenīkuṭṭu, Mra: Ardhaśiśī, Ori: Adhā Kapāli, Tam: Oṭraiththalai Valī, Tel: Tala Okavaipu/Pārśva Noppi, Eng: Hemicrania

Title: Sūryāvarta
Sanskrit: सूर्यावर्त
INTRO: The headache which begins with the sunrise, increases up to the mid day, thereafter starts decreasing and is relieved with the sunset is known as Sūryāvarta. It occurs particularly behind the eye brow.
TREATMENT: Treatment
PATHYA: Śāli and Ṣaṣṭi varities of rice; fruits of Paṭola (a variety of small cucumber snake gourd) and Śigru (horse radish); leaf of Vāstūka (a variety of chenopodium), fruit of Kāravellaka (bitter gourd), Kumārī (aloe); fruit of Drākṣā (raisin or grape) and Āmra (mango), fruit rind of Āmalakī (embelic myrobalan), fruits of Dāḍima (pomegranate), Bījapūra (lemon) and Nārikela (coconut); Karpūra (camphor); roots of Uśīra (khas) and Mustaka (motha); whole plan of Bhṛṅgarāja; milk, Takra (butter milk), Kāñjī, old ghee; and moonlight are useful for the patient of Śiro-Roga.
APATHYA: Avoid suppression of natural urges, tooth brushing and day sleep.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Sūrya Kapālī Murārviṣa, Beng: Adha Kapālī, Dogr: Sūjā De Dard, Sūnyā Chaluleā, Sirepiḍā Honi, Guj: Ardho Magasa Dukhi, Hind: Sūryavarta, Kan: Suryodayadoda Gudida Talenovu, Maly: Kotīnjī, Mra: Suryavarta, Tam: Sūrya Varieththalalai Vali, Tel: Poddupoḍupu Noppi, Eng: Chronic sinusitis

TREATMENT: Treatment

TREATMENT: Treatment

Title: Arūnṣikā
Sanskrit: अरूंषिका
INTRO: Due to the disorders of Kapha and Rakta or due to infestation of lice etc. suppurating pimples having numerous opening develop in the scalp and this condition is known as Arūnṣikā. The affected part of the scalp becomes wet due to the discharge from the pimples.
TREATMENT: Treatment
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Chiteli Ghā, Dogr: Śirapakha, Hind: Sira Kī Phunsiā, Kan: Talehunnu, Maly: Sirsilluntakunna, Mra: Khavaḍe, Ori: Badā Ghā, Tam: Mandaici Srangu, Eng: Boils in scalp

Title: ŚĪTAPITTA
Sanskrit: शीतपित्त
INTRO: The appearance of intensely itching wheels over the body, having elevated centres surrounded by the patches of redness is known as Śītapitta. The wheels tend to disappear in a day or two and sometimes accompanied by fever, vomiting and burning sensation.
TREATMENT: Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Śuddha Svarṇa Gairika (ochre)-1 to 2 g. to be taken with 4 to 6 g. honey twice a day. 2. Triphalā Kvātha-14 to 28 ml. to be taken with 4 to 6 g. honey twice a day. 3. Decoction of equal part of stem of Guḍūcī, and leaf of Paṭola (a variety of small cucumber-snake gourd)-14 to 28 ml. to be taken twice a day. 4. Decoction of equal part of stem of Guḍūcī, rhizome of Haridrā (turmeric), bark of Nimba (neem)-14 to 28 ml. to be taken with honey twice a day. 5. Trikaṭu Cūrṇa 1 to 2 g. to be taken with 4 to 6 g. honey twice a day along with massage of Sarṣapa Taila (mustard oil).
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Haridrā Khaṇḍa: 3 to 6 g. to be taken with 50 ml. water twice a day. 2. Sūtaśekhara Rasa: 60 to 250 mg. to taken with juice of Ārdraka (ginger)-5 ml. twice a day.
PATHYA: Old Śāli variety of rice, Mudga (Phaseolus bean), soup of Kulattha (dolichos bean); fruits of Kāravellaka (bitter gourd) and Śigru (horse radish); leaf of Upodikā (Indian spinach), Vetasa Śuga (cane shoot), Śuṣka Mūlaka (dried radish); curd and honey are the useful articles of diet for the patients of Śītapitta.
APATHYA: Madhura and Amla Rasa, Guru Dravya; fresh Guḍa (jaggery); freshly prepared Madya (wine); Matsya (fish) and day sleep are harmful for the patients of Śītapitta.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Kaisle Ūṭhā, Cākā Uṭhā, Udarda, Beng: Śītapitta, Udarda, Koṭha, Dogr: Sojasī, Chapa Khu Sirkoy, Khorka, Tharapadsadna, Guj: Śīṭapitta, Hind: Pitta Uṭhanā, Pittī Uchalanā, Kan: Pittada Gandde, Sirkoya, khorākā, Maly: Chorinju Tatippeu, Vāttapinārū, Vāttapuru, Mra: Śītapitta, Pitāmbī Vā Gandhī Uṭhāṇe, Ori: Agiyā Vāta, Panj: Pittī, Tam: Thaḍippu, Tel: Daddurlū, Eng: Urticaria

Title: ŚŪLA

INTRO: Colic type of pain in the abdomen is known as Śūla. The symptoms and treatment of common types of Śūla are as follow.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Peṭera Viṣa, Beng: Śūla, Dogr: Śūla, Derda, Guj: Śūḍa, Hind: Śūla, Kan: Hoṭṭe Novū, Maly: Vayathū Vedanā, Mra: Poṭa Dukhī, Ori: Peṭāmāḍa, Peṭakamuḍa, Tam: Sūlai, Tel: Kaḍupu Noppi, Eng: Colic

Title: Āmaja Śūla
Sanskrit: आमजशूल
SYMPTOMS: Intense colic pain which increases after taking food, anorexia, salivation, nausea, vomiting, retention of gases, rumbling noises in the abdomen, constipation, pain in the body are the main signs and symptoms of Āmaja Śūla.
TREATMENT: Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Powder of equal part of Saindhava (rock-salt), Kṛṣṇa Lavaṇa, Viḍa Lavaṇa, Pañcakola, Hiṅgu (asafoetida) fried in ghee to be taken in 12 g. dose with warm water twice a day. 2. Daśamūla Kvātha -14 to 28 ml. to be taken with Saindhava (rock salt)-1 g., Yavakṣāra-1 g. twice a day. 3. Decoction of bark of Śigru (horse radish)-14 to 28 ml. to be taken with fried Hiṅgu (asafoetida)-1 g. and Yavakṣāra-1 g. twice a day. 4. Yavāgu Siddha with decoction of equal part of fruit and root of Pippalī (long pepper), root of Citraka (leadwort), Cavya, Śuṇṭhī (dried ginger) to be taken in 250 g. dose twice a day. 5. Hiṅgu (asafoetida) fried in ghee to be taken in 1 g. dose with Guḍa (jageery) twice a day. 6. Nārikela Kṣāra-1 g. to be taken with water thrice a day.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Hiṅgvāṣṭaka Cūrṇa: 1 to 3 g. to be taken with warm water thrice a day. 2. Śivakṣāra Pācana Cūrṇa: 1 to 3 g. to be taken with warm water thrice a day. 3. Citrakādi Vaṭī: 1 to 2 Vaṭī to be taken with warm water thrice a day. 4. Lasunādi Vaṭī: 1 to 2 Vaṭī to be taken with warm water thrice a day.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Āmāsaya Viṣa, Beng: Āmaja Śūla, Dogr: Āmaśūla, Ajarna Kanne Derde, Guj: Ajīraṇa, Hind: Āmaśūla, Kan: Amadanovu, Maly: Ajīrnam Kondulla Vayaru Vedana, Mra: Amaja Poṭa Dukhī, Tam: Mela Vayiṭru Vali, Tel: Ajīrna Noppi, Eng: Intestinal colic

Title: Ajīrṇa Janya Śūla
Sanskrit: अजीर्णजन्य शूल
INTRO: The colic pain caused by the indigestion is known as Ajīrṇa Janya Śūla.
TREATMENT: Treatment
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Narsārādi Cūrṇa: 1 to 2 g. to be taken with warm water thrice a day. 2. Kṣāra-Rāja: 1 to 2 Vaṭī to be taken with warm water thrice a day. 3. Kuverākṣa Vaṭī: 2 to 3 Vaṭī to be taken warm water thrice a day.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Badha Hajami Janita Viṣa, Beng: Ajīrṇa Janya Śūla, Dogr: Bedhajamī, Guj: Ajiraṇathi Dhukhāvo, Aphāro, Hind: Ajīrṇa Śūla, Maly: Dahanake Tukonduntā, Kunnā Vedanā, Kan: Ajīrṇa Dindada Hotte Novu, Mra: Ajīrṇa Vā Poṭdukhī, Tam: Ama Śūlai, Eng: Pain due to indigestion

Title: Anna-Drava Śūla Evaṁ Pariṇāma Śūla
