INTRO: Please see Āmāśaya Vraṇa.
REGIONAL NAMES:

Title: Kṛmi-Janya Śūla
Sanskrit: कृमिजन्य शूल
SYMPTOMS: The colic pain caused by the intestinal worms is known as Kṛmijanya Śūla. Its other symptoms are loss of appetite, diarrhea, lack of energy, fever and giddiness.
TREATMENT: For the pain, the treatment described for Āmaja Śūla should be given. The treatment of worms should be prescribed as indicated under Kṛmi Roga.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Pelu Janita Śūla, Beng: Kṛmijanya Śūla, Dogr: Kiḍākanne Derda, Hind: Kṛmijanya Śūla, Kan: Hulūvinindadā Hotte Novu, Maly: Kṛmijanya Vedanā, Mra: Kṛmijpoṭa Dūkhī, Tam: Kirumī Vayitru Vali

Title: Pittāśmarī-Janya-Śūla
Sanskrit: पित्ताश्मरीजन्य शूल
INTRO: The pain caused by the gall-stone is known as Pittāśmarī Janya Śūla. The pain is felt in the right upper abdomen and may be referred to right scapula. Fever, fat intolerance and jaundice may also occur.
TREATMENT: Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Powder of Saindhava (rock-salt)-2 g., Trikaṭu-2 g., Śaṅkha Bhasma (conch)- 1 g., Śuddha Hiṅgu (asafoetida)-1 g. to be taken with warm water twice a day. 2. Powder of equal part of Hiṅgu (asafoetida) fried in ghee, Sauvaracala Lavaṇa, Śuṇṭhī (dried ginger)-1 to 3 g. to be taken with warm water twice a day. 3. Decoction of equal part of Triphalā and fruit pulp of Āragvadha (cassia)- 14 to 28 ml. to be taken with 4 to 6 g. honey and 5 to 10 g. Śarkarā (raw sugar) twice a day. 4. Decoction of equal part of Triphalā, bark of Nimba (neem), rhizome of Kaṭukī, fruit pulp of Āragvadha (cassia)-14 to 28 ml. to be taken when cold with 4 to 6 g. honey twice a day. 5. Treatment prescribed under Kāmalā may also be given.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Pittāśmarī Janita Śūla, Beng: Pittāśmarī-Janya Śūla, Dogr: Pitta De Pathrī Kanne Derda, Guj: Pathrī, Hind: Pittāśaya Kī Aśmarī, Pitte Kī Patharī, Kan: Mūtradakallina Novū, Maly: Pittāśmarī Janya Vedanā, Mra: Pittāśmarī Janya Poṭa Dūkhī, Tam: Mutradakallina Novu, Eng: Biliary colic

Title: Vṛkka Śūla (Renal Colic)
Sanskrit: वृक्कशूल
SYMPTOMS: Colic resulting from gravel in urethra, ureter, bladder and kidney accompanied by scanty painful urination with blood may be known as Vṛkka Śūla.
TREATMENT: Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Powdered root of Bījapūra (lemon)-1 g. to be taken with water twice a day. 2. Decoction of root of Eraṇḍa (castor)-14 to 28 ml. to be taken with 1 g. Yavakṣāra twice a day.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Trivikrama Rasa: 60 to 120 mg. to be taken with honey sufficient to make a paste twice a day. 2. Treatment prescribed under Aśmarī, Mūtra kṛcchra etc. may also be followed.
REGIONAL NAMES:

Title: ŚOPHA (ŚOTHA)
Sanskrit: शोफ (शोथ)
INTRO: Accumulation of fluid in the skin and subcutaneous tissues is known as Śopha (Śhotha).
SYMPTOMS: Pitting on pressure, oedema, heaviness in the body, horripilation, discolouration of the skin, are the general signs and symptoms of Śopha. Its common varieties are as follows. Vātaja Śopha (Hṛd-Janya Śopha) This type of oedema is caused by the diminished pumping power of the heart. The oedema first appears on the feet, and increases during the day and tends to subside in the night. On pressing, the skin is depressed but immediately after releasing the pressure regains its position. Pittaja Śopha (Yakṛt Janya Śopha) The oedema duc to the derangement of Yakṛt (liver) is known as Pittaja Śopha. It first appears on the abdomen and then gradually spreads up. Kaphaja Śopha (Vṛkka Janya Śopha) Oedema caused by the impaired function of kidneys is known as Kaphaja Śopha. It first appears in the pits of the eyes and later spread to the other parts of the body.
TREATMENT: Salt restricted diet should be given.
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Powder of Pippalī-1 g. to be taken with Gomūtra-7 to 14 ml. and Guggulu-1 g. twice a day. 2. Equal part of Gomūtra and Eraṇḍa Taila-14 to 28 ml. to be taken twice a day. 3. Powder of equal part of fruit rind of Harītakī (chebulic myrobalan) Śuṇṭhī (dried ginger), wood of Devadāru (deodar)-3 to 6 g. to be taken with milk twice a day. 4. Powder of equal part of whole plant of Kirātatikta (chirata) and Śuṇṭhī (dried ginger)-3 to 6 g. to be taken with Punarnvāṣṭaka Kvātha-14 to 28 ml. twice a day. 5. Powder of equal part of fruit rind of Harītakī (chebulic myrobalan) rhizome of Vacā (sweat flag), root of Rāsnā (Indian groundsel), fruit of Pippalī (long pepper), roots of Mustaka (motha), Śaṭī (zeodary) and Puṣkara (costus root), and Śuṇṭhī (dried ginger), mixed together with equal weight of powdered bark of Arjuna-3 to 6 g. to be taken with 100 to 250 ml. milk twice a day. 6. Decoction of equal part of wood of Devadāru (deodar), root of Punarnavā (pigweed), and Śuṇṭhī (dried ginger)-14 to 28 ml. to be taken with Gomūtra-7 to 14 ml. twice a day. 7. Decoction of equal part of root of Punarnavā (pigweed), bark of Nimba (neem), leaf of Paṭola (a variety of small cucumber), stem of Guḍūcī, wood of Devadāru (deodar), and fruit rind of Harītakī (chebulic myrobalan)-14 to 28 ml. to be taken twice a day. 8. Decoction of equal part of bark of Vāsā, Guḍūcī, whole plant of Bṛhatī (yellow berried night shade)-14 to 28 ml. to be taken with 4 to 6 g. honey twice a day.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Śuddha Śilājatu-1 g. to be taken with Triphalā-3 to 6 g. and 50 ml. warm water or 100 to 250 ml. milk or with powder of Haridarā (turmeric)-3 g. and Gomūtra (cow’s urine)-7 to 14 ml., twice a day. 2. Śivakṣāra Pācana Cūrṇa: 3 to 6 g. to be taken with warm water twice a day. 3. Vardhamāna Pippalī Yoga: Commencing dose is half Pippalī. It is to be taken under the guidance of the specialist. 4. Punarnavādi Kvātha: 14 to 28 ml. to be taken twice a day. 5. Gokṣūrādi Kvātha: 14 to 28 ml. to be taken twice a day. 6. Candraprabhā Vaṭī: 1 to 2 Vaṭī to be taken with warm water twice a day. 7. Ārogyavardhinī Vaṭī: 1 to 2 Vaṭī to be taken with warm water twice a day. 8. Hṛdayāraṇava Rasa: 60 to 120 mg. to be taken with honey to make a paste twice a day. 9. Śṛṅga Bhasma: 120 to 250 mg. to be taken with 4 to 6 g. honey twice a day. 10. Jahāra Moharā Piṣṭi: 60 to 120 mg. to be taken with honey to make a paste twice a day. 11. Hajaralayahūda Piṣṭi: 60 to 120 mg. to be taken with honey to make a paste twice a day. 12. Muktāśukti Piṣṭi: 60 to 120 mg. to be taken with honey to make a paste twice a day. 13. Punarnavā Maṇḍūra: 1 g. to to be taken with 100 to 250 ml. milk twice a day. 14. Maṇḍūra Bhasma: 1 g. to be taken with 100 to 250 ml. milk twice a day. 15. Punarvāsava: 14 to 28 ml. to be taken with equal quantity of water twice a day after meal. 16. Arjunāriṣṭa: 14 to 28 ml. to be taken with equal quantity of water twice a day. 17. Daśamūlāriṣṭa: 14 to 28 ml. to be taken equal quantity of water twice a day after meal.
PATHYA: Old Śāli variety of rice, seeds of Kulattha (dolichos bean), Yava (barley) and Mudga (phaseolus bean); Karkoṭakī (a variety of cucumber), leaf of Śigru (horse radish), Mūlaka (radish), leaf of Paṭola (a variety of small cucumber-snake gourd), whole plant of Punarnavā (pigweed), root of Rāsnā (Indian groundsel), fruit rind of Āmalakī (embelic myrobalan), milk and Takra (butter milk) are the useful articles of diet for the patient of Śopha.
APATHYA: Navīna Anna (freshly harvested cereals), Piṣṭamaya Anna, Amla Rasa, Guru Dravya, Śuṣka Śāka (dried vegetable), curd, salt, Madya (wine), incompatible items of food in diet are harmful for the patients of Śopha. Avoid day sleep, sexual intercourse, suppression of calls of nature and long walks. Treatment under Hṛdroga, Udararoga and Vṛkkaroga along with Pathya and Apathya thereto should be followed according to the cause of Śopha.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Phūlā, Bhikā, Beng: Śotha, Dogr: Śoja, Śojiśa, Guj: Sojo, Hind: Sūjana, Kan: Uṭā, Bāvū, Maly: Nīrū, Mra: Sūjā, Ori: Śotha, Śothaphūṭā, Tam: Sobai, Tel: Nañju/Vāpu, Eng: Oedema

Title: ŚLĪPADA
Sanskrit: श्लीपद
INTRO: Ślīpada is a progressive swelling of lower limb which generally develops after the attack of fever. In this condition due to solid oedema the foot and leg of the patient become hard like stone. Sometimes the disease also affects hand and scrotum.
TREATMENT: Complete rest during fever and maximum use of Rasona (garlic) in the food.
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Decoction of root or leaf or bark of Śakhoṭaka-14 to 28 ml. to be taken twice a day. 2. Powdered fruit rind of Harītakī (chebulic myrobalan) fried in Eraṇḍa Taila (castor oil) to be taken in 3 to 6 g. dose with warm water or 50 ml. milk twice a day.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Mañjiṣṭhādi Kvātha: 14 to 28 ml. to be taken twice a day. 2. Nityānanda Rasa: 1 to 2 Vaṭī to be taken with 50 ml. water twice a day.
PATHYA: Seeds of Yava (barley) and Kulattha (dolichos bean), Taṇḍula (rice); leaf of Paṭola (a variety of small cucumber), fruits of Śigru (horse radish) and Kāravellaka (bitter gourd); root of Punarnavā (pig weed); Mūlaka (radish), leaf of Upodikā (Indian spinach), bulb of Rasona (garlic); Eraṇḍa Taila (castor oil) are useful for the patient of Ślīpada.
APATHYA: Guru, Abhiṣyandi, Piṣṭamaya Dravya, milk products are harmful for the patient of Ślīpada.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Godhā Vāta, Kālā Gesiyā Roga, Beng: Godā Ślīpada, Dogr: Hāthī Pera, Guj: Hāthī Pāgā, Hind: Hāthī Pāv, Kan: Ane Kālu, Maly: Manthū, Mra: Haṭṭi Roga, Tam: Yanaikkal Noy, Tel: Bodakālu, Eng: Elephantiasis

Title: ŚVĀSA ROGA
Sanskrit: श्वासरोग
INTRO: Difficult or laboured breathing is known as Śvāsa Roga. In this condition the expiration of the patients is a forceful upward movement is like that of black smith’s air blower.
SYMPTOMS: The signs and symptoms of common types of Śvāsa Roga viz. Kṣudra Śvāsa and Tamaka Śvāsa are as follows. Kṣudra Śvāsa (Chronic Bronchitis): This is a mild type of Śvāsa Roga and its main symptom is dyspnoea on exertion. Tamaka Śvāsa (Bronchial Asthma): This disease come in the paroxysm of dyspnoea and during the attack, the patient goes in extreme agony, perceives darkness, feels thirst and becomes motionless. On account of frequent coughing, the patient faints and remains in extreme distress till phlegm is coughed out. On account of breathing difficulty in lying down position, the patient is unable to sleep. He gets some relief in sitting position. The disease is flared by clouds, cold water, cold wind, cold weather, and the diet which increases Kapha.
TREATMENT: Practice Prāṇāyāma, keep bowel clean by taking laxatives, take light diet in the night and use only warm water for drinking.
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Decoction of equal part of root of Vāsā (vasaka), rhizome of Haridrā (turmeric), stem of Guḍūcī, fruit of Kaṇṭakārī (yellow berried night shade)-14 to 28 ml. to be taken with 1 g. to powdered Marica (black pepper) twice a day. 2. Dhūmrapāna (smoking) of leaf of Dhattūra (datura).
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Elādi Cūrṇa: 1 to 3 g. to be taken with 4 to 6 g. honey twice a day. 2. Sitopalādi Cūrṇa: 1 to 3 g. to be taken with 4 to 6 g. honey twice a day. 3. Śṛṅgyādi Cūrṇa: 1 to 3 g. to be taken with 4 to 6 g. honey twice a day. 4. Tālisādi Cūrṇa: 1 to 3 g. to be taken with 4 to 6 g. honey twice a day. 5. Daśamūla Kvātha: 14 to 28 ml. to be taken twice a day. 6. Kaṇṭakāryādi Kvātha: 14 to 28 ml. to be taken twice a day. 7. Śṛṅgyādi Kvātha: 14 to 28 ml. to be taken twice a day. 8. Vāsādi Kvātha: 14 to 28 ml. to be taken twice a day. 9. Bhogottara Guṭikā: 500 mg. to 1 g. to be taken with 0.5 g. powdered fruit of Pippalī (long pepper) twice a day. 10. Khadirādi Vaṭī: 2 to 4 Vaṭī to be taken thrice a day. 11. Lavaṅgādi Vaṭī: 1 Vaṭī to be chewed six times a day. 12. Soma Yoga: 120 to 500 mg. to be taken with 4 to 6 g. honey twice a day. 13. Karvīrādi Yoga: 30 to 250 mg. to be taken with honey to make a paste twice a day. 14. Candrāmṛta Rasa: 120 to 250 mg. to be taken with 4 to 6 g. honey twice a day. 15. Abhraka Bhasma (plain): 120 to 250 mg. to be taken with honey to make a paste twice a day. 16. Mayūrapuccha Bhasma: 1 to 2 g. to be taken with honey to make a paste twice a day. 17. Apāmārga Kṣāra: 1 g. to be taken with warm water twice a day. 18. Arka Lavaṇa: 1 g. to be taken with warm water twice a day. 19. Bhāraṅgī Guḍa: 12 to 24 g. to be taken with warm water twice a day. 20. Agastya Harītakī Avaleha: 12 to 24 g. to be taken twice a day. 21. Cyavanprāśavaleha: 12 to 24 g. to be taken twice a day. 22. Citraka Harītakī Avaleha: 12 to 24 g. to be taken twice a day. 23. Vāsāvaleha: 12 to 24 g. to be taken twice a day. 24. Vyāghrīharītakī Avaleha: 12 to 24 g. to be taken twice a day. 25. Drākṣāriṣṭa: 14 to 28 ml. to be taken with equal quantity of water twice a day after meal. 26. Vāsāriṣṭa: 14 to 28 ml. to be taken with equal quantity of water twice a day after meal. 27. Kanakāsava: 5 to 10 ml. to be taken with equal quantity of water after meal. This medicine is to be used cautiously on account of its strong ingredients.
PATHYA: Old Śāli variety of rice, Kulattha (dolichos bean), Godhūma (wheat), Yava (barley), leaf of Vāstūka (a variety of chenopodium), Taṇḍulīyaka (a variety of amaranth), fruit of Paṭola (a variety of small cucumber-snake gourd)), root of Rāsnā (Indian groundsel), Drākṣā (raisin or grape fruit), ghee and goat’s milk are the useful articles of diet for the patients of Śvāsa Roga.
APATHYA: Guru, Śīta and Rūkṣa Anna; Viṣṭambhi, Vidāhi, and Abhiṣyandi Dravya, Māṣa (black phaseolus bean), Sarṣapa Śāka (mustard leaf), food prepared in oil, curd, Matsya (fish) are harmful for the patient of Śvāsa Roga. Suppression of natural urges like urination, thirst, eructation and cough; smoking moving in the sun should be avoided.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Śvāsa, Beng: Śvasa, Dogr: Svasa, Sānsa Phūlanā, Guj: Dam, Hind: Damā, Kan: Guralū Dammu, Maly: Valivu, Mra: Damā, Ori: Śvāsa, Dhakī Siāsī, Tam: Ijhaippu, Tel: Ubbasamu, Eng: Dyspnoea, bronchial asthma

Title: SNĀYUKA ROGA
Sanskrit: स्नायुक रोग
INTRO: This condition is caused by the infestation of a thread like parasite known as guinea worm, which comes out of the skin, gradually after causing swelling and eruption.
SYMPTOMS: In case the parasite gets out in its full length there is no trouble. If the parasite is broken then the symptoms may reappear through another eruption. Due to neglect broken parasites in the arm or groin cause gradual loss of muscular tone of the part leading to lameness.
TREATMENT: Once the parasite is seen at the ruptured site, it should be carefully taken out by winding the parasite on a fine stick after applying a lepa of Devadāli at the site.
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Svarasa (juice) of Nirguṇḍī - 100 ml. to be taken with cow’s ghee 3 days. 2. Śuddha Kupīlu Bīja Majjā - 10 mg. to be taken with 4 to 6 g. honey twice a day. 3. Bilva (bael)- 10 leaves, Dhattūra (datura) 1/2 leaf, Śuddha Sphaṭika (alum)- 4 g. to be taken in 3 to 4 g. dose with cow’s ghee sufficient to make a paste twice a day. 4. Powdered root of Sārivā (Indian sarsaparilla), Kṛṣṇa Sārivā (black sarsaparilla), whole plants of Bṛhatī and Kaṇṭakārī (yellow berried night shade-both varieties), rhizome of Haridrā (turmeric), stem of Dāruharidrā (barberry), roots of Meda, Mahāmedā, and Uśīra (khas), wood of Śveta Candana (white sandal), Śuṇṭhī (dried ginger), fruit fo Yavānī (ptychotis), 12 g. of each to be mixed with Rajata Bhasma-190 g. Its 120 to 240 mg. to be taken with 4 to 6 g. ghee twice a day.

Title: Rakta-Gulma
Sanskrit: रक्तगुल्म
INTRO: Rakta-Gulma is a condition characterized by the appearance of a mass in the uterus with pain and burning sensation. The tumor increases in size and is palpable from the abdomen. The main difference between pregnancy and Rakta-gulma is that in the former case heart beat of the foetus can be heard while in the latter there is no existence of such beat.
TREATMENT: Treatment should generally be undertaken only after it has been ascertained by a gynecologist that conception has not occurred.
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Equal part of powder of Ghṛta Bhṛṣṭa Hiṅgu (asafoetida) and Bhāraṅgī-3 to 6 g. to be taken with decoction of Kṛṣṇa Tila (black sesame)-14 to 28 ml. twice a day. 2. Kalka (paste) of equal part of fruit of Miśreyā (fennel), bark of Karañja (Indian beach), wood of Devadāru (deodar), Bhāraṅgī and root of Pippalī (long pepper)-14 to 28 g. to be taken twice a day. 3. Siddha Ghṛta Prepared with seed of Palāśa (bastard teak) and Kṣāra Jala to be taken in 12 to 24 g. dose with 1 g. powder of Trikaṭu, 1 g. Yavakṣāra and 7 to 14 ml. Madya (wine) twice a day.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Raktagulmu, Beng: Raktagulma, Dogr: Kunni De Golā, Guj: Gulma, Hind: Gulma, Golā, Kan: Raktaḍa Geḍḍe, Maly: Raktagulmam, Mra: Rakta Gulma, Tam: Kamppai Karjhalai, Karuppai Kattai, Eng: Uterine tumour

Title: Garbhasrāva Evaṁ Garbhapāta
Sanskrit: गर्भस्राव एवं गर्भपात
INTRO: Premature expulsion of the foetus up to the four months of pregnancy is known as Garbhasrāva and after four months of pregnancy the expulsion is known Garbha Pāta. Symptoms of pain in pelvis and back, uterine discharge, nervousness of the pregnant woman from the first month onward should be treated as follow.
TREATMENT: Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: First month 1. Powder of equal part of Śuṇṭhī (dried ginger), root of Śatāvarī (wild asparagus), flower of Mallikā (a variety of jasmine)-3 to 6 g. to be taken with 50 to 100 ml. Taṇḍulodaka (rice washing) twice a day. 2. Powder of equal part of Tila (sesame), wood of Padmaka (wild cherry), stem of Padma (lotus) and Ṣaṣṭi (a variety of rice)-3 to 6 g. to be taken with 100 to 250 ml. milk and 5 to 10 g. Śarkarā (raw sugar) twice a day. 3. Powder of equal part of root of Yaṣṭimadhu (glycyrrhiza), seed of Śāka (teak), stem of Kākolī, wood of Devadāru (deodar)-3 to 6 g. to be taken with milk twice a day. Second Month 1. Powder of equal of part of flower of Aśmantaka (white mountain ebony), Śveta Kāñcanāra, seed of Kṛṣṇa Tila (black sesame), roots of Mañjiṣṭhā (madder) and Śatāvarī (wild asparagus)-3 to 6 g. to be taken with 100 to 250 ml. milk twice a day or Dugdha Siddha with these drugs to be taken in 250 ml. dose twice a day. Title: Makkala Śūla
Sanskrit: मक्कलशूल
INTRO: Just after delivery due to some abnormalities a swelling appears below the umbilicus or in the region of bladder which causes colicy pain in the umbilical region or in the whole abdomen and this condition is known as Makkala Śūla. In this the distension of abdomen and retention of urine also occur.
TREATMENT: Treatment
SIMPLE_PREPARATIONS: 1. Caturjātaka Cūrṇa-3 g. to be taken with 4 to 6 g. old Guḍa (jaggery) twice a day. 2. Trikaṭu Cūrṇa-3 g. to be taken with 4 to 6 g. old Guḍa (jaggery) twice a day. 3. Yavakṣāra-1 to 3 g. to be taken with 50 ml. warm or Pippalyādi Kvātha-14 to 28 ml. twice a day. 4. Powder of equal of Śuṇṭhī (dried ginger), Marica (black pepper), fruit of Pippalī (long pepper), Tvak-Dālacīnī (cinnamon bark), Teja Patra (tamal leaf), Bṛhad Elā (large cardamom), Nāgakeśara (Indian ironwood flower stamen), seed of Tumburu (toothache tree)-1 to 3 g. to be taken with old Guḍa (jaggery) twice a day.
COMPOUND_PREPARATIONS: 1. Devadārayādi Kvātha: 14 to 28 ml. to be taken with 1 g. Hiṅgu (asafoetida) and 1 g. Saindhava (rock-salt) twice a day.
REGIONAL NAMES: Asam: Hadilera Kamorā, Beng: Makkala Śūla, Dogr: Lūṭhne Ce Peṭe Derda, Hind: Jera Aṭakane Kā Darda, Kan: Makkala Śūla, Mra: Makkala Śūla, Ori: Dilenī Kanudibā, Tam: Karuppai Vali, Tel: Bālenta Rogamu, Eng: After pains

Title: Sūtikā-Jvara
Sanskrit: सूतिका ज्वर
INTRO: During the delivery if proper care of cleanliness, sterilization etc. is not taken then the patients may suffer form fever which is known as Sūtikā Jvara. It is of six types viz. Vātika, Paittika, Kaphaja, Sannipātika, Stanyotha and Grahotha. Erratic fever with delirium, pain in the body, yawning, horripilation, loss of taste, aversion to cold and liking for warmth, grinding of teeth, dry eructations, sleeplessness, flatulance and rigidity of the body are the signs and symptoms of Vātika Sūtikā Jvara. High grades fever, delirium, giddiness, thirst, burning sensation in the body, vomiting, dryness of the throat, bitter taste in the tongue, paleness of the face, eyes, teeth, nails and urine, liking for cold, etc. are the signs and symptoms of Paittika Sūtikā Jvara. Low grade fever, headache, coryza, cough, sleepiness, drowsiness, excessive salivation, sweet taste in the mouth, heaviness in the body, liking for heat, loss of appetite etc., are the signs and symptoms of Kaphaja Sūtikā Jvara. Alternate feeling of cold and heat, rigor, thirst, restlessness, delirium, difficulty in passing stool, urine and flatus, distension of abdomen, heaviness in the body, feeling of obstruction in the throat are the main signs and symptoms of Sannipātika Sūtikā Jvara. Normally milking starts within three or four days of delivery. Sometimes it starts late causing tightness of breast, thirst, headache, pain in the sides and body, and palpitation. The fever which occurs due to Graha Duṣṭi or due to mental factors like fright, shock is known as Grahotha. Other symptoms are tremors, extreme weakness, delusion, pain in the body, sudden tanning of the skin many times in a day, loss of weight and pulling of lock of hair.
TREATMENT: Treatment Treatment Treatment Treatment The symptoms mentioned above gradually disappear after normal flow of the milk. Treatment described under Stanyadoṣa may be given to relive the symptoms earlier. Treatment Treatment

Title: Stana-Vidradhi
Sanskrit: स्तनविद्रधि
INTRO: Stana-Vidradhi is a disease in which abscess develops in the breast. In the initial stage it is a hard, stony palpable mass and later on all the symptoms of Vidradhi (abscess) are found.
TREATMENT: Stop milk feeding of the baby to ensure outlet of milk by breast pump. Treatment prescribed under Vidradhi should be followed.

Title: SVITRA

Title: HṚDROGA
Sanskrit: हृद्रोग
INTRO: Hṛdroga has been classified into five groups viz. Vātika, Paittika, Kaphaja, Sannipātika, and Kṛmija. Signs, symptoms and treatment of each are as follows. All the symptoms described in Vātika, Paittika and Kaphaja types of Hṛdroga are present in Sannipātika Hṛdroga. Acute pain and itching in the heart area are the main symptoms of Kṛmija Hṛdroga. Other symptoms are nausea, cardiac insufficiency, headache, loss of appetite and oedema.
SYMPTOMS: In Vātika Hṛdroga patient has acute pain in the heart area; the pain is like that of cutting, sawing, churning or stretching. Other symptoms are palpitation, arrhythmia, heart block and fainting. Feeling of heaviness and fatigue in the heart, thirst, burning sensation, sweating, dryness of mouth and fainting are the symptoms of Paittika Hṛdroga. Feeling of seizure of the heart, heaviness in the body; excessive secretion of phlegm, loss appetite, sweet taste in the mouth are the symptoms of Kaphaja Hṛdroga.
